articles.title: Students urged to explore opportunities beyond conventional career paths
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Students must take ownership of their careers, identify their strengths, and continuously upgrade skills to succeed in an evolving professional landscape, say speakers at a career seminar organised by The Hindu FIC

Students must take ownership of their careers, identify their strengths and aspirations, and continuously upgrade their skills to succeed in an evolving professional landscape, said Prof. Satya Duvvuri of the Paari School of Business, SRM University-AP.

Addressing students at a seminar on ‘Career Opportunities in Management & Technology’, organised by The Hindu FIC and Paari School of Business, SRM AP, he urged them to explore opportunities beyond conventional career paths and make informed choices driven by their interests and determination.

Through real-life examples, anecdotes and interactive discussions, Prof. Satya highlighted how several successful professionals from engineering and science backgrounds had utilised their technical knowledge to emerge as prominent leaders in diverse fields.
He emphasised that passion, perseverance and a willingness to learn could open doors to limitless career opportunities.
Logo for The Hindu FIC & SRM AP seminar on careers in management and technology

He underlined the growing importance of analytical thinking, comprehension and proficiency in emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI), in preparing students for future careers. Encouraging them to dream big, work hard and pursue their passions, he said opportunities were often closer than they imagined and that their future depended largely on their own choices and efforts.

Executive Director of Kallam Haranadhareddy Institute of Technology (KHIT) Navya Kallam said that the world offered opportunities across diverse sectors and that engineering graduates could explore areas beyond their core disciplines.
She pointed out that skills such as accounting, which is considered the backbone of any business, could help students become successful entrepreneurs.
KHIT Director Uma Shankar Reddy observed that there was no age limit for acquiring new skills.

Citing the example of the institution’s founder K. Haranadhareddy, who learnt music at the age of 75 and performed at temples, he encouraged students to remain open to learning throughout their lives. He also stressed that higher educational qualifications could strengthen career prospects, noting that additional qualifications often offered an advantage in career advancement and promotions.

Principal of KHIT, Guntur district, B.S.B. Reddy said that rapid technological advancements and the convergence of different technologies were transforming the employment landscape. While certain job roles were becoming obsolete, new opportunities were emerging simultaneously. He expressed confidence that the seminar would help students gain clarity, build confidence and address uncertainties about their career choices.
Executive Director, KHIT, KHM Bharadwaj, Assistant Director, SRM-AP V.V.S. Pradeep and V. Amar from The Hindu were among those participated in the programme.

articles.title: 12 of family injured in fire caused by CNG leak in M.P.'s Orchha; two of them critical
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Scrap dealer Khalil had purchased a CNG cylinder from someone and was trying to dismantle it to extract brass and other metals when the gas leaked out of it and sparked a fire

Twelve members of a family, including three children, suffered burn injuries in a fire that broke out following a CNG leak at a scrap shop in Madhya Pradesh's Orchha town on Friday (November 6, 2026), police said.

The injured were taken to a hospital in Jhansi in neighbouring Uttar Pradesh for treatment, and the condition of two of them — scrap dealer Khalil (60) and his son Sameer (30) — is stated to be critical, Orchha police station house officer Jitendra Singh Gurjar told PTI .
Mr. Khalil had purchased a CNG cylinder from someone and was trying to dismantle it to extract brass and other metals when the gas leaked out of it and sparked a fire, he said.
The blaze engulfed the premises, causing 12 members of Mr. Khalil's family to suffer burn injuries, he said.

Niwari Superintendent of Police Rai Singh Narwaria and District Collector Jamuna Bhide reached the spot after receiving information about the incident, and arranged for the injured to be shifted to the Jhansi medical hospital, the inspector said.
No case has been registered in connection with the incident so far, Mr. Gurjar said, adding that the police would take action based on the investigation.

articles.title: Delhi’s Mustafabad election official lodges police complaint seeking FIR over false Form 7s filing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Delhi’s north east District Election Officer (DEO) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that they have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated

The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) of Mustafabad constituency has lodged a police complaint on Friday (November 7, 2026) seeking FIR under Section 31 of RP Act against the BLA following The Hindu’s report that false Form 7s have been filed seeking deletions of voters who are living at their addresses.

The north east District Election Officer (DEO ) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that election officials have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated. “In connection with reports appearing in print and social media regarding false and fabricated Form-7, a police complaint has been lodged today by the ERO for registration of an FIR under Section 31 of the RP 1950 against the BLA,” a press release from his office also stated.

The Hindu reported on October 30 that in polling part area 129 of Mustafabad constituency, 28 Form 7s seeking deletions of electors found to be living in the area were filed by a BLA registered under Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Chandra Shekhar Nainwal, as per Election Commission of India (ECI) records till October 28. While Mr. Nainwal denied filing these applications and any association with BJP, speaking to The Hindu , nine fresh applications were filed naming him as objector on October 29-30. The reasons cited in these applications were “absent/permanently shifted” and “dead”.

It further said that all 37 forms were scrutinised by the BLO/AERO who found that three electors who were claimed to be dead were found alive at their addresses. All others were also found living at their addresses, as reported by The Hindu .

“Only one case is found to be true whereas 36 cases are found to be false/fabricated. Since the BLA/Objector has knowingly made false statement or declaration in the Form-7, action under Section 31 of the RP act has been invoked for making false statement /declaration in writing in connection with preparation /revision of electoral roll,” the release mentioned.

It stated that verification and inquiry in respect of other Form-7 applications is in progress. As per The Hindu analysis, over 77% of the total 1,021 Form 7s received till November 3 names 20 BJP BLAs as objector. All are against Muslim electors, and several have been found residing at their addresses in different areas.
“Necessary action, as per the guidelines of the Election Commission of India and the extant Act, shall be taken,” the DEO stated in the press release.
Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India

articles.title: Opposition trying to destabilise TVK-led government, says Manickam Tagore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He accuses the Opposition of attempting to create uncertainty and undermining the State’s development
TNCC president Manickam Tagore on Thursday alleged that opposition parties were attempting to destabilise the TVK-led government by approaching its MLAs.

Supporting Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar’s allegation that the DMK and AIADMK were attempting to poach TVK MLAs with the BJP’s support, he said those who had lost power were trying to disturb the government.

Speaking to mediapersons, Mr. Tagore said senior leaders of the DMK, AIADMK, and the BJP had repeatedly questioned the stability of the government. “An honest government has been installed, honest Ministers have been appointed, and the Chief Minister has been delivering a clean administration for the past four months,” he said, adding that the Opposition was attempting to create uncertainty and undermine the State’s development.

On Union Minister of State Jitendra Singh’s allegations about foreign funding for protests in Delhi, Mr. Tagore said he should file a police complaint if he had evidence. “Such baseless claims must stop. As a Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, he should act responsibly. Who is stopping him from going to a police station if he has proof?” he asked.
He also accused the BJP of spreading misinformation to divert attention from allegations of electoral malpractice.

articles.title: Bodies of five fishermen from Tamil Nadu found near Kothapatnam beach in Andhra Pradesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Indian Coast Guard staff on search for four other missing fishermen who were sailing on the same boat which sank 2 km off the shore

The bodies of three fishermen from Tamil Nadu washed ashore at Kothapatnam coast in Ongole on Thursday while the bodies of two more fishermen were found later in the sea by the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) officials at Nizampatnam Port.

Using a Dornier aircraft, the ICG staff in coordination with the personnel of the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC), Chennai, launched a search and rescue (SAR) operation to find five more fishermen, who were sailing on the same boat that sank 2 km off the shore.

According to sources, three boats set out from Tamil Nadu for fishing On October 29, 2026. Owing to the impact of Cyclone Murasu, two boats were anchored for safety near Ramayapatnam Port on November 2 (Monday), while the third boat proceeded towards Nizampatnam Port.

The nine fishermen on the third boat departed from Nizampatnam to meet the other two teams in Ramayapatnam on November 3 (Tuesday). Due to a storm at sea and intense winds, their boat drifted towards the coast of Adani Krishnapatnam Port and capsized.

The nine were identified as Pakkirisamu Suriya (driver), Kuppan, Mohan, Rajesh, Murugan, Kuppusamy, Vijayakanth, Aravindh and Narayanan. While Narayanan was from Cuddalore, the remaining all were from Chennai.

Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu, who was in Kothapatnam to inspect the voting process for the local body elections, visited the place where the bodies of the fishermen washed ashore. ‘’The identification of the bodies will take place after the family members and officials from Tamil Nadu arrive,’’ he added.
“Further action regarding the transport of the bodies and bringing the capsized boat to the shore will be taken in consultation with the officials from Tamil Nadu,’’ the Collector said.
Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, along with the deceased fishermen's family members, reached the mortuary of RIMS Hospital in Ongole for the identification of the bodies.

Andhra Pradesh Fisheries Commissioner Rama Shankar Naik and District Collector P. Raja Babu accompanied the Tamil Naidu Minister. The family members identified four bodies. He said the bodies would be taken to Tamil Nadu after police investigation and post-mortem examination.
"I extend my gratitude to the Andhra Pradesh government for its cooperation. We hope to recover the remaining bodies soon," Mr. Wilson said.
Families of the fishermen who are still missing have urged the State government to take steps on a war footing to find them.
Bharatheeswaran, son of Pakkiri, said his father had spoken to his mother on the evening of November 2.

articles.title: School excursion row: UDF leaders release CCTV footage in support of their claims
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The leadership claimed that the visuals showed the principal and the PTA president entering and leaving the establishment, alleging that a bill of ₹1,100 for alcoholic beverages was settled using the PTA president’s personal ATM card.

The controversy surrounding the recent student study tour conducted by the Meenangadi Government Higher Secondary School saw new developments on Thursday (November 5), with the United Democratic Front (UDF) Meenangadi panchayat committee releasing CCTV footage allegedly showing school Principal, Shivi Krishnan, and the Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) president Hijas Ulladan entering a bar.

At a press conference, UDF leaders, led by former Meenangadi panchayat president K.E. Vinayan, presented the footage purportedly retrieved from the bar in Nampally, Hyderabad. The leadership claimed that the visuals showed the principal and the PTA president entering and leaving the establishment, alleging that a bill of ₹1,100 for alcoholic beverages was settled using the PTA president’s personal ATM card.

Following the disclosure, the UDF Meenangadi leadership lodged a formal complaint with the Wayanad District Police Chief and announced plans to approach the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights. They alleged that students who spoke in support of the school authorities were subjected to severe cyberbullying, intimidation, and harsh online trials by vloggers and online media outlets.

The row originally erupted after allegations emerged that two responsible school officials had consumed alcohol during a recent study tour to Hyderabad. Responding to the accusations, Principal Shivi Krishnan, who is also a leader of a teachers’ association, had refuted the claims and termed them a targeted political move against him.

Though a subsequent medical examination of the principal revealed no presence of alcohol in his blood and a section of students publicly defended him, the UDF countered that online media and vloggers were influenced to sway public opinion, prompting them to release the CCTV footage to substantiate their allegations.

articles.title: Telangana climate conclave to be special feature of global summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Scientists and experts to deliberate on tackling climate change and drought proofing agriculture
The forthcoming Invest Telangana Global Summit – 2026 will feature a special event, Telangana Climate Conclave.

To be held on December 8, the second day of the global summit, the conclave will witness participation of close to 200 scientists, experts from related fields and farmers. The event is being organised to discuss about agriculture patterns that can withstand droughts, animal husbandry, drinking water security, biodiversity, conversion of waste to wealth and other topics.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy wanted an exclusive discussion climate change and challenges posed by El Nino during the global summit. The discussion should result in planning short and long term measures to effectively tackle the problems caused due to climate change as well as a special action plan to handle challenges posed by environmental changes.

The Chief Minister at a meeting with senior officials on Thursday reviewed the status of arrangements being made for the global summit and made several suggestions to the officials concerned. Accordingly, it was decided to appoint a liaison officer for every participant besides ensuring that formalities like registration and issuance of passes be completed on arrival at the airport itself. Participants should be provided with detailed information of the summit proceedings in advance and steps should be taken to ensure that they were not inconvenienced at any point of time.

In addition to liaison officers, security officials should be appointed and elaborate arrangements should be made. Special invites should be sent to companies which evinced interest in investing in the State and officials concerned had been directed to ensure that a comprehensive plan for the successful conduct of the event was finalised by November 15.

Officials informed the Chief Minister that extensive arrangements were being made for the summit, including setting up of additional halls for the exhibitions. Steps had been taken to ensure that programmes related to investments, modern technology, innovations and job opportunities were prioritised besides making arrangements for the success of different exhibitions planned as part of the event.

The Raksha Expo, exclusive defence exhibition, would feature display of latest defence developments, aerospace and cyber security aspects along with drones and robotics. Of the 575 firm that had been invited to attend the summit, 49 had evinced interest to attend the global summit. Special arrangements were being made for animation, visual effects, gaming and related fields and an exclusive pavilion was being set up for start ups. It was decided to invite technological solutions in the fields of agriculture, health, protection of government lands and basic amenities as part of the Telangana Innovation Challenge that was made part of the event. Applications for the challenge would be accepted till November 20.

The Chief Minister wanted special focus on tourism sector as part of the summit while steps should be taken to showcase the measures initiated for education, research and skill development by the State government modelled on “Education to Harvard”.

articles.title: CM directs officials to begin Kaleshwaram barrage restoration works in December
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Final approvals to be secured by month-end; ₹4,193 crore estimated for repairs and restoration

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has directed officials to take up restoration of the damaged Medigadda, Annaram and Sundilla barrages of the Kaleshwaram project strictly in accordance with the recommendations of national-level experts and the National Dam Safety Authority (NDSA), with a target of commencing the works in December.

At a review meeting here, the Chief Minister asked officials to secure the final approvals by the end of November. He also asked Ministers to counter the misleading propaganda that water available at Medigadda. It was also discussed in the Cabinet later.

For water lifted from Medigadda to reach the Yellampalli reservoir, the gates of Annaram and Sundilla barrages would have to be closed. However, the NDSA had advised that the gates of these two barrages, which have structural defects, should remain open.

On the utilisation of Godavari waters through alternative arrangements, Mr. Reddy said the government had lifted water on an unprecedented scale through the Devadula and Sitarama lift irrigation schemes to prevent the downstream Godavari water from going waste.

While the previous government lifted an average of 9.57 tmc ft annually through Devadula, the average had increased to 18.13 tmc ft during the last three years, registering an increase of 89%. By October this year, 16.71 tmc ft had been lifted through Devadula and 8.10 tmc ft through Sitarama, taking the combined utilisation to 24.81 tmc ft, he said.

He said the State would not have faced such difficulties during drought conditions had the previous government constructed a barrage at Tummidihatti and completed the Pranahita project. Water from Pranahita could have been brought to Yellampalli at a lower cost, he observed.

Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy and senior officials explained the restoration plan for the three barrages. Proposals estimated at approximately ₹4,193 crore had been prepared for the restoration of the three barrages. Under the proposed arrangement, the construction agencies would bear the cost of rectifying defects, while the government would meet the expenditure on additional works.

fullParagraphs: Till date, across the eight tranches of mineral block auctions, 100 unique critical and strategic mineral blocks have been offered, of which 64 blocks have been successfully auctioned.

The Ministry of Mines on Thursday launched the ninth tranche of mineral block auctions, featuring 20 critical and strategic mineral blocks, alongside the third tranche of exploration licence auctions covering 11 blocks.
The latest mineral block auction includes deposits of graphite, glauconite, vanadium, gallium, titanium, rare earth elements (REE), tungsten, potash and halite, among other minerals.

The third round of exploration licence auctions, which grants concessions through competitive bidding for reconnaissance and prospecting activities, covers blocks containing copper, potash, halite, vanadium and associated mineralisation.
Across the first eight tranches of mineral block auctions, the government has offered 100 unique critical and strategic mineral blocks, of which 64 have been successfully auctioned.
Under the exploration licence regime, 11 blocks offered in the first two tranches have also been successfully auctioned.

articles.title: Uncertainty over Nigeria vote as court bars opposition leader
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The ADC, one of the main opposition parties trying to oust President Bola Tinubu, has been mired in lawsuits around its leadership, which have now ensnared its 2027 nominee

A Nigerian court on Thursday (November 5, 2026) declared invalid the nomination of Atiku Abubakar as the presidential candidate for the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC), just two months before the country’s elections.

The party, which accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of involvement in the lawsuit, will appeal, its spokesman said — but the ruling creates legal headaches for Abubakar and uncertainty for voters with the January 16 vote around the corner.
The ADC, one of the main opposition parties trying to oust President Bola Tinubu, has been mired in lawsuits around its leadership, which have now ensnared its 2027 nominee.

Thursday’s (November 5, 2026) decision is “another desperate attempt to cripple the opposition and deny Nigerians the right to choose their leaders in the forthcoming general elections”, ADC spokesman Bolaji Abdullahi said in a statement.
Earlier this year, the federal government backed a separate lawsuit over the ADC’s eligibility to contest the 2027 vote in Africa’s most populous country.
Tinubu spokesman Daniel Bwala told AFP the APC “is not involved at all” in the suit over the party’s leadership that sparked Thursday’s (November 5, 2026) decision.
Nigerian media reported that the federal high court in Abuja overturned the current leadership of the ADC by David Mark, who has been fighting with Nafiu Bala Gombe leading the party.
In ruling against Mr. Mark, the nomination of Mr. Abubakar — made while he was at the party’s helm — has also been tossed, Nigerian media reported.
The decision was handed down a day after Mr. Abubakar launched his campaign with a rally in Sokoto state. “The timing of this judgment is no coincidence,” Mr. Abubakar said in a statement.
He did not address the ruling at a rally in northwestern Kebbi state later that day.

Sadiq Ibrahim Dasin, the ADC’s chairman in Mr. Abubakar’s home state of Adamawa, told AFP that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) “has not raised a finger on the qualification of any of our candidates”. “We should continue with the campaign,” he said.
During Nigeria’s 2023 poll, European Union election observers said “excessive pre-election litigation exposed pervasive intraparty conflicts”.

A Nigerian court on Thursday (November 5, 2026) declared invalid the nomination of Atiku Abubakar as the presidential candidate for the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC), just two months before the country’s elections.

The party, which accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of involvement in the lawsuit, will appeal, its spokesman said — but the ruling creates legal headaches for Abubakar and uncertainty for voters with the January 16 vote around the corner.

The ADC, one of the main opposition parties trying to oust President Bola Tinubu, has been mired in lawsuits around its leadership, which have now ensnared its 2027 nominee.

Thursday’s (November 5, 2026) decision is “another desperate attempt to cripple the opposition and deny Nigerians the right to choose their leaders in the forthcoming general elections”, ADC spokesman Bolaji Abdullahi said in a statement.

Earlier this year, the federal government backed a separate lawsuit over the ADC’s eligibility to contest the 2027 vote in Africa’s most populous country.

Tinubu spokesman Daniel Bwala told AFP the APC “is not involved at all” in the suit over the party’s leadership that sparked Thursday’s (November 5, 2026) decision.

Nigerian media reported that the federal high court in Abuja overturned the current leadership of the ADC by David Mark, who has been fighting with Nafiu Bala Gombe leading the party.

In ruling against Mr. Mark, the nomination of Mr. Abubakar — made while he was at the party’s helm — has also been tossed, Nigerian media reported.

The decision was handed down a day after Mr. Abubakar launched his campaign with a rally in Sokoto state. “The timing of this judgment is no coincidence,” Mr. Abubakar said in a statement.

He did not address the ruling at a rally in northwestern Kebbi state later that day.

Sadiq Ibrahim Dasin, the ADC’s chairman in Mr. Abubakar’s home state of Adamawa, told AFP that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) “has not raised a finger on the qualification of any of our candidates”. “We should continue with the campaign,” he said.

articles.title: Eight dead in mass shooting in rural west Turkiye: officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The shooting struck in a rural area near Afyonkarahisar, a town halfway between the capital Ankara and the coastal city of Izmir
Eight people were shot dead in three villages in west-central Turkiye on Thursday (November 5, 2026), local officials said, as police pressed a major manhunt to find the gunman.
“Unfortunately, eight of our citizens have lost their lives, and one has been seriously injured in armed attacks in our province,” the Afyonkarahisar governor’s office said.
The shooting struck in a rural area near Afyonkarahisar, a town halfway between the capital Ankara and the coastal city of Izmir.
Two women with gunshot wounds were found on a road in Yukaritandir village, and despite being rushed to the hospital, both died, Anadolu state news agency said.
Three more bodies were found in Kiyir village, which lies a half-hour drive to the northeast, and another three in Ayazini village, a further half-hour drive east, it said.
Another person found in critical condition was fighting for their life in hospital, it said, without saying where they had been injured.
Grainy CCTV footage published by Turkish media showed a man in a black jacket, white trousers and glasses clutching a rifle as he stood by a faded red minivan.

Police later found the red vehicle stuck in the mud on the outskirts of the university town of Eskisehir, which lies about 100 kilometres (60 miles) to the north, the suspect having fled on foot, the private NTV channel said.

DHA news agency said investigators were looking to see if there was any connection with an earlier incident in the centre of Afyonkarahisar in which a woman in a car was shot and seriously injured by a gunman.

articles.title: Trump debacle: On the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Democrats must use their win to influence policy and improve lives

President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan , making him the first Muslim Senator in history ; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate ; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths

Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren calls of strengthening the tribal community
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hemant Soren said that collective participation and mutual cooperation are essential for the holistic development of the tribal society

Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren on Thursday (November 5, 2026) called for further strengthening of the tribal community. He asserted that the tribal society holds specific social rights, which have also been granted recognition by the Indian Constitution.

Mr. Soren said this while addressing the concluding day of the two-day ‘Marang Buru Dhoromgad Mahasammelan’ at the Madhuban Police Station grounds in Pirtand, Giridih district, organised by Marang Buru Bachao Sangharsh Morcha. Marang Buru refers as supreme deity.

Sarna followers from different parts of India have gathered at the conference. called to protect tribal culture, traditional practices and religious heritage. The conference focused on Santhal religious tradition.

His wife, MLA Kalpana Soren, and representatives of the tribal community from various districts of Jharkhand, including Fagu Besra (Central President of Morcha) and representatives of the tribal community from Assam, Odisha, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, and West Bengal were also present.
Speaking in the Santhali language, the Mr. Soren pointed out that there are many regions in the country where no activity can be undertaken without the consent and permission of the tribal community.
Mr. Soren stressed the necessity of collective participation and mutual cooperation for the holistic development of the community, while assuring them of all possible support.
“The preservation of ‘Marang Buru Dhoromgad’ is essential, and that it is the collective responsibility of all of us to ensure its care,”Mr. Soren said,
Mr. Soren explained that the tribal society is the oldest in the country adding that while the roots of this society remain strong, its branches have diversified.

“Today, some members of the community identify as Hindu, while others follow the ‘Sarna’ tradition. People speak both tribal languages ​​and Hindi. Our ancestors have lived in the forests; the forests provide us with livelihoods and are held in the same regard as the divine,”Mr. Soren said.

A large population of Jharkhand follows Sarna religion. People of this society are worshippers of ancient traditions and nature and consider worshipping trees, mountains and protecting forests as their religion. Several times, Mr. Soren has said that concern of protecting the traditional religious existence of tribals based on nature is certainly a serious question.

In the past, he wrote a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi as well, seeking recognition of the Sarna religious code for tribals asserting that the population of tribals in the state has declined from 38% to 26% in the last eight decades.

Mr. Soren said that his father, ‘Dishom Guru’ Shibu Soren, and his mother, Rupi Soren, have passed away and informed that their funeral rites were performed in accordance with traditional customs and rituals. He urged the youth to understand their own traditions and customs, and to become familiar with the historical background of their community.

articles.title: Bihar NDA leaders led by CM Samrat Choudhary review the council results
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday (November 5, 2026) convened a meeting of National Democratic Alliance (NDA) leaders at his official residence (Lok Sevak Awas) to review the performance in the recently concluded Bihar Legislative Council polls held in eight seats.
Out of eight seats, NDA won three, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) bagged two seats, whereas Janata Dal (United) won one. Both BJP and JD(U) had contested four seats each.

Whereas Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) won two seats and Prashan Kishor’s Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) also bagged one seat making its entry into the Council and rest two seats won by Independent candidates.

All the top leaders of the Bihar NDA were present in the meeting, including JD(U) State President Umesh Singh Kushwaha, both Deputy Chief Minister Bijendra Yadav and Vijay Kumar Choudhary, BJP State President Sanjay Saraogi and others.

In the results declared last week, Independent candidate Bansdihar Brajwasi defeated JD(U)’s Abhishek Jha from Tirhut Graduates’ seat, while another independent candidate Rahul Raj defeated JD(U)’s Anand Pushkar from Saran Teachers’ seat.

Both independent candidates—who won by defeating the JD(U) later joined the BJP. However, when the controversy started over their “joining”, they said that they extended their support to the BJP. This has caused resentment among JD(U) leaders.
Sources said that in the meeting, JD(U) levelled charges against the alliance partner for failing to cooperate and also tried to sabotage their candidate.

However, after the NDA meeting, Mr. Saraogi briefed the media and said that the NDA meeting was held to discuss the plan for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Vaishali on November 21, a day after the NDA government led by Mr. Choudhary will complete one year.

Earlier in the day, JD(U) National Working President Sanjay Jha also called a review meeting in which all the candidates who lost the election were called to speak about their grievances. A source said that it was decided that strict action would be taken against leaders found to be involved in anti-party activities.
“Candidates who contested the election have been asked to submit written complaints regarding any lack of cooperation from BJP leaders and party workers, “a JD(U) leader said.

The review meeting also addressed the organisation’s role, the level of cooperation provided, and its shortcomings during the election. It is expected that further action will be taken based on the complaints.
Prashant Kishor, on the other hand, issued a statement over the internal strife within the JD(U), asserting that Nitish Kumar was the party’s true strength.

articles.title: Residents of disputed villages in Kotia cross Odisha border to vote in Andhra Pradesh polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Odisha political parties accuse A.P. of bribing people to secure their votes in MPTC and ZPTC elections

Several voters from Kotia gram panchayat, whose jurisdiction has long been disputed between Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, crossed the Odisha border on Thursday to cast their votes in the mandal parishad territorial constituency and zilla parishad territorial constituency elections conducted by the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission.
The Odisha government had deployed 16 platoons of police and erected three border checkpoints, restricting people’s entry and exit. However, several voters sneaked out from the borders to cast votes.
The Andhra Pradesh government had set up a polling booth for villagers of Kotia at Sariki in its State boundary.

Political parties in Odisha accused leaders from Andhra Pradesh of bribing people to get their votes. “Some were taken to the other side of the boundary on Wednesday. After casting their votes, they returned,” said veteran Congress MLA Tara Prasad Bahinipati, who hails from Koraput district.

Similarly, Bhrugu Buxipatra, a senior BJD leader, said a few had crossed borders to vote. However, this time, the people of Odisha were successful by not letting Andhra Pradesh set up its polling booth inside Odisha, he said.

Koraput Sub-Collector Fabi Rasheed said security personnel and Executive Magistrates were deployed in bordering villages to prevent untoward incidents. “Villagers did cross the border, but we have no idea if they voted in the Andhra Pradesh elections,” Ms. Rasheed said.
In the run-up to elections, political parties from Odisha had camped at borders by not allowing polling booths inside the State.

Both Odisha and Andhra Pradesh have been claiming their jurisdictional rights since 1950s. The dispute surfaced in 1955, two years after the formation of Andhra Province, when Andhra Pradesh officials attempted to collect land revenue from the villages. In 1954 and 1967 elections, some villagers of Kotia had participated in elections for both the States. Odisha government had moved Supreme Court over Kotia dispute in 1968.
Koraput District Collector had filed contempt petition in the Supreme Court in October this year, alleging Andhra Pradesh violated the 2006 status quo order.

On March 30, 2006, the Supreme Court disposed of the original suit (1968), holding that it lacked jurisdiction to adjudicate the dispute because of the proviso to Article 131. It directed that the status quo should be maintained until the dispute was taken up by an appropriate authority in accordance with law. According to legal experts, issues under Article 131 of the Constitution are resolved only by Parliament.
Residents of Kotia Group of Villages avail welfare benefits from both the State. Some possess voter identity card of both States and cast their votes depending on poll schedule.

articles.title: Kochi police yet to complete verification of private bus employees
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police launched the background verification drive following a series of incidents of criminal behaviour involving private bus crew

The Kochi City police’s special drive to conduct background verification of private bus employees and issue them special identity cards is yet to be completed, even two months after the initiative was launched.

The police, according to sources, are planning to issue the ID cards by next week, though they admitted that a final decision on how to proceed with the drive was yet to be taken. An officer involved in the process said the verification of over 1,500 employees, including drivers and conductors, had been completed. It is roughly estimated that around 2,000 employees work as bus crew in the city.

Bus employees were asked to submit their personal details to the police in a pro forma for verification. The police launched the background verification drive in response to a series of incidents involving alleged criminal behaviour by private bus employees in recent times. The Special Branch of the police is conducting the verification based on the applications received by the traffic wing.

Sources said the police were planning to introduce smart ID cards for the bus crew, though the details of the cards were yet to be finalised. However, the police are yet to decide whether the cards should be issued to all employees who undergo verification, the officer said.

Once the verification is completed, it would be up to the bus operator to decide whether a person should be employed or not,” the officer said.

articles.title: Melania Trump calls for ‘enduring’ Ukraine truce as rivals meet at White House
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The unprecedented meeting hoped to build on a localised six-day truce in the starvation-hit Ukrainian city of Oleshky that U.S. President Donald Trump’s wife had announced last month

U.S. First Lady Melania Trump called for a “more enduring” ceasefire in Ukraine as she hosted a rare meeting between officials from the war-torn country and its invader Russia at the White House on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
The unprecedented meeting hoped to build on a localised six-day truce in the starvation-hit Ukrainian city of Oleshky that U.S. President Donald Trump’s wife had announced last month.
“Now we must use the courage we brought to Oleshky to find common ground through a shared concern for the suffering of innocent people,” Ms. Melania Trump told reporters.
“Together, we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire.”
The Slovenian-born former model said she was sending the envoys back with personal letters to Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
She urged them to use the Oleshky ceasefire — the longest truce so far in the Russian invasion that began in February 2022 — as a “spark in a world of darkness.”

“The ceasefire in Oleshky would not be possible without President Putin and President Zelenskyy. Their cooperation establishes a meaningful precedent for advancing peace throughout the region,” she added.
The rare halt in fighting, which was respected by both sides, allowed roads to be demined and residents to depart for either Ukraine or Russia.

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev said he thanked Ms. Melania Trump on Mr. Putin’s behalf for her “distinguished humanitarian role” in brokering the truce in Oleshky and for work on reuniting children separated from their families by the war.
The White House meeting also reunited Russia’s human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova and her counterpart from Kyiv, Dmytro Lubinets, who formed an unlikely bond during the Oleshky ceasefire.

The pair were on the ground in the devastated town, addressing the media together on efforts to evacuate residents and deliver aid, in one of the most substantial instances of cooperation between the warring countries.
The U.S. first lady’s efforts come ahead of trilateral talks next week in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the Ukraine war — the first between Russian, Ukraine and the United States since February.

articles.title: Maharashtra FDA seizes drugs, cosmetics worth ₹34.51 lakh, cancels 122 licences
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The FDA urged citizens to report instances of illegal drug manufacturing or sales, as well as suspected substandard drugs, medical devices and cosmetics, to its commissioner’s office or the nearest district office

The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) seized drugs and cosmetics worth ₹34.51 lakh, cancelled 122 licences and suspended 422 others following enforcement action across the State in October 2026, according to a press note issued by the department on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

The FDA conducted 1,986 inspections of drug manufacturing, sales and other regulated establishments during the month and issued 674 notices. Of these, 1,694 inspections were conducted at drug sales establishments and 292 at manufacturing and other regulated establishments. The department cancelled 105 licences and suspended 367 licences of sales establishments, while 17 licences were cancelled and 55 suspended in the manufacturing and other categories.

The department also carried out 11 search and seizure operations involving alleged violations related to the manufacture, storage and sale of drugs and cosmetics. Two FIRs were registered, and four persons were arrested under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act in connection with the illegal sale of narcotic drugs.

Among the major seizures, FDA officials recovered allopathic drugs worth ₹22.03 lakh from the premises of Phoenix Medicorp in Nagpur on October 7. According to the department, the establishment had stored drugs at unlicensed premises despite surrendering its licences.
In Mumbai, FDA officials seized spurious drugs identified as Empirime tablets and Cardiurex 2 ml, worth ₹1.01 lakh, from INHS Asvini in Colaba on October 29, according to the department.

In separate operations in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on October 14 and 25, officials seized 199 Nitrosun 10 tablets containing Nitrazepam. Four persons were arrested in connection with their alleged illegal sale.

The FDA also seized cosmetic soaps worth ₹4.05 lakh from Vedas Herbals Mahila Gruh Udyog in Baramati, Pune district, on October 14, for alleged manufacturing without a licence. In Vasai East, officials seized raw materials, packaging materials and machinery worth ₹1.83 lakh from G.B. Cosmetics on October 10 in connection with alleged unlicensed manufacture and sale of nail polish.

The Konkan division recorded the highest number of inspections in October at 556, followed by Pune with 375 and Greater Mumbai with 322. Konkan also accounted for the highest number of regulatory actions at 156, followed by Greater Mumbai with 105 and Pune with 77.

Between April 1 and October 31, the FDA conducted 7,950 inspections across Maharashtra, issued 2,888 notices, cancelled 555 licences and suspended 2,074 licences. The department recorded 2,629 regulatory actions, comprising licence cancellations and suspensions, during the seven-month period.

The FDA urged citizens to report instances of illegal drug manufacturing or sales, as well as suspected substandard drugs, medical devices and cosmetics, to its commissioner’s office or the nearest district office.

articles.title: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, a joint press release stated

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on Thursday (November 5, 2026) met Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu, with discussions focused on “possible outcomes and initiatives” from the expected upcoming visit of the Himalayan nation’s leader to New Delhi.
Concluding his official engagements in Nepal that spanned Wednesday and Thursday, Mr. Misri also met Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal.

“The Foreign Secretary of India highlighted the wide-ranging engagement and overall progress in diverse areas of bilateral cooperation, and discussed possible outcomes and initiatives in the context of the upcoming visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal to India,” stated a joint press release issued by the Ministry of External Affairs and Kathmandu’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Mr. Misri held detailed talks with his host, Nepali Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai, on the “mutually beneficial partnership” between India and Nepal.

Mr. Shah had earlier this year highlighted the border dispute with India in the Lipulekh-Kalapai-Limpiyadhura area that is part of India’s Uttarakhand but claimed by Nepal as a sticking point in ties.
Mr. Shah had sought to involve other countries, such as the United Kingdom and China, in talks on the issue. But India wants the matter to be resolved bilaterally.
The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, the joint press release stated.

Mr. Misri’s discussions with Nepali stakeholders included a “commerce and development partnership, hydropower, physical connectivity, border management, energy and people-to-people ties”, as well as new areas like digital connectivity and AI.
Mr. Misri also met Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Minister for Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal.
Mr. Shah was sworn in as Prime Minister in March this year following the Gen-Z uprising in Nepal in September 2025 that led to the ouster of the previous government.

articles.title: India-born Nithya Raman beats Democratic incumbent to become LA mayor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Leftist Nithya Raman, who was the first DSA-affiliated Los Angeles City Council member, will now helm the entertainment capital as it prepares to host the 2028 Olympics

Democratic socialist Nithya Raman ousted incumbent Democrat Karen Bass to become the next mayor of Los Angeles, ending a heated race that saw the one-time allies spar over frustration with the status quo.
Ms. Bass called Raman on Thursday (November 5, 2026) to concede, after the latest numbers showed Raman with 52% of the vote against the outgoing mayor’s 48%, with three-quarters of votes counted.
“I’m deeply honored to be your next mayor,” said India-born Nithya Raman, 45, in a statement on social media.
“I love this city. I believe in its people. The work ahead will be hard, and change will take time. And together, we are going to build a future as extraordinary as the city we call home.”

Ms. Raman campaigned in the nation’s second-largest city on a platform of “pothole politics” — dubbing broken streetlights and jagged sidewalks as failures of her predecessor’s leadership — while harnessing the anger of younger voters over affordability.

Her victory is yet another in the win column for candidates backed by the Democratic Socialists of America, who have propelled a cadre of left-wing leaders into office in cities across the country as well as Congress.
Ms. Raman, who was the first DSA-affiliated Los Angeles City Council member, will now helm the entertainment capital as it prepares to host the 2028 Olympics.
Ms. Bass, 73, was elected in 2022 as the first Black woman mayor in Los Angeles history and entered the role with decades of state and federal government experience.
But her term was riddled with setbacks. She was haunted by her handling of deadly wildfires in 2025, which erupted while she was traveling for the Biden administration.
“While this is not the outcome we hoped for, the people of Los Angeles have spoken,” Ms. Bass said in a statement.

“I have called Councilmember Nithya Raman to congratulate her on her victory, and I have committed to ensuring a smooth and seamless transition. Moving this city forward is what Los Angeles needs from all of us.”
Ms. Raman was an 11th-hour entrant into the race, and had even initially backed Bass’s re-election bid.

Ms. Bass, 73, was elected in 2022 as the first Black woman mayor in Los Angeles history and entered the role with decades of state and federal government experience.

articles.title: The ecological fallout of Israel’s war in Gaza
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The destruction of Gaza’s ecosystems underscores the need for accountability under international law

On November 5, 2001, the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) designated November 6 each year as the International Day for Preventing the Exploitation of the Environment in War and Armed Conflict . This recognition underscores the far-reaching impacts of environmental damage caused by armed conflict, including degradation of ecosystems and resource depletion well after the conflict period. This impact often extends beyond the limits of national territories and affects future generations.

Considering the importance of the issue, the International Law Commission (ILC), in its report titled ‘Protection of the Environment in Relation to Armed Conflicts’ (PERAC), adopted 27 draft principles in 2022, which were formally noted by the UNGA on December 7, 2022. The overarching purpose of these principles is to enhance the protection of the environment in relation to armed conflicts. The first principle of the PERAC provides that the principles apply to the protection of the environment before, during and after an armed conflict, including in situations of occupation. In this context, Israel’s responsibility for internationally wrongful acts causing environmental harm arises not only from its ongoing genocide in Gaza but also from its continuing role as an occupying power.

articles.title: Two actors held on charge of assaulting and robbing doctor in Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The 41-year-old doctor was allegedly assaulted and robbed of valuables worth ₹3.25 lakh after being lured to an apartment on the pretext of an emergency medical need

The Kadavanthra police have arrested two film actors in a case in which a 41-year-old doctor was allegedly assaulted and robbed of valuables worth ₹3.25 lakh by a group after being lured to an apartment in Kochi on the pretext of in need of emergency medical care.
The arrested persons were identified as Bibin Perumpally and Athulya Chandra, the first and third accused, respectively.

The case was registered based on a complaint filed by the doctor, a resident of Kureekad in Ernakulam. According to the first information report, there are 12 accused persons, including one identifiable person and nine others whose identities are yet to be established.

The accused have been booked under the non-bailable provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including Sections 127(2) (wrongful confinement), 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 296(b) (obscene acts and words), 351(2) (criminal intimidation), and 310 (robbery/dacoity). The incident allegedly took place between 6.30 p.m. and 10.30 p.m. on November 2, 2026.

articles.title: Form 8 must be decided during SIR; deletion without hearing denies vote: Bombay HC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bench also ordered the Election Commission of India to restore the six names, and to set aside the rejection of their Form 8 applications
The Goa bench of The Bombay High Court held that removal of an elector’s name from the roll without a hearing denies the citizen the right to vote.

The Bench delivered the judgment on a petition by six members of the Salgaonkar family that an Electoral Registration Officer must decide a Form 8 application while Special Intensive Revision is underway. The Bench also ordered the Election Commission of India to restore the six names, and to set aside the rejection of their Form 8 applications.

The judgment, delivered by a Bench of Justice Valmiki Menezes and Justice Amit Jamsandekar, records that Section 22 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and Rule 13 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 continue to operate during a revision, whether Intensive or Summary, and that an ERO who receives Form 8 is bound to decide the application rather than refuse it because the revision is underway. The Bench rejected the contention of the ECI that an ERO may refuse Form 8 while revision is underway.

The Bench cited Rule 21A of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 and said that the Rule reflects the proviso to Section 22 of the Act, which requires an ERO to give a person whose name is on the roll and is required to be deleted, an opportunity to show cause before deletion. The Court added that an ERO must make an endeavour to give a voter who does not reside in the constituency an opportunity to show cause why the action proposed should not be taken.

The Court examined Sections 22 and 23 of the Act with Rules 13 and 25 of the Rules and drew a line between Form 6 and Form 8 by holding that Form 6 is for a person who seeks inclusion for the first time and requires a declaration that the name is not on any Assembly or Parliamentary roll, while Form 8 is for a voter on the roll who seeks shift of residence or correction of entries, so a voter who shifts within the constituency can file only Form 8 and cannot be directed to file Form 6 during SIR.

The Bench held that a direction to file Form 6 would require the voter to declare that the name was not on a roll and that the application was for inclusion for the first time, which would conflict with the record and expose the applicant to Section 31 of the Act. It also held that removal of a name from the roll after revision, and without a hearing, when the elector has submitted Form 8 for shift of residence within that constituency, denies the right to vote.

The petitioners had their names on the electoral roll in Part 29 of the Santa Cruz constituency in Goa since 1995 and moved to Part 25 before the SIR began in November 2025. When a Booth Level Officer visited the address on the roll the landlord said they had moved, after which the petitioners approached the BLO at the address to which they moved on November 12, 2025 and were directed to submit Form 8.

The BLO uploaded Form 8 on December 8, 2025, verification took place, and the ECI told the petitioners that the verification report had been submitted and the applications forwarded to the ERO, but when the roll was published on December 16, 2025 the names were absent from Part 29 and Part 25. Subsequently, on January 21, 2026 the ERO rejected Form 8 and told them the EPIC numbers had been deleted and that they should submit Form 6.

The petitioners challenged the rejection before the District Election Officer and the Chief Electoral Officer, both of whom upheld it, and they then moved the High Court contending that rejection of Form 8 was not in accordance with the Act and the Rules and that the names had been deleted without notice or hearing.

articles.title: Pune Customs seizes hydroponic marijuana worth ₹3.72 crore at airport, arrests passenger
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The interception was based on passenger profiling and suspicious findings during baggage scanning, a press note issued by Pune Customs said

Pune Customs arrested an Indian passenger arriving from Bangkok and seized 10.642 kg of hydroponic marijuana worth an estimated ₹3.72 crore at Pune International Airport on November 4. The contraband was concealed in packets labelled as freeze-dried durian fruit and hidden among food items in the passenger’s check-in baggage.

According to a press note issued by Pune Customs on November 5, officers of the Air Intelligence Unit (AIU) and the airport batch intercepted the passenger, who arrived on Air India Express flight IX-291, on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) evening. The interception was based on passenger profiling and suspicious findings during baggage scanning.

During a detailed examination of the trolley bag, officials discovered nine rectangular silver-coloured packets bearing the label “Freeze Dried Monthong Durian” concealed among packets of noodles. Each packet was further wrapped in two layers of vacuum-sealed black polythene.

Upon opening the packages, officers found yellowish-green dried floral material emitting a pungent odour. Preliminary tests conducted using a narcotics field-testing kit returned a positive result for marijuana, which Customs identified as hydroponic weed.

The entire consignment, weighing 10.642 kg and valued at approximately ₹3.72 crore, was seized along with the packaging materials under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.
The passenger was subsequently arrested and produced before a judicial magistrate, who remanded the accused to judicial custody until November 18.
Customs officials said further investigation was underway to ascertain the possible involvement of a smuggling syndicate.

During a detailed examination of the trolley bag, officials discovered nine rectangular silver-coloured packets bearing the label “Freeze Dried Monthong Durian” concealed among packets of noodles. Each packet was further wrapped in two layers of vacuum-sealed black polythene.

Upon opening the packages, officers found yellowish-green dried floral material emitting a pungent odour. Preliminary tests conducted using a narcotics field-testing kit returned a positive result for marijuana, which Customs identified as hydroponic weed.

The entire consignment, weighing 10.642 kg and valued at approximately ₹3.72 crore, was seized along with the packaging materials under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.

The passenger was subsequently arrested and produced before a judicial magistrate, who remanded the accused to judicial custody until November 18.

Customs officials said further investigation was underway to ascertain the possible involvement of a smuggling syndicate.

fullParagraphs: For an economy aspiring to become a developed nation by 2047, the statistical blind spots could translate into costly policy mistakes, misdirected investments and ineffective welfare schemes

India’s statistical requirements have outgrown the conventional survey-based architecture, requiring a more scientific and technological architecture to better capture key performance indicators of economy, even as it should avoid the growing risks of synthetic data.

Seeking to move official data collection beyond periodic surveys and administrative records, the VISTAR or Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research is a major overhaul of India’s official statistical system at the centre and state levels using interoperable datasets, bridging data gaps and generating timely, reliable socioeconomic indicators for evidence-based policymaking.

articles.title: Making sense of the blue shift in U.S. midterm election | a collection
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Analytical insights from The Hindu on the 2026 U.S. midterm results, blue wave shifts, and key state races

Democrats seized control of U.S. Congress after the midterm election on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), winning the Senate and House in a nationwide rebuke of President Donald Trump, likely limiting the rest of his term.

In a massive blue wave across the country, Trump’s Republican Party faced stunning defeats in its strongholds Texas, Georgia, Iowa and Ohio, where it lost the Governor’s posts to the Democrats. The Grand Old Party (GOP) also faced a drubbing in Senate races in Texas, Maine, South Carolina, North Carolina, Kansas, Iowa and Ohio, where Trump campaigned with a simple message, urging voters to pretend that he was on the ballot.

In a historic turn of events in U.S. political history, Texas Democrat James Talarico, a former teacher who ran on a “politics of love”, defeated Attorney General Ken Paxton to win a Senate seat—the first Democrat statewide winner since 1994. Separately, Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican Governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican rule. Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers in Michigan to become the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.

articles.title: Key federal panel approves Trump’s arch while it is being challenged in court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The National Capital Planning Commission voted 8-4 to approve the 76-metre memorial arch near Washington, as three lawsuits challenge it and a judge is expected to rule soon on whether to block construction.
A federal judge late on Thursday (November 5, 2026) blocked the Trump administration from breaking ground on a towering memorial arch for 14 days.

The temporary restraining order by U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, halting the work, represents a major setback for one of President Donald Trump’s most prominent projects in his vision to remake Washington.

The decision followed a series of steps taken earlier on Thursday by the government, including the final approval of the arch by the National Capital Planning Commission in an 8-4 vote after a hearing of nine and a half hours, where dozens of witnesses opposed the construction.

The administration said the work could begin as soon as the approval was in place, the Interior Department issued a final decision authorising construction and the National Park Service published the proper notification.
In issuing the temporary stop, Judge Chutkan said Virginia and the District of Columbia had shown that the immediacy of the construction would cause real harm to the plaintiffs.

“The harm is certain,” she wrote. “Defendants initially notified the court that construction could begin as early as November 5, 2026, if the NCPC approves the project at its meeting that day and the Department of the Interior authorizes construction.” In their filing, Virginia and the District of Columbia warned of traffic pattern distortions, as well as concerns about the impact on mutual aid emergency calls if the arch were to proceed.

“Second, the District and Virginia will incur significant unrecoverable costs. As soon as construction begins, DDOT [District Department of Transportation] will need to expend staff time and operating resources to affirmatively and proactively manage temporary detours, crashes or disabled vehicles,” Judge Chutkan wrote.

The judge’s decision came just over an hour after the commission’s hearing ended. The final vote came after nine and a half hours and scores of people opposing it. The vote broke along federal and local lines. Those in favour work for the administration or are connected to the President, who was pushing for the immediate construction. Opponents represented the city of Washington.
The panel’s Trump-appointed chairman launched the meeting with a gushing appraisal of the towering monument and lauded Mr. Trump for wanting to build it.

“President Trump understands as president and a superb builder that it’s important to our national identity to display who we are through grand monuments,” said Mark Paoletta, the commission’s chairman.

As Mr. Trump has often remarked, “the great cities around the world have arches: Paris, Rome, London,” said Mr. Paoletta, who also serves as general counsel for the White House Office of Management and Budget.

Commissioner Paul Ingrassia, a lawyer for the General Services Administration, said the arch was “not about politics. It’s about remembrance. It’s about celebrating our history. It’s about commemorating veterans. And it’s really something that’s a noble tribute to our nation and something that we can all rally behind.”

articles.title: Mahabharata, Arthashastra, Rajatarangini manuscripts added to UNESCO memory regional register
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat hailed the inscriptions as a landmark recognition of India’s extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage

Manuscripts of the epic Mahabharata, Kalhana’s 12th-century historical chronicle Rajatarangini, and Kautilya’s Arthashastra, a work on governance and statecraft, have been inscribed on UNESCO’s Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, officials said on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
PIB Culture made the announcement on X and shared photos of UNESCO certificates.

“A moment of immense pride for India! The Rajatarangini, Mahabharata and Arthashastra have been inscribed in @UNESCO’s Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, marking a historic milestone in the global recognition of India’s rich civilisational heritage!” it said.

🇮🇳 A moment of immense pride for India! The Rājataraṅgiṇī, Mahābhārata and Arthaśāstra have been inscribed in @UNESCO's Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, marking a historic milestone in the global recognition of India's rich civilisational heritage! https://t.co/LjJwIILhmf
The decision was taken at the 11th Session of the Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register held in Jakarta, Indonesia, the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) said.
According to an official, the IGNCA played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.
Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat hailed the inscriptions as a landmark recognition of India’s extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage.

“A moment of immense pride for India! The inclusion of Rajatarangini, Mahabharata and Arthashastra in @UNESCO Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register is a landmark recognition of India’s extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage,” he posted.

“These timeless works embody our rich traditions of historical inquiry, philosophical thought and statecraft, whose wisdom continues to inspire humanity. Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble PM Shri @narendramodi Ji, India’s civilisational legacy is receiving unprecedented global recognition and its rightful place on the world stage,” the minister added.

With the recognition, India’s historical, literary, philosophical and political thought receives wider international acknowledgement, taking the country’s total number of inscriptions in the Regional Register to six, officials said.

Illustrated manuscripts of the Ramcharitamanas, featuring intricate miniature paintings, preserving Tulsidas’ work; a rare 15th-century manuscript containing animal fables and moral stories from the Panchatantra; and the manuscript of the Sahrdayaloka-Locana, a text of Indian poetics, were inscribed in the regional register in 2024.

A moment of immense pride for India! The inclusion of Rājataraṅgiṇī, Mahābhārata and Arthaśāstra in @UNESCO Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register is a landmark recognition of India's extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage. These timeless works embody our rich traditions of historical inquiry, philosophical thought and statecraft, whose wisdom continues to inspire humanity. Under the visionary leadership of Hon'ble PM Shri @narendramodi Ji, India's civilisational legacy is receiving unprecedented global recognition and its rightful place on the world stage.

articles.title: Trump to participate in Deepavali celebration at White House
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The celebrations are scheduled to be held at the Oval Office, continuing a tradition started by President George W Bush
President Donald Trump will participate in a Deepavali celebration at the White House on Friday.
The celebrations are scheduled to be held at the Oval Office, continuing a tradition started by President George W Bush.
Earlier, the ceremonies were mostly held in the Eisenhower Executive Office Building in the presence of Indian-American community members and Indian diplomats.
In 2009, President Barack Obama became the first president to light a lamp (diya) at the White House, during a ceremony in the East Room.
Since then, lamp lighting ceremonies have been held in various locations in the White House, including the Oval Office and the Roosevelt Room.
Last year, India’s Ambassador to the U.S. Vinay Kwatra joined Mr. Trump in the Oval Office to celebrate Deepavali with the traditional lighting of the lamp.
