articles.title: Indian NGO REACH receives Kochon Prize 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Presented by the Kochon Foundation, an independent Korean non-profit foundation, in partnership with the Stop TB Partnership, the Kochon Prize recognises individuals and organisations that have made significant contributions to the fight against TB

Resource group for Education and Advocacy for Community Health (REACH), a not-for-profit organisation working to strengthen the tuberculosis (TB) response in India, has been awarded the Kochon Prize 2026, becoming the first civil society, non-profit organisation from India to receive this prestigious global recognition for its contributions to combating TB, a press release said.

Presented by the Kochon Foundation, an independent Korean non-profit foundation, in partnership with the Stop TB Partnership, the Kochon Prize recognises individuals and organisations that have made significant contributions to the fight against TB. The 2026 Kochon Prize is shared by REACH, the Centre for Health Solutions, Kenya, and the Marshall Islands TB Control Program. Previous winners from India include L.S. Chauhan (2006), head of the Revised National TB Control Programme, the Indian Council of Medical Research (2017) and Molbio Diagnostics (2024). The award was presented at the Stop TB Partnership Board Meeting held in Indonesia on November 5, 2026.

“Treat the person, not the disease - our journey with TB communities has been just that. We realised early on that overcoming barriers to care means addressing more than clinical needs - it means recognising social, community, family, mental health and situational challenges. That is the essence of integrated care: seeing the whole person, understanding their realities, and doing whatever it takes to ensure that no one is left behind,” said Nalini Krishnan, chairperson and co-founder, REACH.

“REACH is a remarkable and rare organisation that has been consistently ahead of the curve in terms of public health action, and particularly in the field of TB. A women-led organisation, they genuinely care about the people they’re supporting, beyond the numbers, data and reports to donor. However, they combine this with a robust scientific and technical approach and a shrewd understanding of the public health landscape in the country,” said Soumya Swaminathan, chairperson, M. S. Swaminathan Research Foundation and former chief scientist, WHO, who nominated REACH for the award.

“This recognition is testimony to the dedication of the community health workers, TB Nanbans and TB Champions who work alongside us, and to the families affected by TB and non-communicable diseases (NCDs) who have placed their trust in us. We are deeply grateful to their unwavering commitment and fortitude, and are energised to do more to help facilitate equitable access to health,” said Ramya Ananthakrishnan, director, REACH.

articles.title: Documentary highlights role of family physicians in strengthening primary healthcare
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The documentary is intended to initiate wider conversations on reviving primary healthcare networks in urban and rural communities, and recognising neighbourhood doctors as an integral part of the healthcare system

The role of family physicians in ensuring accessible, affordable and patient-centred healthcare came into focus at the premiere of the documentary ‘The Doctor Next Door: A Legacy of Care’, screened at the Indian Heritage Academy in Bengaluru earlier this week.

Through accounts of veteran physicians, patients and young medical professionals, the film examines the decline of neighbourhood family practices and the growing fragmentation of healthcare. It highlights how long-standing doctor-patient relationships built on trust, familiarity and personal attention remain central to effective primary care.

The documentary draws attention to the rising dependence on specialised and corporate hospital-based treatment, making a case for strengthening family medicine as the foundation of India’s healthcare system.

Swetha Reddy, project manager of the documentary, said the film features perspectives from young medical students and practitioners considering careers in general practice, highlighting the need for changes in medical education and healthcare policy to encourage family medicine.

Directed by Ganesh Shankar Raj of Mindia Films and produced in collaboration with the Academy of Family Physicians of India (AFPI), the non-profit documentary explores the enduring relationship between family doctors and patients, and the importance of continuity of care in an increasingly specialised healthcare system.

The screening was followed by a panel discussion featuring scientists, medical professionals, senior family physicians, and community health advocates. The discussion centred on the challenges facing primary healthcare, the need to strengthen family medicine, and the importance of human relationships in medical practice.
Veteran family physician B.C. Rao was among the contributors to the initiative, alongside representatives of AFPI and other healthcare professionals.

The organisers said the documentary was intended to initiate wider conversations on reviving primary healthcare networks in urban and rural communities, and recognising neighbourhood doctors as an integral part of the healthcare system.

articles.title: Amid the sparkle of Deepavali, ophthalmologists sound a note of caution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Lighting firecrackers is part of the fun of Deepavali. But this should be done safely. Ophthalmologists warn that a moment of carelessness can cause eye injuries ranging from minor abrasions to severe ocular trauma

The sound of firecrackers filling the air is not far away as Deepavali draws closer. But the excitement of bursting firecrackers comes with a word of caution from ophthalmologists as they warn that a moment of carelessness can cause eye injuries ranging from minor abrasions to severe ocular trauma.

M. Elangovan, director, Regional Institute of Ophthalmology and Government Ophthalmic Hospital (RIO-GOH), Chennai, said that there are different types of crackers. “Bursting types (explosive crackers) will produce irregular, small and forcible particles in all directions and are the most dangerous. These particles can travel at such a velocity that they could hit or penetrate any soft surface. Then, there is direct heat injury caused by crackers such as sparklers that can cause scar formations in the cornea or conjunctiva due to the heat generated. Sudden and close exposure to bright light-emitting crackers can also cause bleaching or temporary blackout due to the impact on the rod and cone cells in the retina,” he explained.

articles.title: Cancer care: Long battle for affordable treatment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Advances in oncology have improved treatment options, but their benefits remain out of reach for many patients who cannot afford to complete the prescribed course. This is despite the recent decision to cap trade margins on 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines, providing some relief, writes Afshan Yasmeen...

A 45-year-old garment factory worker from Bengaluru Rural diagnosed with stage IV-A cancer of the mouth faces an arduous course of treatment: chemotherapy to shrink the tumour, extensive surgery involving reconstruction, followed by radiation and chemotherapy. The cost of medicines and supportive drugs of around ₹93,000 alone, besides treatment costs, are staggering for her family with a modest monthly income of ₹28,000. With funds running out, she is facing the risk of discontinuing the final stages of treatment.

Likewise, a 56-year-old shopkeeper from Mysuru district, diagnosed with recurrent, inoperable hypopharyngeal cancer involving the oesophagus, has a different but equally difficult challenge. After three cycles of chemotherapy, the disease has shown partial response. Immunotherapy could offer another treatment option, but its cost remains prohibitive. Spending another ₹2.4 lakh to ₹8 lakh over the next 2 to 3 months for bi-weekly immunotherapy is virtually impossible on a ₹45,000/month income.
Science, Space & Environment Report: Cancer care: Long battle for affordable treatment. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.

articles.title: Deepavali with pets: Why pet parents are choosing quieter holiday getaways
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: As fireworks unsettle dogs and cats, pet owners are trading noisy city celebrations for countryside retreats, pet hostels and quieter holidays

As Deepavali approaches, pets often become anxious at the sound of firecrackers. Dogs and cats may hide under beds or in dark corners, while some lose interest in playtime, walks and even pee breaks. For pet owners, finding ways to ease their distress is an ongoing challenge. Some who love celebrating Deepavali but cannot bear to see their pets shivering and panting are now choosing quieter destinations to spend the festival.
Frodo from Bengaluru | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Pet parent JP Daisy boards her cat at a hostel in Hyderabad’s Kokapet with soundproof rooms during Deepavali. Watching her usually docile Siamese, Sharpay, run helter-skelter as firecracker noise peaks in the evening makes Daisy anxious. “She is a lightweight cat and usually eats very little. During Deepavali, she stops eating. One of our friends suggested a place to board her. Sharpay is not clingy, so boarding her is easy,” she says.

Pet boarding facilities also see a surge in demand during festivals, and not just from people travelling. With diyas lit in homes, unattended flames can pose a safety risk. At Pet Cafe Hyderabad, a boarding facility and restaurant in Banjara Hills, founder Deven Baheti says regulars book slots weeks, sometimes months, ahead of Deepavali.

“The open space and location make it comfortable for pets. Ours is a quiet locality, with few homes bursting firecrackers. To further drown out the noise, we play calming music, use vet-approved anti-anxiety drops and essential oils, and apply calming sprays to help them relax,” says Deven.

With boarding (charges of ₹1000 per day) slots fully booked, Deven and his team are preparing to keep the pets occupied with play and grooming sessions. “We do it for the love of animals. Even reactive pets are managed by a few of us and kept in separate enclosures, away from the friendly ones.”

Voicing use of vet-approved calming drops Bengaluru based Neeta Sharma said “That is the only way to calm our pet rescued Indie Frodo. The other two a labrador and a Beagle don’t care much about the sound.”
A boarder at Pet Cafe Hyd | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Not all pet parents can board their pets, or are comfortable with the idea. Many instead look for pet-friendly homestays and resorts away from the city. With several properties now welcoming pets, finding the right one is the only challenge. In Chevella, about 50 kilometres from Hyderabad, homestays have become a welcome respite for pet owners. Ramya R, a pet parent, says the search for a suitable getaway begins soon after Ganesh Chaturthi. “The crackers on visarjan days are a reminder that we need to start looking.”

Pollam Gattu, a farmhouse in Chevella surrounded by carrot and flower fields, has become their regular Deepavali escape. The area sees fewer firecrackers than the city, making it a quieter retreat. “In villages, it is relatively quieter than in the city. I can’t say it is absolutely silent, but it is not as noisy with firecrackers as the city is,” she says.

What about Deepavali puja and other rituals? “We keep the decor light at home. One of our cousins stays back for a few hours to keep the doors open. It is all a matter of arrangement and coordination. In the end, our two-year-old Labrador comes home happy.”

At K-Resorts in Puducherry, almost all of its 56 villas are occupied by pet owners seeking respite from Deepavali noise. Founder Prateek Shah says, “This is the time of year when demand comes not from the holiday crowd but from families in Tamil Nadu looking for a quieter place to celebrate Deepavali.”

articles.title: Google sued over suicide-related AI chats on school computer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The teenager was not able to access Google's Gemini app, nor OpenAI's ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school
The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer.

Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant's low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world.

The teenager was not able to access Google's Gemini app, nor OpenAI's ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google's search engine, which contains AI-powered tools.
Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students.

"Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they're interacting with AI," Andrew Liddell, one of the family's attorneys, told AFP on Thursday.
The complaint alleges that the child had been a "happy 13-year-old girl" in North Carolina who received great grades, played music and participated in Girl Scouts.

Despite "no history" of mental illness, within months of using Google's AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a "quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis" according to the complaint.
On March 17, the school's monitoring software flagged a document titled "Funeral," and the school notified her parents.
Her mother then saw the child writing a farewell letter in real-time after logging into her daughter's account, and her father intervened.
"We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously," Google spokesperson Jose Castaneda told AFP.
Google argues that AI mode includes safeguards against self-harm and attempts to bypass them.
But the child "was able to keep going back over and over and over again," Liddle said. "Whatever safeguards they think they put in place were obviously insufficient."

articles.title: Supreme Court stands firm by March 11 judgment on assessing OBC creamy layer policy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: As far as the operation of the 2025 batch was concerned, the Court said the service allocation would be in compliance with the March 2026 judgment

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) stood firm by its March 11, 2026 judgment , which upheld the assessment of the OBC non-creamy layer status as per a 1993 Office Memorandum, which excluded parental salary income and agricultural income from the income/wealth test.

A Bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and R. Mahadevan did not agree with the government’s plea for a “reasonable time” of two years to undertake the necessary exercise of establishing equivalence of posts after consulting stakeholders and formulating an appropriate and uniform policy/mechanism for determination of OBC creamy layer status.

The court clarified that although the result of the Civil Service Examination 2025 was declared on March 6, 2026, the services had still not been allocated to the successful candidates. It said that since the process of allocation was pending, there would be no reasonable justification to defer the implementation of the March 11 judgment. It said the creamy layer principle, as interpreted in the judgment, would govern the allocation of services of OBC candidates selected through the Civil Service Examination 2025.

The judgment on Friday (November 6, 2026) highlighted the Department of Personnel and Training’s (DoPT) assurance, recorded in the March 2026 verdict, that it would create supernumerary posts to accommodate candidates, who are parties in the case and satisfy the non-creamy layer criteria, subject to their fulfilling all the eligibility conditions. The DoPT position had also been recorded in the 21st Report of the Parliamentary Committee on the Welfare of Other Backward Classes.

Justice Mahadevan said the government may accordingly accommodate the candidates, who are parties before the apex court, provided they fulfil the requisite eligibility criteria. The court clarified that the judgment was applicable to the parties before it and would not be used to reopen appointments concluded prior to the verdict.

The government, in its application filed through Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati for a modification of the March 11 judgment, had said a retrospective implementation of the Supreme Court verdict would have significant consequences for recruitment, service allocation, cadre allocation, seniority, admissions and the administration of OBC reservation generally, affecting lakhs.

The court reiterated that individual claims pending before any court, tribunal, or other competent forum or authority should be considered on their own merits. The court expressed no opinion on the merits of such claims. The court extended the timeline for deciding these claims by eight weeks. On March 11, the court had given a six-month deadline.

The court said the Centre was at liberty to formulate its policy concerning reservation and the creamy layer criteria in accordance with the Constitution. It refused to prescribe any timeline for establishing equivalence between posts or consulting stakeholders in the formulation of the creamy layer policy, noting that these issues fell within the domain of the Executive and the Legislature.
Advocate Shashank Ratnoo, who appeared for the candidates, said the Supreme Court’s intervention has put an end to a decade-long injustice.

Senior advocate P. Wilson, who also represents the candidates, said the Centre had been merely trying to delay, even undo a final judgment of the apex court. He criticised that the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) had failed to comply with court directions, Parliamentary Committee recommendations, and its own 1993 rules.

Under the 1993 Office Memorandum, the government had devised a policy to exclude salary income and agricultural income of parents to calculate whether an OBC candidate belonged to the OBC creamy layer, that is, a high-income group excluded from reservation.

However, in 2004, the DoPT had issued a clarification counting in the salaries of parents working in Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), banks, or private companies, while ignoring the salaries of government employees in equivalent posts. This had led to wards of PSU employees getting disqualified for OBC reservation benefits after being included in the creamy layer bracket, unlike similarly placed children of government officers.

Candidates who qualify for the Mains examination will receive e-summon letters of personality tests (Interviews), which can be downloaded from the commission’s website.

No paper/physical summon letters will be issued for the personality tests (interviews) by the commission.

articles.title: Nedumbassery luxury car crash: Kerala HC grants bail to all four accused
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice Kauser Edappagath allows bail applications of four accused considering that all are in their early twenties, lack of criminal history, and the time already spent in custody
The Kerala High Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) granted bail to the four youths who were accused in the Nedumbassery luxury car accident that led to the death of three young two-wheeler riders.

Justice Kauser Edappagath allowed the bail applications of the four accused, considering that all accused were in their early twenties, the lack of criminal history, and the time already spent in custody. Suhail Sajeev, the first accused would be released on November 16, as the State had sought more time pertaining to the investigation. The other three would be released at the earliest.
The court held that it could not jump to the conclusion that the accused had prior knowledge of the alleged offences owing to mere alcohol consumption or speeding.

The accused had contended that as students, their continued detention would negatively affect their education and that they would fulfil any bail conditions necessary to ensure their continued cooperation.

Around 1.45 a.m. on October 11, the car driven by Sajeev crashed into a two-wheeler on Airport Road near Athani, claiming the lives of Gopika, Devika and Iyas. The other accused – Ninav, Joyal S. Anto and Ameen Shah – were in the car with Sajeev during the incident. All four were charged under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for rash and negligent driving, culpable homicide not amounting to murder, and abetment with a common intention.

articles.title: Relief for Keralam’s Vallarpadam project evictees as Cochin Port Authority releases dredged sand to fortify three rehab sites
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a letter to Executive Engineer, PWD, CoPA has sought details of the agency/contractor concerned and work order

Meeting a long-standing demand of families displaced for the rail and road connectivity project linked to the Vallarpadam International Container Transshipment Terminal (ICTT), the Cochin Port Authority (CoPA) has agreed to release, free of cost, 52,958.70 cubic metres of dredged sand currently stocked at Puthuvypeen for fortifying three rehabilitation sites identified for the evictees.

In a letter issued to the Executive Engineer, PWD, the CoPA has sought details of the agency/contractor concerned and the work order, registration numbers of the vehicles to be engaged for transportation, and those of the authorised representative in charge of the sand stack yard and available during transportation. Production of a transit pass from the Geologist has also been sought before the commencement of transportation.

“We have been demanding this for long. The sand will be used for fortifying the rehabilitation sites at Mulavukad for 14 families, Adarsh Nagar and Indira Nagar for 56 and 118 families respectively in Thuthiyoor near Kakkanad. We have also submitted a memorandum to the Minister in charge of Ernakulam, Rojy M. John, detailing our demands, including a job for one person from each displaced family as promised,” said Francis Kalathungal, general convenor of the Moolamppilly Coordination Committee.

As many as 316 families were evicted from seven villages for the project in 2008, including the forcible eviction of ten families from Moolamppilly. A government order issued by the then Principal Secretary, Revenue, on March 19, 2008, in connection with the rehabilitation package, had promised employment to one person from each evicted family based on educational qualifications. However, the CoPA has remained non-committal on the demand for jobs.

Mr. John said a delegation representing the evictees had recently met him and submitted a memorandum. “The State government will convene a meeting of stakeholders to resolve their issues. Before that, we will have to study the matter,” he said.

Meanwhile, the PWD has written to the district administration requesting to deposit ₹2.68 crore, the collective estimate for transporting sand and fortifying the three rehabilitation sites, as a prelude to submit the estimate for technical sanction. The district administration has accorded administrative sanction for the construction of a protection wall for rehabilitation plots allotted to four families along the banks of a water body, for which the Executive Engineer of the Irrigation Division, Ernakulam, has submitted an estimate of ₹19.50 lakh.

articles.title: AAP spent Centre's ₹1,600 crore flood relief funds for Punjab elsewhere: CM Saini
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini on Friday (November 6, 2026) alleged that the AAP government in Punjab had spent elsewhere the ₹1,600 crore announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the flood-hit State last year.

Mr. Saini said he had earlier watched a video on social media in which Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann had promised compensation for every loss suffered by people during the devastating floods, down to a single hen.
CM Mann had also said he did not need to look towards the Centre for funds, Mr. Saini said.
However, when floods hit Punjab, CM Mann did not have money to compensate farmers, the Haryana Chief Minister told reporters in Chandigarh.
The Prime Minister had provided ₹1,600 crore to Punjab and ₹1,500 crore to Himachal Pradesh for the natural calamity last year, Saini said.

"Himachal did not say that it had not received the money, as it utilised it. The Punjab government is still saying that it has not received the money, whereas it spent the funds elsewhere," he alleged.

Mr. Saini further claimed that farmers from Punjab had told him that AAP ministers distributed compensation cheques in their presence and posed for photographs with the media, but took the cheques back after the media left.
"This is what they do. Then how will the people of Punjab vote for them?" he asked.
Targeting CM Mann, Mr. Saini said the Punjab Chief Minister had spent five years cracking jokes instead of working.
He also alleged that AAP had failed to fulfil its pre-election promise of providing ₹1,000 per month to every woman in Punjab ahead of the 2022 Assembly polls.
The women were made to wait until the next elections drew near, he said, asking who would now pay them the promised arrears of ₹50,000.
Mr. Saini accused the Congress and its INDIA bloc partners of repeatedly targeting constitutional institutions, including the Election Commission, alleging that it had become their habit.

articles.title: Lab tests show ethanol blend in E20 petrol as high as 31% in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs of Karnataka demands penalising OMCs, an E20 spoilage fund to compensate consumers

Petrol sold by several major oil companies in Karnataka contained ethanol far above the prescribed 20% level, in some cases as high as 31.2%, the State government has alleged, raising questions about transparency in the controversial ethanol blend petrol being sold to consumers across the country.

The samples in question were taken recently by the Department of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs from Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Tumakuru, and Dakshina Kannada districts in Karnataka, said Rizwan Arshad, Minister of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Karnataka, on November 6.

Petrol samples from major Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) recorded ethanol blend percentage of 31.2% and 30.5%, respectively. Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), Nayara, and Shell petrol samples revealed 26.5%, 26.1%, and 25.5% ethanol blend, respectively, he said.

Mr. Arshad said the samples were initially submitted to the in-house laboratories of IOCL and BPCL. But. he claimed, the test reports issued by these laboratories did not disclose the ethanol content in the fuel, despite it being one of the prescribed testing parameters. “This raises serious concerns on transparency from the oil majors and what they are hiding from the consumers,” he said.

“The Department of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Karnataka, later got the same samples tested at labs recognised by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), and International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO). These reports have revealed higher ethanol blends,” Mr. Arshad said.

The Modi Government has already forced E20 petrol on the people, despite serious concerns over reduced mileage, additional fuel expenses and compatibility with older vehicles. Now, what we have uncovered in Karnataka is even more alarming. Our Government's independent laboratory tests have found ethanol content as high as 31.2% in petrol sold by major oil companies, with samples from seven districts exceeding the prescribed 20% limit. Even the Centre has acknowledged that E20 can reduce fuel efficiency in certain vehicles. What happens when the ethanol content goes beyond 30%? Who will bear the additional fuel costs and the risk to vehicle performance? Why should ordinary motorists pay the price for such failures? And look at the Modi Government's double standards: It claims ethanol blending benefits farmers, yet it has now excluded ethanol made from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from its latest procurement tender. At a time when Karnataka's farmers are already suffering from severe drought, the Centre is restricting an important market for sugarcane-based ethanol while allowing petrol to be sold with ethanol levels far beyond the prescribed limit. Where is the promised benefit to farmers? Where is the protection for motorists? Is this not deceiving both farmers and consumers? Prime Minister @narendramodi and Union Minister @nitin_gadkari owe the people an explanation. When the Union Government itself has prescribed a 20% blending standard, how is petrol containing over 30% ethanol reaching consumers? Who is monitoring these oil companies? Where is the accountability? We will place Karnataka's findings before the Union Government. I demand an immediate investigation, strict action against those responsible, transparent disclosure of ethanol content at every petrol pump and necessary safeguards for consumers.
ALSO WATCH SC refuses plea seeking mandatory E20 ethanol disclosure

Mr. Arshad said 99% of India’s over 35 crore vehicles are not built for ethanol blend of more than 20%, and the risk is not just limited to old vehicles. “Vehicles sold after April 2023 have been certified only up to E20. With lower-ethanol blend petrol withdrawn from nearly one lakh fuel stations, the consumer has been left with no alternative,” he said.
Assuming a 10% mileage loss at ₹100/litre, he said the hidden loss to consumers would add up to around ₹62,000 crore, on the basis of India’s consumption of 6,200 crore litres of fuel every year.
The Minister claimed that adding damage and repair costs due to higher blends, the loss would be around ₹1 lakh crore, but did not elaborate on how he arrived at this figure.

Mr. Arshad demanded that the Union Government penalise OMCs for ‘over-blending’, even as the Karnataka government will continue to conduct these tests and release their findings. “Every fuel pump in the country should be mandated to display ethanol blend percentage, allowing consumers to choose between the range of blends available,” he said.

The Minister demanded that the Union Government establish an E20 spoilage fund and compensate every consumer whose vehicle has been damaged, through a time-bound claims process with damage certified by authorised service centres.

The Minister demanded that the Union Government establish an E20 spoilage fund and compensate every consumer whose vehicle has been damaged, through a time-bound claims process with damage certified by authorised service centres.

articles.title: Supreme Court seeks response from NewsClick, Purkayastha on ED plea against High Court order
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Court seeks replies from NewsClick, Purkayastha on ED plea challenging Delhi High Court order quashing money-laundering case; responses to be filed within four weeks

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) sought responses from news portal NewsClick and its editor-in-chief, Prabir Purkayastha, on a plea by the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) against a Delhi High Court order that quashed a money-laundering case registered for alleged violations of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) rules.
A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to NewsClick and Mr. Purkayastha and sought their responses within four weeks.

At the outset, the counsel appearing for the ED sought four weeks’ time, as Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju, representing the agency, was not available. Justice Bagchi initially said that the appeal did not inspire confidence.
The ED counsel further submitted that the Delhi Police was also in the process of challenging the quashing of the FIR related to the predicate offence and sought a four-week adjournment.

On May 29, the Delhi High Court had said the continuation of an FIR registered by the Delhi Police’s Economic Offences Wing (EOW) was “nothing but a gross abuse of the process of law”, and once the FIR under the predicate offence was quashed, the ED’s Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) in the matter was also liable to be closed.

The EOW’s 2020 FIR alleged that PPK NewsClick Studio Pvt. Ltd., the parent company of NewsClick, received ₹9.59 crore FDI from Worldwide Media Holdings LLC, U.S., in the financial year 2018-19, in violation of the foreign investment law.

articles.title: Railway freezes proposal to extend Kollam-Kottayam MEMU to Ernakulam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The decision comes daily commuters and passengers’ associations said that extending the route to Ernakulam would disrupt the current schedule and inconvenience regular commuters.

The Railway Ministry has temporarily frozen the proposal to extend the 66315/66316 Kollam–Kottayam–Kollam MEMU train to Ernakulam. The decision comes in the wake of intense protests from daily commuters and passengers’ associations.

According to Kodikunnil Suresh MP, Railways had earlier approved a proposal to introduce a new train service on the Ernakulam–Kottayam–Kollam route to ease the severe overcrowding and travel hardship faced by passengers on the Venad Express. However, instead of introducing a fresh service as requested, officials moved to extend the existing Kollam–Kottayam MEMU to Ernakulam. The MP alleged that this move to extend the current service instead of sanctioning a new train stemmed from political intervention by the BJP.

The MEMU service is crucial for hundreds of daily commuters across key stations including Kollam, Sasthamkotta, Karunagappally, Kayamkulam, Chengannur, Tiruvalla, Changanassery, and Kottayam. The train’s current schedule provides vital relief, especially for evening commuters travelling from Kottayam towards Kollam and intermediate stops. Passengers had expressed deep concern that extending the route to Ernakulam would disrupt the current schedule and inconvenience regular commuters.

articles.title: Devi Shetty conferred with France’s National Order of Merit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dr. Shetty was recognised for extending vaccination and logistical support to the French Consulate and the wider French community during the pandemic

The Government of France has conferred the Chevalier de l’Ordre national du Mérite (Knight of the National Order of Merit) on Devi Shetty, founder and chairman of Narayana Health, in recognition of his support to the French community in Bengaluru during the COVID-19 pandemic.
The honour was presented by Marc Lamy, Consul General of France in Bengaluru, at a ceremony held at Narayana Health City on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

Dr. Shetty was recognised for extending vaccination and logistical support to the French Consulate and the wider French community during the pandemic, demonstrating solidarity at a time of unprecedented challenges.

“We are delighted to recognise Dr. Devi Shetty for his generosity and unwavering support to the French community in Bengaluru during the pandemic. His actions reflect the true spirit of solidarity and the enduring friendship between France and India,” Mr. Lamy said.
Accepting the honour, Dr. Shetty said he was grateful to the French government and acknowledged the contribution of Narayana Health’s teams in extending assistance during the pandemic.

“During the pandemic, we were happy to extend our support to the French community in Bengaluru. It was a difficult time for everyone, and standing together and helping one another was what mattered most,” he said.

Established in 1963 by French President Charles de Gaulle, the Ordre national du Mérite is France’s second-highest national distinction after the Legion of Honour. It recognises distinguished service by French and foreign nationals in civilian and military fields.
The ceremony was attended by members of the French Consulate, the Narayana Health board and management, and the French community.

An intercity bus that was carrying children and teenagers to school crashed on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning in eastern France, killing one minor and one young adult, French authorities said.
The Prefecture in the Ain region said one minor and one young adult were killed, while 16 people were injured, including three seriously.

articles.title: Asian parties reject ‘unilateral actions’, call for respect for international law
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The declaration was unanimously adopted at the 13th General Assembly of ICAPP, held in Seoul from November 4 to 6, with representatives of 83 political parties from across Asia participating

The International Conference of Asian Political Parties (ICAPP) on Friday (November 6, 2026) adopted the Seoul Declaration, expressing concern over unilateral actions and reaffirming state sovereignty and territorial integrity, while also calling for strict adherence to the principles of the UN Charter amid growing geopolitical tensions.

The declaration was unanimously adopted at the 13th General Assembly of ICAPP, held in Seoul from November 4 to 6, with representatives of 83 political parties from across Asia participating. The summit was jointly hosted by South Korea’s governing Democratic Party and the Opposition People Power Party.

The plenary sessions of the Assembly, attended by representatives from Palestine, Iran, China, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and others, saw discussions on contemporary conflicts, including in Palestine and Iran. Though there is no reference to these conflicts in the declaration, members expressed “great concern” on unilateral actions, intensifying geopolitical rivalry and weakening international cooperation. It said non-interference in the internal affairs of states, the peaceful settlement of international disputes, and the equal status of all nations were essential to maintaining peace, stability and reconciliation.

“We were particularly concerned that in international relations, unilateral actions, the use of the threat of force, and selective observance of international obligations can erode confidence in the international legal order,” reads the declaration.

Rejecting the use or threat of force as instruments of diplomacy, the participating parties called on all countries to respect international law consistently, irrespective of their size or geopolitical influence. They also stressed the need to keep diplomatic channels open, including between adversaries.
The declaration sought to place the principles of the UN Charter at the centre of efforts to rebuild trust among nations.

Answering a question from The Hindu on whether ICAPP can be a platform for mediation and conflict resolution in Asia, Chung Eui-yong, Chairperson of the ICAPP Standing Committee and former Minister of Foreign Affairs of South Korea, said ICAPP is a platform for dialogue between political parties and that parties can influence governments in moving towards peaceful settlement of disputes.

“We are not governments. Political parties represent people. What we can do is influence our governments. The governing as well as Opposition parties should put in their best effort to influence government policies and promote peace,” said Mr. Chung.
He added that in the Seoul declaration, “we agreed to reject war as an instrument of coercion. This demonstrates our strong commitment to peaceful settlement of conflicts.”

Beyond geopolitical security, the declaration addressed challenges to democratic governance, climate change and the rapid development of artificial intelligence. It highlighted a growing deficit of trust between nations, citizens, and institutions, and called for responsible, human-centred oversight of AI technologies, equitable climate finance for developing countries facing climate-related disasters, and stronger democratic accountability.

The assembly also welcomed the launch of the Inter-Continental Dialogue among Political Parties (ICDPP), an initiative aimed at bridging ideological differences and preventing the international community from fragmenting into competing blocs.
The 14th ICAPP General Assembly will be held in 2028 in Vietnam.

articles.title: Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Judge Tanya Chutkan’s temporary restraining order came just over an hour after the National Capital Planning Commission approved the memorial arch in an 8-4 vote
A federal judge late on Thursday (November 5, 2026) blocked the Trump administration from breaking ground on a towering memorial arch for 14 days.

The temporary restraining order by U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, halting the work, represents a major setback for one of President Donald Trump’s most prominent projects in his vision to remake Washington.

The decision followed a series of steps taken earlier on Thursday by the government, including the final approval of the arch by the National Capital Planning Commission in an 8-4 vote after a hearing of nine and a half hours, where dozens of witnesses opposed the construction.

The administration said the work could begin as soon as the approval was in place, the Interior Department issued a final decision authorising construction and the National Park Service published the proper notification.
In issuing the temporary stop, Judge Chutkan said Virginia and the District of Columbia had shown that the immediacy of the construction would cause real harm to the plaintiffs.

“The harm is certain,” she wrote. “Defendants initially notified the court that construction could begin as early as November 5, 2026, if the NCPC approves the project at its meeting that day and the Department of the Interior authorizes construction.” In their filing, Virginia and the District of Columbia warned of traffic pattern distortions, as well as concerns about the impact on mutual aid emergency calls if the arch were to proceed.

“Second, the District and Virginia will incur significant unrecoverable costs. As soon as construction begins, DDOT [District Department of Transportation] will need to expend staff time and operating resources to affirmatively and proactively manage temporary detours, crashes or disabled vehicles,” Judge Chutkan wrote.

The judge’s decision came just over an hour after the commission’s hearing ended. The final vote came after nine and a half hours and scores of people opposing it. The vote broke along federal and local lines. Those in favour work for the administration or are connected to the President, who was pushing for the immediate construction. Opponents represented the city of Washington.
The panel’s Trump-appointed chairman launched the meeting with a gushing appraisal of the towering monument and lauded Mr. Trump for wanting to build it.

“President Trump understands as president and a superb builder that it’s important to our national identity to display who we are through grand monuments,” said Mark Paoletta, the commission’s chairman.

As Mr. Trump has often remarked, “the great cities around the world have arches: Paris, Rome, London,” said Mr. Paoletta, who also serves as general counsel for the White House Office of Management and Budget.

Commissioner Paul Ingrassia, a lawyer for the General Services Administration, said the arch was “not about politics. It’s about remembrance. It’s about celebrating our history. It’s about commemorating veterans. And it’s really something that’s a noble tribute to our nation and something that we can all rally behind.”

articles.title: After Donald Trump’s midterm poll rout, South America breathes easy as far-right feels the heat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Just a day after a blue wave swept across the U.S. in midterms election shaking President Donald Trump’s administration, the fall of Santiago Pena carries significance beyond the borders of the country of seven million people

On Wednesday (November 4, 2026), rising tensions in Asuncion, the capital of Paraguay, turned violent as hundreds of thousands stormed the streets to protest locking out of their accounts in the country’s biggest bank. As fires burned and people anxiously queued outside the collapsed bank, President Santiago Pena, a former shareholder in the bank, announced his resignation.

But as Congress moved to impeach him, Mr. Pena disappeared amid rumours that he had fled to Argentina — just as Brazilian far-right leader Flávio Bolsonaro did last week before fleeing to U.S. after losing the election to President Lula da Silva. “We have information that he left the country without telling anyone. I think he went to Argentina and sought asylum,” said Paraguayan Senator Antonio Velázquez on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

articles.title: Keralam’s mangrove cover expanded in past decade despite prior decline, finds study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute based in Kochi compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts
Mangrove cover in Keralam registered an overall increase over the past decade, a new study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) has found.

The study, presented at the international symposium on fisheries and remote sensing hosted at CMFRI, compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts. It found an overall rise in mangrove cover during the period, despite the State having lost nearly 90% of its mangroves over the past five decades, a statement issued by CMFRI in Kochi said.

Mangroves serve as vital breeding and nursery grounds for fish, protect coastlines from cyclones and storm surges, and help absorb atmospheric carbon. The findings highlight the potential of satellite-based monitoring to track mangrove recovery and support conservation efforts along Keralam’s coast.

The three-day international symposium is being jointly organised by Trevor Platt Science Foundation, Department of Chemical Oceanography of the Cochin University of Science and Technology (CUSAT), CMFRI and Marine Biological Association of India.

Another study presented at the symposium highlighted the increasing incidence of marine heatwaves in the Bay of Bengal. The region experienced more than 100 marine heatwave events between 1982 and 2023, with both their frequency and cumulative intensity showing an increasing trend.
The study was presented by the Department of Oceanography of Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh.

articles.title: Air quality of Delhi worsens, many parts reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Many parts of the national capital, including IIT Delhi, ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri, witnessed “severe” level air pollution

The overall air quality of Delhi worsened and continued to be in the “very poor” category on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning, while many parts of the city reeled under “severe” level of air pollution, according to official data.
Many parts of the national capital, including IIT Delhi, ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri, witnessed “severe” level air pollution.
Other cities and towns in north India, including Noida, Gurugram, and Faridabad also witnessed overall “very poor” air quality, on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning.
The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 391 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on Friday, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.
“Severe” level air pollution affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing diseases, as per the CPCB.
The overall air quality of Delhi is likely to be in the “severe” category for three days, as per the Central government’s ‘Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi’.

The 24-hour average overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi stood at 369 (very poor) on Thursday at 4 p.m. on Thursday, slightly down from 377 (very poor) a day earlier, as per the Central Pollution Control Board’s daily bulletin, which is treated as the day’s AQI. A higher AQI means worsening of air quality.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

articles.title: Vattavada panchayat in Munnar imposes entry fee for tourist vehicles
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A green checkpost has been set up at Oorkkad near Vattavada to collect the fee

The Vattavada grama panchayat near the Munnar hill station in Idukki has introduced an entry fee for tourist vehicles, effective October 31. According to officials, a green checkpost has been set up at Oorkkad near Vattavada to collect the fee. The rates are fixed at ₹100 for tourist buses, ₹50 for cars, and ₹30 for two-wheelers. Vattavada panchayat assistant secretary Pratheesh Raj P.J. said the fee was introduced to ensure proper waste management in the emerging destination.

“The entry fee does not apply to local residents or those operating businesses in the Vattavada area,” the official said. “When vehicles enter, staff stationed at the checkpost will provide a bag to deposit waste, which visitors can hand over upon their return. Plastic waste will also be collected at entry. Under current guidelines, the panchayat cannot utilise plan funds for waste treatment activities, and due to this funding shortfall, sanitation workers have gone unpaid for the past three months. The entry fee will be utilised entirely for waste management and local tourism development,” said the official.

Officials noted that Vattavada is an increasingly popular getaway near Munnar, which attracts large crowds, thanks to its cool-season vegetable and fruit farming. However, the influx has led to widespread dumping of food and plastic waste along roadsides, which the panchayat cannot manage without dedicated revenue. “The panchayat spent an average of ₹45 lakh on waste treatment works over the past year, and due to the fund crisis, we cannot sustain these operations without alternative revenue. The entry fee has been introduced specifically for this purpose,” an official stated.

Mr. Pratheesh Raj further highlighted the role of the Chakliya community in local sanitation efforts. “Out of 42 sanitation and Haritha Karma Sena workers, 38 belong to the Chakliya community. Ensuring job and wage security for them is vital for the panchayat,” he said. Officials added that the local body also plans to channel revenue into infrastructure upgrades to further support sustainable tourism in Vattavada.

articles.title: Swift grievance redressal system for entrepreneurs and investors put in place on K-SWIFT portal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Every query or grievance registered through the system will be automatically routed to the department and officer concerned.

A ticket-based query and grievance redressal system has been put in place under the ‘Invest Kerala Helpdesk’ on the K-SWIFT Portal as the centralised mechanism for the registration, tracking, escalation and resolution of queries, complaints and grievances raised by entrepreneurs and investors. Every query or grievance registered through the system will be automatically routed to the department and officer concerned.

The helpdesk, implemented by the Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation (KSIDC), will serve as the single point of intake for all queries and grievances relating to the single window system. The government has mandated that the high priority queries and grievances have to be addressed by the respective departments within three days, while the medium ones need to be addressed in five days and low priority grievances within seven days.

Any ticket, especially department or service-level grievances remaining unresolved beyond the applicable timelines shall be automatically escalated to the Managing Director, KSIDC, and thereafter to the Secretary (Industries), who will be the final escalation authority.

As per the single window guidebook approved by the government, no department or agency processing an application through K-SWIFT can mark an application as ‘rejected’, unless the reason for rejection, detailed rejection remarks, the legal or procedural basis for rejection, details of missing or deficient documents are recorded in the system, along with the name, designation, date and time of the officer rejecting the application.

Applicants can file an appeal through K-SWIFT against an eligible rejected application, along with the relevant application and rejection details, grounds of appeal and supporting documents. Every department and agency integrated with K-SWIFT will designate an officer as the Appellate Authority for applications relating to the services under its jurisdiction.

articles.title: Sharad Pawar's health improving, to be discharged on Saturday morning: Sule
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited Mr. Pawar in the hospital

Nationalist Congress Party (SP) MP Supriya Sule has said on Friday (November 6) that her father, Sharad Pawar, the party chief, is recovering and would be discharged from Breach Candy Hospital on Saturday morning (November 7).
He could be discharged at 11 a.m. on Saturday, she told PTI .

Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and TMC chief Mamata Banerjee spoke to her over phone to inquire about her father's health, Ms. Sule added.
Mr. Pawar, 85, was undergoing treatment for respiratory problems and chest infection.
He was admitted to Pune's Ruby Hall Clinic on November 2. After being discharged on November 4, he was admitted to Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai.
Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde on Friday visited Mr. Pawar in the hospital.
“He (Pawar) is doing very well. There is no reason to worry.... He is in good condition, and his willpower is strong,” Mr. Shinde said while talking to reporters.

Mr. Shinde said that during the hospital visit, Mr. Pawar enquired about the drought situation in the State, particularly Satara — both prominent politicians have their ancestral roots in the western Maharashtra district.

The Deputy CM, who heads the ruling coalition ally Shiv Sena, maintained the former Union agriculture minister was sensitive to the drought situation, where 304 talukas are facing a severe water scarcity due to a deficient monsoon this year.
The Shiv Sena chief insisted no political inference should be drawn from the meeting with Pawar, a prominent Opposition politician.

articles.title: Voters in SIR states can now refill Enumeration Forms to get back in final list instead of Form 6
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The directions apply to Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland; the ECI clarified that for those voters who have already filled in Form 6, need not submit the enumeration form with the statement afresh

Voters who have been marked as Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate (ASDD) in the seven States where the SIR process is on at present can now fill the Enumeration Form again to get back into the list instead of resorting to Form 6 which is used for registration of first time voters.
These electors were marked absent as their Enumeration Forms had been issued but not received back, resulting in their exclusion from the Draft Electoral Rolls during the ongoing SIR exercise.

The ECI directive comes after the Supreme Court on October 28 while hearing a petition filed by activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri on deletion of voters through SIR in Delhi, had asked the Election Commission why it was asking the deleted voters to use Form 6 for re-inclusion in rolls and why Form 8 could not be used.

In a directive to CEOs of seven states, Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland, the ECI on Friday (November 6, 2026) said that booth-wise lists of all such electors, who were marked as Absent/Shifted/Dead/Duplicate (ASDD) and whose Enumeration Forms were not received back and consequently who could not be included in the Draft Electoral Roll during the ongoing SIR, shall be displayed afresh on the notice boards of the respective polling stations, from where the names were deleted with the probable reasons for non-inclusion of the names of such electors.
Partially filled Enumeration Forms in respect of all such ASDD electors shall be generated afresh in ERO dashboard in ECINET.

In case an elector has not shifted residence, they may submit their duly filled-in and signed Enumeration Forms along with the enclosed statement, mentioning the reason as to why they could not submit the Enumeration Form earlier while those who have shifted the place of residence within the State, shall submit Enumeration Form along with the Statement enclosed indicating the new address and the Assembly Constituency.

Till now, voters whose names were missing in the draft rolls had to fill Form 6 to re-enter the electoral rolls. Form 6, includes a declaration which says that the said voter has not been registered anywhere else and this had led to concerns among many regarding the legality of the process.
The ECI clarified that for those voters who have already filled in Form 6, need not submit the enumeration form with the statement afresh.

Shortly after the ECI communique, Ms. Bharadwaj and Ms. Johri welcomed the move. “We believe this is an important step in addressing large scale exclusions caused during SIR. The provision to re-assign the old EPIC numbers is important as it will ensure preservation of voter’s historical record of being an existing voter”.
“Just in Delhi, out of 47.56 lakh deleted in the first phase and put on ASDD, 31.59 lakh were marked as permanently shifted and 11.73 as absent/untraceable,” they said.
Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said it was a belated admission that wrongful deletion and exclusion has indeed taken place under the ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate) category.

“The ECI is carrying out corrective after corrective after the nation-wide outrage and anger over SIR which has robbed over 13 crore Indians of their constitutional right to vote. Every new set of orders begs the question: what was the point of this bureaucratic mess that every Indian has been put through? These repeated clarifications and amendments actually expose the true intent of the diabolical PM-HM. They have been caught out,” he said.

articles.title: IAF hands over 39.5-acre sports complex land to Centre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The move comes days after the Land and Development Office under the Ministry issued notices to the facility to return the land on Lok Kalyan Marg

T he Indian Air Force has handed over 39.5 acres of land housing a sports complex, a swimming pool and other amenities to the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, an official said on Friday (November 6, 2026).
The move comes days after the Land and Development Office (L&DO) under the Ministry issued notices to the facility to return the land on Lok Kalyan Marg.

An official said that a joint team of the Defence Estates Office and the L&DO will conduct a survey to determine the boundaries of the land. There has been no official word on the purpose of reclaiming the land parcel.
The sports complex is located near the Delhi Race Club and Jaipur Polo Grounds, where the L&DO under the MoHUA has also taken steps to reclaim land.
In the past few months, the Centre has expedited the process of reclaiming prime land parcels in the surrounding area.

Workers and residents of the jhuggis around the area said that the slum clusters surrounding the Jaipur Polo Grounds and the Delhi Race Club had also witnessed demolitions over the past few weeks, with debris from the demolished structures still lying in the area.

Over the past several weeks, the government has initiated a review of prime land parcels near Lok Kalyan Marg through the L&DO, with a view to reclaiming plots used for defence golf and sports facilities.
The MoHUA had earlier asked the concerned entities to hand over the land housing the Air Force Golf Course.
In August, the department evicted the Delhi Race Club from its 53-acre premises on Lok Kalyan Marg, citing the requirement of the land for an unspecified public purpose.
It also reclaimed the Jaipur Polo Ground from the India Polo Association, citing broader public purposes, governance and defence infrastructure projects.

The Department has also initiated eviction proceedings against the Delhi Gymkhana Club to reclaim its 27-acre premises, citing the need for defence infrastructure. The matter is pending before the court.

Workers and residents of the jhuggis around the area said that the slum clusters surrounding the Jaipur Polo Grounds and the Delhi Race Club had also witnessed demolitions over the past few weeks, with debris from the demolished structures still lying in the area.

Over the past several weeks, the government has initiated a review of prime land parcels near Lok Kalyan Marg through the L&DO, with a view to reclaiming plots used for defence golf and sports facilities.

The MoHUA had earlier asked the concerned entities to hand over the land housing the Air Force Golf Course.

In August, the department evicted the Delhi Race Club from its 53-acre premises on Lok Kalyan Marg, citing the requirement of the land for an unspecified public purpose.

It also reclaimed the Jaipur Polo Ground from the India Polo Association, citing broader public purposes, governance and defence infrastructure projects.

The Department has also initiated eviction proceedings against the Delhi Gymkhana Club to reclaim its 27-acre premises, citing the need for defence infrastructure. The matter is pending before the court.

articles.title: Magnitude-6.1 earthquake hits off Tokyo, no tsunami alert: weather agency
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: There were no immediate reports of damage or injuries
A magnitude-6.1 earthquake struck off the coast of Tokyo on Friday (November 6, 2026), Japanese authorities said, but no tsunami alert was issued.
The shallow quake hit at 7.39 p.m. (1039 GMT) in the sea off the coast of the country’s Kanto region, the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) said on its website.
Its epicentre was about 169 kilometres (105 miles) southeast of Asahi, which is just east of the capital Tokyo, according to the United States Geological Survey.
The JMA said is recorded a “seismic intensity 3” on Japan’s 0-7 scale, meaning that “almost everyone indoors feels the shaking” and “dishes on shelves may rattle”.

articles.title: India-born Saba Haider wins Illinois State Representative election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: An alumnus of Aligarh Muslim University (AMU), Saba Haider earned an MSc in Wildlife Science from the institution; the AMU Network congratulated her on her victory, describing it as a "proud moment for the university community"
India-born Democrat Saba Haider has won election to the Illinois House of Representatives, becoming the first South Asian woman to be elected to the state's General Assembly.

Ms. Haider won the November 3 U.S. mid-term elections from the 84th District with 70.9% of the votes, securing 20,756 ballots against her Republican rival Brian Scopa, who received 8,520 votes, or 29.1%.
The 84th District covers parts of Will, DuPage, Kane and Kendall counties, including Aurora, Naperville, Oswego, Montgomery and Boulder Hill.

“We did it! We worked hard for the last 15 months talking to voters in every corner of District 84 to learn what they care about, what they want to see change, and how we can work together to build stronger, more prosperous, and more inclusive communities,” Ms. Haider said in a social media post on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
She thanked voters, family members, friends, campaign team members and volunteers, describing the campaign as a "grassroots, people-powered movement".
"Ultimately this election was about the people who call this community home. It was about building the future we all deserve," she said.
Ms. Haider said her victory was for everyone who believes in an Illinois that is "a fair, just, and welcoming place for all".
Before entering the Illinois legislature, Ms. Haider served as a DuPage County Board member and community advocate.
Born in India, her family hails from Bulandshahr district in Uttar Pradesh. She immigrated to the United States about 20 years ago.
“Since then, I’ve dedicated my life towards giving back to the community that helped me and my family make Illinois our home," Haider said during her campaign.

She said she wanted to continue serving the community by taking its concerns to Springfield, the state capital, and working with elected representatives to address the challenges faced by working families.

"I know firsthand the struggles our working families are going through, and I want to work with our elected officials to find solutions to the problems we all face,” Ms. Haider said during her poll campaign.

articles.title: Cyclones caused over ₹500 crore loss to A.P. Energy Department, says Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Over 7,500 power poles damaged by Cyclone Murasu; restoration targeted by Saturday evening, says Gottipati Ravi Kumar

Cyclones Arnab and Murasu have caused preliminary losses of over ₹500 crore to the Andhra Pradesh Energy Department, with more than 7,500 electricity poles damaged by Cyclone Murasu alone, Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar said.

He toured cyclone-affected areas in the Addanki and Santhanuthalapadu Assembly constituencies in Prakasam district on Friday. He said electricity lines, conductors and distribution transformers had suffered extensive damage and restoration work was progressing on a war footing.

The Minister set a target of restoring power supply in all affected areas by Saturday evening. Power supply had been fully restored in the Godavari districts by Thursday evening, while restoration in the remaining cyclone-hit areas had reached 70% by Friday, he said.

He directed officials to prioritise domestic connections, followed by agricultural and aquaculture connections. More than 3,000 electricity personnel from Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana had been deployed for restoration work.

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu coordinated with his counterparts in the three States to mobilise additional manpower and equipment. Mr. Ravi Kumar interacted with electricity personnel from Ballari in Karnataka at Alavalapadu and teams from Nidamanuru.

During his visit to J. Panguluru, Korisapadu and Naguluppalapadu mandals, the Minister inspected damaged mango orchards, nurseries, houses, cattle sheds and electricity infrastructure. Crops such as maize, banana, papaya, amla and mango had also suffered damage.

Tobacco crops and curing barns were affected in parts of Santhanuthalapadu, Addanki and Ongole. The Minister spoke to the Prakasam District Collector and Agriculture Department officials and directed them to complete a speedy and transparent assessment of crop losses.

articles.title: Karnataka CM and Dy. CM question BJP-led Union government on higher ethanol blends
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Pointing to findings from petrol samples tested across the State showing ethanol blends higher than the prescribed 20% on the social media platform X, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said the Union government cannot turn a blind eye to the violation of E20 norms and blend more ethanol, thereby imposing a financial burden on ordinary citizens. “Reduced mileage, potential vehicle damage and rising maintenance costs are concerns that deserve serious attention. It is unacceptable that consumers bear the cost while oil companies continue to report substantial profits,” he said.

Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara said the “Modi-led government had already forced E20 petrol on the people, despite serious concerns over reduced mileage, additional fuel expenses and compatibility with older vehicles,” and the findings by the Department of Legal Metrology, Karnataka, were even more alarming.

He called the BJP-led Union government’s claim that an ethanol blend of petrol would help farmers a “double standard”. “It [the BJP-led Union government] claims that ethanol blending benefits farmers, yet it has now excluded ethanol made from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from its latest procurement tender. At a time when Karnataka’s farmers are already suffering from severe drought, the Centre is restricting an important market for sugarcane-based ethanol while allowing petrol to be sold with ethanol levels far beyond the prescribed limit. Where is the promised benefit to farmers? Where is the protection for motorists? Is this not deceiving both farmers and consumers?” he asked.

Mr. Parameshwara said Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari owe the people an explanation. He demanded “an immediate investigation, strict action against those responsible, transparent disclosure of ethanol content at every petrol pump and necessary safeguards for consumers”.

articles.title: BJP MLA asserts TDP-Jana Sena-BJP alliance will remain intact
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Adinarayana Reddy dismisses YSRCP’s hopes of a split; says alliance will address organisational shortcomings and emerge stronger

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Legislative Assembly Chief Whip and MLA C. Adinarayana Reddy on Friday asserted that the TDP-Jana Sena-BJP alliance would remain intact and emerge stronger, dismissing the YSR Congress Party’s hopes of a split in the coalition.

Addressing a press conference at the BJP State office, he said the alliance had secured public support in the recent local body elections and would strive to improve its performance in future elections by addressing organisational shortcomings.

He cautioned against comparing local body election results with those of general elections, pointing out that candidates’ personal influence, local grievances and lack of coordination among leaders could affect electoral outcomes. The alliance would identify and address these shortcomings, he said.

Targeting YSR Congress Party president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, he alleged that the former Chief Minister was criticising the coalition to remain politically relevant and obstructing development instead of respecting the people’s mandate. He asked Mr. Jagan to explain the CBI and Enforcement Directorate cases against him and demanded that the facts surrounding the murder of former MP Y.S. Vivekananda Reddy be brought to light.

Mr. Adinarayana Reddy accused the previous YSRCP government of undermining the State’s development prospects by delaying the Amaravati capital and Polavaram irrigation projects. The coalition government was according priority to infrastructure development, investment promotion, renewable energy and industrial growth, he said.
Citing investment opportunities in aerospace and defence manufacturing at Puttaparthi, he said the sector could attract investments of around ₹15,000 crore.
Referring to the BJP’s performance in Jammalamadugu constituency, he said the party had won 19 councillor seats in Yerraguntla municipality and secured encouraging results in the MPTC elections.
The alliance aimed to put Andhra Pradesh on a stronger development path by 2029 and realise the vision of a developed State by 2047, he said.
BJP State spokesperson Shaik Baji and party leaders Sashi Bhushan Reddy and Rajesh Reddy were present.

articles.title: Number of polling stations in Keralam increases by 216
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The total number has now gone up to 30,682, says Chief Electoral Officer D. Sajith Babu

The number of polling stations in Keralam has gone up by 216, taking the total number to 30,682, Chief Electoral Officer (Keralam) D. Sajith Babu said on Friday. The Election Commission of India (ECI) had given its approval for the rationalisation of polling stations. Before the exercise, Keralam had 30,471 stations, the same number it had for the 2026 Assembly elections.
While 216 new stations have been formed, five existing ones in Ernakulam district have been merged. Also, 178 polling station buildings/places have been changed.

After the rationalisation, Malappuram continues to have the highest number of polling stations (3,773), followed by Thiruvananthapuram (unchanged at 3,173) and Ernakulam (3,154). Wayanad has the lowest number (717).

The number of voters at each station, availability of amenities, accessibility and geographical peculiarities were taken into account for the exercise. “The new polling stations have been formed, and some of them have been changed based on the criteria prescribed by the ECI and the maximum number of voters allowed in each polling station,” the CEO said.

articles.title: AIDSO opposes move to bring government schools under private adoption
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO), Mysuru district committee, staged a protest near Ramaswamy Circle here on Friday, opposing the State government’s reported move to allow private educational institutions and corporate companies to adopt government schools.
Addressing the protesters, AIDSO district secretary Nitin alleged that the government was paving the way for the closure of 45,000 government schools through the KPS-Magnet policy.

He claimed that a meeting was held at Vidhana Soudha on November 4 to facilitate the adoption of government schools by corporate companies and private educational institutions. “In the first phase, 2,000 government schools would be taken up for adoption,” he alleged.

Criticising remarks by the Chief Minister and other government representatives questioning the quality of education in government schools despite teachers drawing salaries ranging from ₹70,000 to ₹1.5 lakh, he said such statements ignored the government’s responsibility to address policy-related shortcomings in the public education system.

Under the proposal, each private institution would adopt three government schools and be allowed to name the developed schools after itself, the AIDSO claimed in a statement. The government had also reportedly sought private institutions’ support in providing teachers, computers and laboratory equipment, besides making available old buses from private schools, he alleged.
He also claimed that 14 government schools had already been merged with the Hegganuru Karnataka Public School in Kanakapura taluk of Bengaluru South district.

Social activist Ugra Narasimhe Gowda termed the move to hand over government schools built with taxpayers’ money to private institutions as “anti-education”. He urged people to oppose the KPS-Magnet scheme, which he said went against the spirit of the Right to Education Act.
Retired Kannada professor Latha Mysuru criticised Kannada activists and writers for not opposing the policy. DSS leader Chornalli Shivanna also spoke.
Members of the Save Public Education Committee, farmers’ associations, social activists, AIDSO office-bearers and students participated in the protest.
