articles.title: $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq 100 as U.S. midterm outcome adds to AI stock slump
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Democrats’ victories raise prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects as investors reassess AI spending; Indian equities buck global market weakness

Global technology stocks tumbled on fears that the massive infrastructure investments underpinning the artificial intelligence (AI) boom may take longer to build, finance and monetise, even as Indian equities bucked the worldwide sell-off with a sharp rally on November 6.

The sell-off, fuelled by concerns over mounting AI-related capital expenditure and uncertain returns, gathered momentum following the U.S. midterm election results. Democrats’ victories have heightened the prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects and possible restrictions on new developments, adding to investor anxiety.

The Nasdaq-100 plunged 6.36% on November 5, erasing approximately $2.53 trillion from its aggregate adjusted market value, according to Nasdaq index data. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 4.36% and 3.44%, respectively.
Semiconductor stocks bore the brunt, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index slumping 12.2%. Nvidia lost about 9%, while AMD and Micron Technology shed more than 17% each.
The weakness spilled over into Asian markets on Friday. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 6.02%, after plunging more than 8% intraday. Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 5.96%, while Taiwan’s TAIEX lost 4.51%.
Indian equities, however, bucked the trend. The Sensex surged 1,718 points, or 2.17%, to close at 81,028.02, while the Nifty 50 advanced 2.01% to 25,030.35.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) were net buyers of Indian equities worth ₹14,974.68 crore on November 5, against net sales of ₹10,444.54 crore by domestic institutional investors (DIIs), provisional exchange data across the NSE, BSE and MSEI showed.

A Macquarie Research note flagged potential regulatory headwinds for data-centre development following election outcomes in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, where proposals to impose moratoriums or restrictions on new projects could affect the industry.

Greater scrutiny of power connections, backup-generator emissions, water consumption, zoning and taxation could prolong approvals and raise project costs. The impact may be more pronounced for projects in the pipeline than for facilities that have already secured approvals and power capacity.

Macquarie said approved but unleased data-centre capacity could gain value if fresh supply faces delays, benefiting well-capitalised operators with access to power and approved sites. It remained positive on the digital infrastructure sector.

The broader concern is whether chip demand can translate into supplier revenues if data-centre projects are held up by financing constraints, electricity shortages or regulatory hurdles. Capital Market Laboratories analyst Ophir Gottlieb has argued that slower construction could favour cloud companies with existing infrastructure, even as equipment suppliers face order delays.

Yet underlying demand remains robust. AMD’s data-centre revenue surged 97% year-on-year to $8.55 billion in the September quarter. According to a November 5 Huatai Research analysis, the company expects segment revenue to grow about 50% sequentially in the December quarter. AMD also expects overall revenue growth of more than 80% in 2027, with data-centre operations contributing over 80% of total revenue.

articles.title: ADNOC inks 10-year LNG supply and purchase agreement with Gujarat Energy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: This would be ADNOC’s fifth long-term LNG supply agreement with India.

Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) on Friday signed a 10-year sales and purchase agreement with Gujarat Energy to supply up to four million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from 2028, further strengthening its presence in India’s expanding gas market.
The agreement marks ADNOC’s fifth LNG supply deal with an Indian company, following similar arrangements with Bharat Petroleum, Indian Oil Corporation, GAIL and Hindustan Petroleum.
Under the agreement, XRG, ADNOC’s international investment arm, will supply LNG produced outside the Gulf and owned by it through ADNOC’s global LNG marketing and trading platform.

He added, “Through our integrated LNG marketing and trading platform, we are connecting our growing international portfolio with customers in key regions across global markets, while providing India with reliable, flexible and long-term LNG supplies.”

ADNOC’s global LNG marketing and trading platform also has supply agreements with Japan’s INPEX and Thailand’s Gulf Group. The platform aims to market 47 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of LNG beyond 2030.
Avantika Singh Aulakh, Managing Director of Gujarat Energy, said, “Through this partnership, Gujarat Energy and ADNOC are joining forces to fully realize the power of our collaboration.”
Gujarat Energy operates a city gas distribution network spanning 44 districts across six states.

articles.title: Trump discusses West Asia de-escalation with Qatar's Emir
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The telephone call between Trump and Qatar's Emir Sheik Tamim bin Hamad al Thani centred on international efforts to end tensions, according to a statement from the Qatari ruler's media office

U.S. President Donald Trump has discussed efforts to de-escalate tensions in the West Asia in a telephone call with Qatar's Emir as the region remained on edge over the possibility of renewed U.S. military action against Iran.
The telephone call between Mr. Trump and Qatar's Emir Sheik Tamim bin Hamad al Thani centred on international efforts to end tensions, according to a statement from the Qatari ruler's media office.
The two discussed in particular Qatar's mediation efforts aimed at reaching “a comprehensive agreement that ends the crisis and achieves security and stability in the region.”

Qatar has been mediating between the United States and Iran to end the war. Qatar and other U.S.-allied Gulf Arab countries came under heavy fire from Iran earlier in the U.S.-Iran war and have been anxious to avoid a new escalation that could leave them vulnerable to attacks.

During the call, Sheik Tamim “stressed the importance of continuing dialogue and adopting diplomatic means to resolve disputes, sparing the region further escalation, and ensuring freedom of maritime navigation and the security of energy supplies,” according to the statement.

articles.title: Europe bomb threats 'likely co-ordinated campaign': Irish government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The hoaxes in Dublin came as more European flights were also hit on November 6 by bomb threats, the latest this week forcing authorities to reroute some planes or escort civilian aircraft with fighter jets

Ireland's government said on Friday (November 6, 2026) that hoax bomb claims sent to Irish media outlets amid a spate of threats against Europe-wide flights were "likely" part of a "co-ordinated campaign of disruption".

The hoaxes in Dublin came as more European flights were also hit on Friday (November 6, 2026) by bomb threats, the latest this week forcing authorities to reroute some planes or escort civilian aircraft with fighter jets.

The Irish government confirmed police responded after national broadcaster RTE , Virgin Media , Newstalk radio, and The Irish Independent newspaper all received what turned out to be hoax bomb claims.
"It is not known yet who is responsible for these threats, whether it is individuals or a centralised or co-ordinated effort," it said in a statement.
"However, these threats come on the heels of the ongoing disruption to aviation around Europe caused by similar threats, and it seems likely that this is a co-ordinated campaign of disruption."
It added that "the threats made this morning against media organisations here are very serious".
"Hoax threats such as these cause fear, distress and disruption to people going about their daily lives and activities; they achieve no positive purpose whatsoever," the statement said.
It noted police were working alongside Ireland's military, cyber, and aviation authorities, as well as European counterparts, to find the culprits.
"Every effort will be made to identify those responsible and to hold them to account," the government vowed.
Police were promptly deployed to RTE's Dublin headquarters and the other targeted sites following the threats, the outlets reported.
Newstalk radio host Claire Byrne said after returning to air that staff there had been advised to leave their building following "a message that we received".
"We've been advised that we could return to the building and that that warning was a hoax," she added.

articles.title: Jay Rockefeller, heir to famed dynasty and healthcare advocate in U.S. Senate, dies at 89
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Jay Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was a great-grandson of oil tycoon John ‌D. Rockefeller and the scion of a family that formed a political dynasty

John D. “Jay” Rockefeller IV, the progeny of one of America’s most famous and wealthiest families, who during three decades in the U.S. Senate sought expanded healthcare for the poor and excoriated President George W. Bush’s handling of ​the Iraq War, died on Friday (November 6, 2026) at his home in Washington, the Washington Post reported. He was 89.
His family did not provide a cause, the ‌newspaper added.

Mr. Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was elected in 1984 to the first of his ​five six-year terms representing West Virginia in the Senate after two terms as Governor of the poor coal-mining State.

Mr. Rockefeller voted ⁠in 2002 in favour of the Republican Bush’s measure authorising the Iraq war, which began with a U.S.-led invasion in 2003. He later expressed regret over that vote and, as head of the Senate intelligence committee, accused Mr. Bush of taking the nation to war on “false premises.”

articles.title: Airstrikes on market in southwestern Yemen kill at least 20, Houthis say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson, Anees Alsabahi, told Houthi-run TV Al Masirah that 15 people were also wounded in the airstrikes on the market in al-Waziyah in the province of Taiz
Airstrikes hit a market in southwestern Yemen on Friday (November 6, 2026), killing at least 20 people, according to an official with Iran-backed Houthi rebels.
It would be one of the deadliest attacks since fighting resumed between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces.
A Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson, Anees Alsabahi, told Houthi-run TV Al Masirah that 15 people were also wounded in the airstrikes on the market in al-Waziyah in the province of Taiz.
He said that the death toll was expected to rise from the airstrikes, which he blamed on the Saudi-led coalition.

Local authorities in Taiz acknowledged that an attack on a busy market killed and wounded people, without providing details on the actual toll. But the authorities in Taiz blamed the Houthis for the incident. They said that no airstrikes were carried out in the area.
The Associated Press couldn't immediately independently verify the claims of responsibility.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans

Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.
Editorial Context: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Myanmar to conduct byelections next April
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The move indicates the military's increasing confidence in its ability to control territory in the Southeast Asian nation after it claimed advances following a string of offensives

Myanmar will hold byelections next April, the polling commission said on Friday (November 6, 2026), encompassing areas where the pro-military parliament could not previously hold voting due to the country's devastating civil war.
The move indicates the military's increasing confidence in its ability to control territory in the Southeast Asian nation after it claimed advances following a string of offensives.
Myanmar has been embroiled in civil war since the military ousted the elected government of Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi in 2021.
The junta staged phased elections last December and January, which it touted as a return to democracy following the coup.
But the highly restrictive poll was blocked in areas where rebels seized control in opposition to military rule, rejecting the elections as a charade.
The Union Election Commission said byelections will take place on April 4, 2027 in 39 constituencies of the lower and upper houses of Parliament, according to a statement published by state media.
According to an AFP tally, one-third of those constituencies are places where voting in the previous elections was called off for security reasons.
The scheduled votes are in areas where fighting is still raging, though, including the northern region of Sagaing, central Mandalay region and the western state of Chin.
The remaining two-thirds of constituencies will replace lawmakers who have been compelled by the constitution to vacate their seats after being promoted to senior government roles.
Myanmar's Parliament is dominated by lawmakers from the pro-military Union Solidarity and Development Party, while Suu Kyi's party was dissolved and she remains detained.
Min Aung Hlaing, who led the 2021 coup that ousted Suu Kyi, was swiftly voted in as civilian president. Analysts and activists describe the new government as a fig leaf for military rule.
The civil war sparked by the military takeover is now in its sixth year, and is estimated to have claimed over 100,000 lives according to conflict monitor ACLED.

articles.title: Israel Opposition eases on ultra-Orthodox draft to oust Netanyahu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Listing the most important goals as removing Netanyahu and avoiding new elections, Opposition partner Avigdor Liberman said it was time to compromise and "understand that trying to have everything risks getting nothing".

Israel's Opposition saw a new path on Friday (October 6, 2026) to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as one of its leaders backtracked on demands that ultra-Orthodox Jews serve in the military, opening the door to a once improbable alliance with the community.
Neither Mr. Netanyahu nor Opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot reached a majority in the October 27 election, with Israeli society highly polarised over Mr. Netanyahu and worn down by three years of war.

Mr. Eisenkot, a former military commander whose campaign sought to appeal to secular and liberal Israelis, could form a government with Israeli-Arabs, whose seat count soared on anger over Mr. Netanyahu's far-right government.

But an alliance with Israeli-Arabs faces strong disagreement from Opposition partner Avigdor Liberman, a one-time aide to Mr. Netanyahu who now sharply criticises the Prime Minister but shares his hawkish views on the Palestinians.

Mr. Liberman said on Friday (November 6, 2026) he would not back down on refusing to work with Israeli-Arabs but called for talks with ultra-Orthodox Jews, even though he has berated the community for years and ran on promises to end its exemption from Israel's mandatory military service.

Listing the most important goals as removing Mr. Netanyahu and avoiding new elections, Mr. Liberman said it was time to compromise and "understand that trying to have everything risks getting nothing".
"This also includes the issue of the conscription law," he said in a social media statement.

"This pains me, and I know it pains many others as well. But given the full range of challenges we face today, the national interest of the State of Israel and the Jewish people must take precedence over all other considerations."

President Isaac Herzog plans on Sunday (November 8, 2026) to announce who will have the first chance to form a government — most logically Mr. Eisenkot, as he has received the most endorsements thanks to support from Israeli-Arabs.
Yair Golan, Israel's main left-wing leader and part of the Opposition bloc, said "serious work" was underway to form a coalition.
"I'm more optimistic than I was on the Wednesday (November 4, 2026) morning after the election results. There is progress. There is a will," he said.

Ultra-Orthodox Jews' exemption from military service has fuelled widespread resentment among other Israelis, with reservists serving multiple tours in the wars Israel has been fighting since the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas.

articles.title: FBI arrests Thomas Markle, father of Meghan, over child sexual abuse material

fullParagraphs: Meghan Markle recently said she was “deeply distressed” by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her father's former home

Thomas Markle, the father of Prince Harry's wife Meghan, was arrested on Friday morning (November 6, 2026) by federal agents in Florida on charges related to child sexual abuse material, people familiar with the matter told The Associated Press.
The people who confirmed his arrest were not authorised to publicly discuss the investigation and spoke on the condition of anonymity. Thomas Markle was taken into custody near Tampa.

Meghan Markle recently said she was “deeply distressed” by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her father's former home. She also revealed that a letter containing “troubling allegations” about him had been sent to London police in 2018.
Meghan, an American citizen who starred in the U.S. television drama Suits , married Harry at Windsor Castle in 2018. They have two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet.

Her father, a retired television lighting and photography director, did not attend the wedding, prompting extensive coverage in the British media of Meghan's estrangement from her father. Meghan said she decided to distance herself from him to protect her children.

articles.title: Two USCIRF officials claim vigilante attacks on gurdwaras in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: India describes U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom as a biased organisation that lacks credibility

Two officials of an American advisory body on religious freedom have claimed that Sikh gurdwaras in India have been targeted with vigilante attacks and urged the U.S. government to press New Delhi to hold perpetrators of such violence accountable.

"Over the last several weeks, Sikh gurdwaras in India have been targeted with vigilante attacks, including attempts to harm religious leaders,” U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) Commissioner David Anderson said in a social media post without elaborating.
ALSO WATCH Sukhbir Singh Badal injured in knife attack inside Nanded gurdwara
Mr. Anderson said the U.S. should link security assistance to the Indian government's response to violence that stops people from exercising freedom of religious belief (FoRB).

Another USCIRF Commissioner, Joe Grogan, said attacks on houses of worship in India, including churches, gurdwaras, and mosques, undermine FoRB rights enshrined in international law. “The US government should continue to press the Indian government to hold perpetrators of such violence accountable & protect places of worship,” he said.
India describes USCIRF as a biased organisation that lacks credibility.
Established by the U.S. government in 1998 after the inaction of the International Religious Freedom Act, the recommendations of USCIRF are non-binding on the U.S. State Department.

articles.title: Airstrikes on market in southwestern Yemen kill at least 30, Houthis say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson, Anees Alsabahi, told Houthi-run TV Al Masirah that 15 people were also wounded in the airstrikes on the market in al-Waziyah in the province of Taiz
Yemen’s Houthis said the toll from an airstrike on a market in Taiz province, southwestern Yemen, on Friday (November 6, 2026) increased to 30 dead, as the warring sides traded blame for the attack.

“Saudi enemy aircraft targeted the Hadara market in Waziyah district, resulting in 30 deaths and eight injuries,” the Houthis’ Health Ministry said in a statement carried by the group’s Saba news agency, updating an earlier toll.
It would be one of the deadliest attacks since fighting resumed between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces.
A Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson, Anees Alsabahi, told Houthi-run TV Al Masirah that 15 people were also wounded in the airstrikes on the market in al-Waziyah in the province of Taiz.
He said that the death toll was expected to rise from the airstrikes, which he blamed on the Saudi-led coalition.

Local authorities in Taiz acknowledged that an attack on a busy market killed and wounded people, without providing details on the actual toll. But the authorities in Taiz blamed the Houthis for the incident. They said that no airstrikes were carried out in the area.
The Associated Press couldn't immediately independently verify the claims of responsibility.

Yemen’s Houthis said the toll from an airstrike on a market in Taiz province, southwestern Yemen, on Friday (November 6, 2026) increased to 30 dead, as the warring sides traded blame for the attack.

“Saudi enemy aircraft targeted the Hadara market in Waziyah district, resulting in 30 deaths and eight injuries,” the Houthis’ Health Ministry said in a statement carried by the group’s Saba news agency, updating an earlier toll.

It would be one of the deadliest attacks since fighting resumed between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces.

A Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson, Anees Alsabahi, told Houthi-run TV Al Masirah that 15 people were also wounded in the airstrikes on the market in al-Waziyah in the province of Taiz.

He said that the death toll was expected to rise from the airstrikes, which he blamed on the Saudi-led coalition.

Local authorities in Taiz acknowledged that an attack on a busy market killed and wounded people, without providing details on the actual toll. But the authorities in Taiz blamed the Houthis for the incident. They said that no airstrikes were carried out in the area.

The Associated Press couldn't immediately independently verify the claims of responsibility.

articles.title: Helping hand: On Cyclones Arnab and Murasu
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: States need help to rebuild public infrastructure after damage in cyclones

Long-term preparedness and a swift response by authorities minimised casualties when the back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu hit two places of the Andhra Pradesh coast. In Andhra Pradesh, damage from Cyclone Arnab , which made landfall on October 28 was estimated at roughly ₹4,526 crore. Initial estimates of the damage by Cyclone Murasu, which crossed the coast on November 3, indicate that about 52,500 hectares of standing crops were affected. The State reported seven deaths from the two cyclones. The first cyclone damaged nearly 90,000 hectares of standing crops in southern parts of Odisha. After preliminary on-the-spot assessment of flood-hit areas, the Union government is expected to soon release the first instalment of funds to the affected States. Personnel from Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu have also gone to the rescue of Andhra Pradesh.

The deployment of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) and other technologies has significantly reduced human casualties and property damage. During Cyclone Hudhud in October 2014, Andhra Pradesh reported 63 deaths and damage estimated at nearly ₹22,000 crore. As natural disasters become more frequent in India, greater collaboration is needed between higher learning institutions, especially in science and technology, and central and State government agencies. Authorities must develop an effective compensation framework for saving crops/crop losses. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, a crop insurance scheme that was launched by the Union government a decade ago, has not provided farmers with comprehensive safety cover, as they suffer due to the vagaries of nature. The Union government should improve the scheme so that all farmers are encouraged to bring their crops under the scheme, while State governments should raise awareness about the insurance scheme and support agriculturists by topping up benefits that are under the insurance cover. The Centre should also focus on financial assistance for permanent restoration projects. The initial stand of the Union government was that the National and State Disaster Response Funds were meant for response and relief, not recovery and reconstruction, but following the 15th Finance Commission’s nudge, it added recovery and reconstruction as a component of the two funds two years ago. However, when public infrastructure suffers extensive damage, the Centre should provide additional assistance to ease the burden on affected States. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his team at the Centre must act in the spirit of “cooperative federalism”.

articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities

Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.title: Two 17-year-old students sexually assaulted at party, two booked under PoCSO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two 17-year-old girl students were allegedly sexually assaulted after being made to consume alcohol at a party in Balanagar on the night of October 1. Police have registered a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act against two youths in connection with the incident.

The suspects have been identified as Ganesh alias Ghana, 19, and Tarun, 26, who is married. Ganesh was in a relationship with one of the victims and had invited her to the party. She took a friend along with her.

According to Madhura Nagar police Inspector H. Prabhakar, after taking the two students to the venue, the youths allegedly made them consume alcohol before sexually assaulting them. “The students had consumed one beer each. One of the victims later fell unwell and was taken to a hospital, where suspicion arose of a possible sexual assault,” said the officer, adding that when questioned, the students disclosed what had happened. Their statements were subsequently recorded at a Bharosa Centre.

The students were admitted to a hospital in Madhuranagar following the incident. They later approached the Madhuranagar police and lodged a complaint, based on which a case was registered and an investigation taken up.

articles.title: Karnataka will integrate all its skilling efforts into a single unified system: CM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: To reshape State’s workforce pipeline, government will allocate ₹5,000 crore to streamline its fragmented skilling initiatives spread across various departments and entities and also train 30 lakh beneficiaries over the next seven years

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has announced a plan to integrate the State’s fragmented skilling efforts into a single unified system, budgeting an estimated investment of ₹5,000 crore to train 30 lakh beneficiaries over the next seven years.

Speaking at the Bengaluru Skill Summit on Wednesday, the Chief Minister also revealed the formation of a new State Vision Group for skill development, chaired by Mindtree co-founder Subroto Bagchi, to fundamentally reshape the state’s workforce pipeline to meet future demands.

The policy shift comes at a time when Karnataka, which produces over one lakh engineering graduates every year, has several of them facing underemployment or accepting entry-level positions with low salaries. With over 550 Global Capability Centres (GCCs) currently operating in Bengaluru and an additional 500 targeted by 2029, the government is rushing to upgrade its vocational training ecosystem before an estimated 3.5 lakh upcoming jobs are introduced to the market.

Mr. Shivakumar stressed that traditional degrees were no longer the primary benchmark for corporate recruitment, drawing parallels to international markets where practical capability out-values formal certification.

The newly formed Vision Group would oversee the implementation of specialised training programmes across highly technical emerging sectors, including artificial intelligence, green energy, advanced manufacturing, and digital services. The initiative was aimed at capitalising on the State’s distinct demographic dividend, where 65% of the total population was under the age of 35, he added.

The summit witnessed the signing of more than 40 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) involving local Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), which officials claim would immediately secure over 10,000 jobs for regional youth, anchoring the expanded training regime under the Koushalya Karnataka Yojane framework.

Mr. Shivakumar launched Udyoga Sethu, a digital employment platform by the State government at the Bengaluru Skill Summit to connect skilled talent with employment opportunities available with various enterprises.

Yuva Udyoga Setu is an AI-powered, unified skill development and employment portal and it serves as a direct bridge connecting local job seekers with verified private-sector employers. The platform, which operates under the Karnataka Skill Development Corporation (KSDC) and the Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood, will offer seamless job matching (connects job seekers with corporate employers).

Enterprises can register and post their openings on the portal completely free of charge. It also claims to offer access to targeted training programs like the Chief Minister’s Kaushalya Karnataka Yojane (CMKKY) and specialised training for diverse segments (including Nal Jal Mitra and training for prison inmates).

articles.title: Visvesvaraya Technological University decides to introduce on-demand examinations for candidates who failed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With the introduction of the on-demand examination system, students will no longer have to wait for the university to announce the supplementary examination schedule

To avoid the loss of an academic year for students who could not attend the scheduled semester examinations in any subject or who failed in one or more subjects, the Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU) has decided to conduct “on-demand examinations”.

With the introduction of the on-demand examination system, students will no longer have to wait for the university to announce the supplementary examination schedule. The university will be ready to conduct examinations at a time convenient to students, based on their requests, even for a single student. Students can even request to write examinations on public holidays.

Speaking to The Hindu , S. Vidyashankar, Vice-Chancellor, VTU, said, “With the intention of providing greater convenience to students, we have decided to introduce on-demand examinations. We have also made all the necessary preparations for this initiative. Even if a single student wishes to appear for an examination, we will conduct it for them.”
VTU has decided to announce the results within 24 hours of the examination for students appearing for these on-demand examinations.

VTU has instructed all affiliated engineering colleges under its jurisdiction to inform students about this opportunity. Details regarding eligibility, examination schedules, and the application process will be announced shortly.

Among the public universities in the State, VTU is the first to take up such an initiative. There are 220 engineering colleges under VTU’s jurisdiction, with around three lakh students currently pursuing their studies. Approximately 70,000 students secure admission every year. On average, around 20% of students fail in one or more subjects in each semester examination. Earlier, such students had to wait for six to seven months to reappear for their examinations.

VTU will use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to prepare question papers. There is already a bank of 500-600 question papers for each subject. The university has also made the necessary arrangements and deployed the required staff to conduct these examinations.

articles.title: Police Inspector awarded two-month imprisonment in contempt case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana High Court awarded two-month imprisonment to a police officer of the rank of Inspector, holding him guilty in a contempt of court case.

Justice C.V. Bhaskar Reddy of the HC also imposed a fine of ₹ 2,000 on Inspector M. Prem Kumar. The sentence, however, was suspended for two weeks providing an opportunity to the Inspector for an appeal. The contempt case was filed by A. Sekhar Babu and seven others contending that the Inspector failed to provide aid to protect their plots despite specific orders from the HC - passed in 2023.

The petitioners, majority of them senior citizens, stated that despite a specific direction from a single judge of the HC to provide protection to them from illegal interference by three persons (who were made respondents in the writ petition), the then Station House Officer Prem Kumar failed to act. The Inspector contended that he had no knowledge of the earlier order of the HC in the matter. “However, the absence of prior knowledge of the an order cannot justify inaction. It was incumbent upon him to examine the order and take appropriate steps in accordance with law to ensure its implementation,” the judge noted.

articles.title: After a decade, Chikkajala Fort near Bengaluru to get a new lease of life using CSR funds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In 2016, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), which implemented the road widening project of NH 44, demolished the northern side of the fort

A decade after a part of it was demolished to make way for road works, the Chikkajala Fort, which is 25 km away from Bengaluru city and on the way to Kempegowda International Airport (KIA), will soon be restored using Corporate Social Responsbility (CSR) funds from a private organisation.

A ceremony was recently held at the fort to mark the beginning of the project, with Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda in attendance, along with members of Intach and Kashi Ra, the organisation funding the project.

The fort includes a small Anjaneya Swamy Temple, where a daily puja is performed by a local priest, and kalyani and stone mantapas on two acres under survey number 116, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Revenue Department. These were built in the 19th century, inspired by the Vijayanagara style, and used as a ‘chatra’ or rest stops for soldiers, businesspersons, and others professions who travelled long distances. The stones in the kalyani and mantapa feature carvings of nagabhanda , elephant, shivalinga , purnakumba and anjaneya , fishes, birds and a few others, said a senior official from the Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage.

When The Hindu visited Chikkajala Fort, huge trees and bushes had grown inside the mantapa. The branches and roots had spread across the roof and flooring of the mantapa while the stones of the kalyani and Anjaneya Temple are intact. However, there is no water in the kalyani, which has remained dry for a long time.
The branches and roots are spread across the roof and flooring of the mantapa. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

In 2016, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), which implemented the road widening project of NH 44, demolished the northern side (entrance) of the fort, which The Hindu had reported about then. The fort, which was circular in shape before the demolition, is now semi-circular and opens to the road.

Meera Iyer, convener of the Bengaluru Chapter, Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH), said, “The villagers informed us that the bottom of the kalyani was cemented during a film shoot by the film team. Hence, there is no water in it. However, many trees have grown around and spread their roots in the mantapa. INTACH is yet to start its documentation and study on how to retain these trees and restore the stones of the mantapa. In our earlier projects, the trees were retained and walls were restored with the help of experts. After documentation, a Detailed Project Report (DPR) will be prepared, along with the calculation of the total cost it will incur.”

She added that once the fort is restored, it will be a tourist place for those visiting Bengaluru, and cultural activities are likely to be organised so that more people know the history and importance of the monument. “We are also planning to involve college students studying architecture and provide them with a first-hand experience working on live restoration projects like this fort,” she said.

articles.title: U.S. midterm elections 2026 LIVE: Trump says 'largely true' Iran war caused election loss
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Democrats won full control of the U.S. Congress in a sweeping midterm rout with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party

Canada’s push to reduce economic dependence on the United States will not change after President Donald Trump’s Republican Party suffered a crushing midterm election defeat, an official said Wednesday.

Prime Minister Mark Carney has maintained that trade with the United States, a cornerstone of the Canadian economy, will not return to a pre-Trump normal and that his country must urgently diversify its trading relationships.
U.S. Democratic Party leaders have been critical of Mr. Trump’s trade war with Canada and called for the reversal of sweeping tariffs that have impacted businesses on both sides of the border.
But the Canadian Minister responsible for US-Canada trade, Dominic LeBlanc, stressed Wednesday that Ottawa’s focus on repositioning the economy “hasn’t changed.”
President Donald Trump said on Wednesday the ‌Iran war has been worth it despite acknowledging its role ⁠in losses in U.S. midterm elections in which his Republican party lost control ‌of Congress.
“The Iran thing we had to do, and ‌we continue to do it,” ‌he told ⁠reporters.
Trump defends Iran war, blames GOP losses on not “transferring the love” to candidates amid midterm fallout.
US President Donald Trump said Wednesday that if the Democrats were to launch an effort to impeach him when they take control of Congress next year, it would “destroy” their party.

Asked about prospective impeachment a day after his Republican Party suffered a sweeping midterm election loss, Mr. Trump said: “I think it would destroy the Democrat Party if they did that,” insisting there was “no reason” for him to be impeached.

U.S. President Donald Trump concedes that the war he ordered on Iran was partly to blame for his Republican Party’s sweeping midterms losses -- but even as he comes under pressure, analysts said Wednesday that he has few good options ahead.
It remains to be seen what path Trump will take after emerging politically weakened as Democrats seized control of both the Senate and House of Representatives in Tuesday’s vote.

The U.S. leader also remains caught between a desire to diplomatically end the war with Iran -- which has sharply driven up gasoline costs for American voters -- and his threats to “finish it off” with Tehran.

articles.title: What the BRICS carbon market partnership needs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: BRICS can turn fragmented carbon markets into a coordinated trading framework

On September 12, at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the New Delhi Declaration confirmed that BRICS members look forward to implementing the Memorandum of Understanding on the BRICS Carbon Markets Partnership. The commitment remains modest: on capacity-building and experience-sharing, with no trading framework, targets or timeline. The Rio summit acknowledged the memorandum in 2025, and New Delhi has reiterated it. With India’s BRICS presidency entering its final quarter, operationalising the partnership requires not so much a common trading platform as a common rulebook.

Eight BRICS members reportedly operate voluntary markets, and Brazil, China, India and Indonesia host over a third of the carbon credit projects registered worldwide. Compliance systems are maturing, too. China’s emissions trading system (ETS) — added steel, cement and aluminium through its 2024-25 allocation plan. India’s Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) has notified emission-intensity targets for 490 entities across nine sectors and opened an offset mechanism. Brazil’s Law of 2024 establishes the Brazilian Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading System (SBCE), a cap-and-trade system. However, none of these markets is linked to another.

articles.title: Vance tries to distance himself from Iran war after Republican Party’s deep losses in midterm elections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: J.D. Vance, who has said he would decide after the election whether to run for President in 2028, issued a lengthy social media post blaming the unpopular conflict with Iran for the Grand Old Party’s drubbing

J.D. Vance publicly broke from President Donald Trump's defence of the Iran war on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) after the Republican Party's deep losses in the midterm elections, attempting to distance himself from voters' clear rebuke of the President as the Vice President faces questions about his own political ambitions.

Mr. Vance, who has said he would decide after the election whether to run for President in 2028, issued a lengthy social media post blaming the unpopular conflict with Iran for the GOP's (Grand Old Party) drubbing. Mr. Vance said, "If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so.”

But arguing that the war was worth it is what Mr. Trump repeatedly did on the campaign trail and continued to do in interviews as election results came in. Mr. Trump told The New York Times late Tuesday that the decision to go to war this year was “very wise" and told Politico it was “an absolutely correct one.”
The White House did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) about the Vice President's post.

The Republican, who had long advocated for restraint in U.S. military intervention overseas, was lukewarm in his defence of the conflict after Mr. Trump launched it and even became the face of an unsuccessful attempt to end the fighting.

About six in 10 voters said the U.S. made the “wrong decision” in taking military action against Iran, according to the AP Voter Poll, a survey of more than 1,00,000 voters in the United States. Most of those voters dissatisfied with the Iran war backed the Democratic candidate in their U.S. House race, but the survey suggested the Iran war was not the leading issue for most voters.
Only about one-third of voters said the war in Iran was “crucial” to their vote for Congress, well below the roughly half who said that about the cost of living or government corruption.

Nearly all voters who backed the Democratic candidate in their U.S. House race said going to war with Iran was the “wrong decision,” while roughly eight in 10 voters who backed the Republican candidate said it was the “right decision.”

A former Marine who served in Iraq, Mr. Vance had been critical of that conflict and said after becoming Vice President that a Trump administration would not send troops into the “open-ended conflicts” of the past.

After Mr. Trump launched the war with Iran this past spring, Mr. Vance was noticeably quiet in speaking about it, a conspicuous change for a politician known for being a pugnacious defender of the President.
This summer, he tried to argue the conflict was worth it, telling conservative podcast host Megyn Kelly in an interview that, “If we transformed the Middle East, this is fundamentally worth it."

But after Democrats swept control of both the House and the Senate on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), defeating GOP candidates even in deep-red areas that Mr. Trump carried by wide margins two years ago, Mr. Vance said in his post that “the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone."

articles.title: Science should move past ‘top 2%’ label
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: India needs both fundamental research and practical solutions without making inclusion in the ‘top 2% scientists’ database’ the primary goal

Indian scientists, like scientists everywhere, deserve recognition for the work they do in advancing knowledge. International visibility is one such form of recognition. Recent media reports stated that India’s presence in the “ top 2% scientists’ database ” is on the rise. Irrespective of whether Indian scientists are included in these lists or not, many of them make important research contributions. Their work must be recognised on its own merits. However, it becomes a concern when inclusion in a database becomes a target or when exclusion is mistaken for lack of worth.

John Loannidis and his collaborators, the creators of the “top 2% scientists’ database”, have cautioned against treating inclusion in the database as conclusive evidence of research excellence. First, the database relies on publication and citation records from Scopus without checking for their originality. Second, the accuracy of author profiles and classification of disciplines affect the results. Third, it does not consider contributions published in regional languages.

articles.title: Government proposes immediate suspension of manufacturing licences of substandard drugs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Proposed amendment provides for mandatory corrective measures before revocation of the suspension; suspension shall continue until the manufacturer undertakes corrective action

The Union Health Ministry has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to immediately suspend the manufacturing licences of drugs declared Not of Standard Quality (NSQ) on specified critical quality parameters.

The government said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that the proposed amendments seek to enable prompt regulatory intervention upon detection of substandard medicines, prevent their continued manufacture and distribution, and strengthen the mechanism for ensuring compliance with prescribed quality standards, in the interest of patient safety and public health.

Under the existing provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945, suspension or cancellation of a manufacturing licence is preceded by the prescribed regulatory procedure, including issuance of a show-cause notice. This may result in a time gap between the declaration of a drug as NSQ and the initiation of regulatory action. During this period, the drug may remain in circulation, posing potential risks to public health and making effective recall more challenging.

To address this regulatory concern, the Ministry has proposed a provision for immediate suspension of the manufacturing licence of the drug by the Central Licensing Approving Authority or the State Licensing Authority upon receipt of a government analyst’s report declaring the drug as NSQ with respect to assay, dissolution, related substances, impurities or sterility.

“These parameters are critical to determining the quality of medicines. The proposed provision aims to ensure that instances of non-compliance involving these specified parameters are met with prompt regulatory action, thereby minimising potential risks to patients,’’ the Ministry said.

The proposed amendment provides for mandatory corrective measures before revocation of the suspension. The suspension shall continue until the manufacturer undertakes an effective root cause analysis to identify the reasons for the quality failure and implements appropriate Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) to the satisfaction of the licensing authority.

Suspension can be revoked after the requisite corrective and preventive measures are implemented and then verified by the licensing authority. This mechanism will ensure that identified quality deficiencies are adequately addressed and necessary safeguards are put in place to prevent their recurrence.

“To further strengthen regulatory coordination and facilitate timely action, consequential amendments have also been proposed to Form 13, relating to the test report of the Government Analyst. Under the proposed mechanism, the Government Analyst’s report would be endorsed to the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI), the concerned State/UT Licensing Authority under whose jurisdiction the manufacturing site is located, as well as the manufacturer and marketer of the concerned drug,’’ the government said.

It added that the proposed arrangement is aimed at ensuring timely communication of NSQ findings to the relevant authorities and stakeholders, thereby facilitating coordinated regulatory action and strengthening accountability across the drug manufacturing and marketing chain.

The proposed amendments follow deliberations at the 65th meeting of the Drugs Consultative Committee, held on December 20, 2024, and recommendations of the 92nd meeting of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board, held on April 24, 2025.

The amendments are expected to strengthen post-marketing regulatory surveillance, facilitate timely action against substandard medicines, promote greater accountability among manufacturers and marketers, and reinforce public confidence in the quality of medicines available in the country.

The draft amendments have been notified for public consultation, inviting objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public within 30 days from the date on which copies of the Gazette of India containing the draft rules are made available to the public.

articles.title: Celebrations among NDA alliance leaders after landslide victory
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Celebrations broke out among NDA alliance leaders and workers in Vijayawada following the alliance’s emphatic victory in the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation elections.

MP Kesineni Sivanath, East MLA Gadde Ramamohan, NTR district parliamentary constituency in-charge M. Mallikarjuna Rao, BJP NTR district president Gadde Anuradha and others participated in the programme. They felicitated the newly-elected Mayor Vangaveeti Radha Krishna on Wednesday.

Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Sivanath pointed out that people have demonstrated their confidence in the NDA alliance through the election results. Despite the relatively low voter turnout, people had given the alliance such a decisive mandate, he said.
The MP said the victory had placed greater responsibility on the alliance and assured that they would live up to people’s expectations by developing Vijayawada in all sectors.
The MP said the delay in finalising seat-sharing arrangements within the alliance and certain other factors had cost them victory in another three to four divisions.
He said they were always willing to consider constructive suggestions from anyone, including former IPS officer A.B. Venkateswara Rao, if they were beneficial to the people and the party.

Later, Mr. Radha Krishna expressed his gratitude to Jana Sena Party president and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan for giving him the opportunity to serve as Mayor and to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu for encouraging him. He also thanked the people of Vijayawada for their confidence in him.

They expressed confidence that the city would be transformed into a developed urban centre by prioritising infrastructure, sanitation, drinking water supply, roads and the resolution of public grievances, in line with the hopes and aspirations of Vijayawada residents.

articles.title: Kochi police yet to complete verification of private bus employees
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police launched the background verification drive following a series of incidents of criminal behaviour involving private bus crew

The Kochi City police’s special drive to conduct background verification of private bus employees and issue them special identity cards is yet to be completed, even two months after the initiative was launched.

The police, according to sources, are planning to issue the ID cards by next week, though they admitted that a final decision on how to proceed with the drive was yet to be taken. Earlier, the police had planned to complete the process within a few weeks in September and then by the end of October, but the initial plan could not be implemented.

An officer involved in the process said the verification of over 1,500 employees, including drivers and conductors, had been completed. It is roughly estimated that around 2,000 employees work as bus crew in the city.

Bus employees were asked to submit their personal details to the police in a pro forma for verification. The police launched the background verification drive in response to a series of incidents involving alleged criminal behaviour by private bus employees in recent times. The Special Branch of the police is conducting the verification based on the applications received by the traffic wing.

Sources said the police were planning to introduce smart ID cards for the bus crew, though the details of the cards were yet to be finalised. However, the police are yet to decide whether the cards should be issued to all employees who undergo verification, the officer said.

“We have come across employees who were booked for minor offences, including drunk driving, during the verification. For those who have a criminal background, we will note adverse remarks. Once the verification is completed, it would be up to the bus operator to decide whether a person should be employed or not,” the officer said.
District Police Chief (Kochi City) R. Nishanthini is yet to review the project, which was initiated by her predecessor, Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar, sources said.

articles.title: Direct T.N. DGP to frame guidelines regarding registration of criminal cases for social media posts, political criticism and online speech, insists a PIL plea before Madras High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Litigant says the Telangana High Court had framed a set of guidelines last year for the police in the neighbouring State and that Tamil Nadu could take a cue from that judgment

A public interest litigation petition has been filed before the Madras High Court seeking a direction to the Director General of Police/Head of Police Force (DGP/HoPF) to frame uniform guidelines to be followed by the police personnel across the State while dealing with complaints regarding social media posts, political criticism, satire and online speech.

The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan is expected to hear the plea filed by Chennai-based advocate H. Syed Alim. The petitioner had sought a direction to the DGP/HoPF to frame the guidelines on the basis of a representation made by him on August 20, 2026 and circulate them to all the police divisions and wings.

He said, the need for the case had arisen because of increasing number of criminal cases booked against political commentators, activists and social media users for criticism, satire, political opinion and democratic dissent expressed through online platforms. He said, in several instances, police had entertained the complaints mechanically without examining whether the speech was protected under Article 19(1) of the Constitution.

Referring to the cases booked against DMK Vilathikulam MLA G.V. Markandayan, the party’s Gen Z wing leader A. Anbanantham and the party sympathiser Vinoth Suryakumar, the PIL petitioner said, all these instances call for the laying down of guidelines to be followed by the police while dealing with complaints against the democratic right to free speech.

He said, the Telangana High Court had on September 10, 2025 laid down eight guidelines to be followed by the police to prevent misuse of criminal law in matters concerning political speech and social media posts. The guidelines included verification of the locus standi of the complainants, conduct of preliminary inquiry in cognisable offences and applying a high threshold for social media posts and public speech-related offences.

The Telangana High Court had cautioned the police against mechanical registration of criminal cases in matters concerning harsh, offensive, or critical political speeches. Since defamation was a non cognisable offence, the court had said, the police could not directly register FIRs in such matters without a judicial magistrate’s order. It had also warned the police against automatic arrests and insisted upon closing frivolous/motivated complaints.

Though the State of Telangana took the matter on appeal, the Supreme Court had refused to interfere with the guidelines on February 2, 2026. Therefore, the Tamil Nadu DGP/HoPF could also frame similar guidelines by taking a cue from the Telangana High Court verdict, the petitioner said.

articles.title: Anaemia burden — iron alone is no solution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: India must tackle its anaemia burden through targeted nutrition, better diagnostics and comprehensive public health measures, not salt fortification alone

India’s anaemia burden is not in doubt. The fifth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5 ) found that more than half of women and about two-thirds of young children are anaemic. In this context, double-fortified salt (DFS) — fortified with iodine and iron — is often proposed as a potentially transformative solution. However, the case for DFS rests on convenience: everyone consumes salt, so why not add iron to it? But convenience is not efficacy, and a policy that asks the country to continue consuming salt to deliver iron deserves closer scrutiny.

Iron fortification of salt is a vehicle that cuts against public health. Indians consume, by most estimates, roughly twice the five grams of salt a day recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO). About one in three adults has hypertension, and India’s own non-communicable disease (NCD) action plan commits to a 30% relative reduction in salt intake.

articles.title: Recruitment for more than 11,000 posts in Bihar’s health department to begin soon
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Currently, updated details of vacant positions have been sought from all 38 districts of the state. All recruitments will be conducted at the State Health Society level
Bihar’s Health department is all set to begin the process to fill more than 11,000 administrative, technical and medical support positions.

Sharing the information, State Health Society Executive Director Nawal Kishore Chaudhary on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) said the official recruitment notification for this massive hiring drive is expected to be issued by the last week of this month.
Preparations for the recruitment process are almost complete, he said adding that a recruitment calendar will also be released shortly.

Currently, updated details of vacant positions have been sought from all 38 districts of the State. The information is being gathered from district-level health institutions, Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community Health Centres (CHCs) and Sub-Divisional Hospitals.

According to the Executive Director, recruitment will be carried out for several positions, including Staff Nurses, Laboratory Technicians, managerial-category posts, Block Health Managers (BHM), NME personnel at the block level, and clerical staff.
The recruitment for several other vacant positions will be undertaken in the second phase.
Mr. Chaudhary, added that the completion of the first phase of recruitment for more than 11,000 posts will undoubtedly bring significant and positive changes to Bihar’s healthcare sector.

“Dedicated teams will be made available at the block and panchayat levels to support doctors and paramedical staff, thereby improving the quality of primary healthcare services in remote areas especially in rural areas. The number of healthcare workers in district and sub-divisional hospitals will be better aligned with patient loads, reducing the excessive workload on existing employees, “Mr. Chaudhary said.

He pointed out that an adequate number of laboratory technicians and nurses will ensure that patients receive timely diagnostic reports and quality healthcare services. He mentioned that the appointment of Block Health Managers and clerical staff will also help ensure that government healthcare schemes reach the general public more efficiently and in, transparent and quick manner.
Mr. Chaudhary further stated that the recruitment calendar has almost been finalised and will be made public as soon as it gets approval from the authorities concerned.

The department’s primary objective is to complete the entire recruitment process- including selection, document verification and distribution of appointment letters- in a transparent manner within 6 to 7 months from the date of the issuance of the official notification, he added.

articles.title: More than 43 lakh pucca houses completed in Bihar for poor families
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ₹56,743.40 crore spent under PMAY-G so far in the State; of the 43 lakh houses, 36.63 lakh pucca houses built in just yearrs between FY 2016-17 & 2021-22
Under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin) schem, a total of 43,14,959 poor families in the state have so far completed the construction of their pucca houses.

According to figures released by the Rural Development Department, approval for construction of pucca houses for 49,09,740 beneficiaries have been granted against the overall target of 49,16,649 houses set from the financial year 2016-17 onwards.
The Bihar government has spent a total of ₹56,743.40 crore so far on the implementation of this scheme to provide houses equipped with basic amenities.

PMAY-G, which is a Union Ministry of Rural Development’s flagship scheme, aims to provide a pucca house with basic amenities to all houseless households and those living in kutcha or dilapidated houses.
According to the Rural Development Department’s officials, the implementation of the scheme in the State has been accelerated by dividing it primarily into two phases.

In the first phase, a target was set to construct 37,01,138 houses during the financial years 2016-17 to 2021-22. Against this target, the department promptly approved housing assistance for 37,00,531 beneficiaries, of which construction of 36,63,701 houses has been completed.

All three instalments of financial assistance were released to beneficiaries on time during the first phase. A target of constructing 12,15,511 houses has been set under the second phase, covering the financial years 2024-25 and 2025-26. So far, housing approvals have been granted to 12,09,209 beneficiaries.
The first instalment has been paid to 11,70,945 beneficiaries, while the second instalment paid to 10,21,366 beneficiaries, and the third instalment paid to 7,13,329 beneficiaries.

As a result, 6,51,258 beneficiaries have also completed the construction of their pucca houses under the second phase. A total of 43,14,959 beneficiaries’ houses have been completed in the first and second phases. A total of 36,63,701 beneficiaries’ houses have been completed in the first phase while 6,51,258 beneficiaries’ houses have been completed in the second phase.
With financial assistance of ₹1.20 lakh per beneficiary, these pucca houses are providing shelter to homeless families.

“The government is fully committed to ensuring that the benefits of development reach the most disadvantaged sections of society in rural areas. Poor and vulnerable families are not only receiving shelter but also an opportunity to live with dignity through the PMAY-Gramin,” the Rural Development Department and Information & Public Relations Department Minister Shravan Kumar said.

The department is ensuring the construction of approved houses with complete transparency and efficiency, Mr. Kumar said, adding that payments of instalments are being transferred directly into the bank accounts of beneficiaries on time so that there are no obstacles in the construction process.

articles.title: Explosion damages railway track in northern Rajasthan district
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

A powerful explosion damaged the Anupgarh-Suratgarh railway track in northern Rajasthan ’s Sriganganagar district on Tuesday night (November 3, 2026), prompting a multi-agency investigation into a suspected attempt at train sabotage. A passenger train had passed through the stretch barely 45 minutes before the incident.

The blast, which occurred near 50 GB village, shattered two concrete railway sleepers beneath the tracks, dislodged the track clips and created a two-foot-deep crater at the site. The North-Western Railway cancelled four train services on the route on Wednesday as a precautionary measure.

Villagers living about 200 metres away from the spot heard the explosion and informed the police. While the forensic experts collected samples from the site, the security agencies were examining the vital aspects of intensity of the explosion and nature of the explosive substances used.

Sriganganagar Superintendent of Police Harishankar Yadav said the teams from the National Investigation Agency (NIA) and Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) had arrived to join the probe. “The district police are carrying out the investigation. The exact nature of the explosion will be determined after the forensic report is received,” Mr. Yadav said.
