articles.title: U.P. to match Assembly voter lists with Panchayat and Urban local body rolls to find missing voters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: U.P. CEO office said that guidelines have been sent to all District Election Officers (DEOs), who have been told to carry out the matching thoroughly

Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh has directed that voter lists of all Assembly constituencies of the State be matched with Panchayat and Urban Body electoral rolls in order to find eligible citizens missing from the rolls during the Special Summary Revision of Voter Lists 2027.

In an official statement on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), the U.P. CEO office said that guidelines have been sent to all District Election Officers (DEOs), who have been told to carry out the matching thoroughly.

Directions have also been issued to Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to get Form 6 filled for every identified eligible citizen who is not on the voter list of any Assembly constituency in India.

District Electoral Officers have also been asked to use fair price shops run by the Food and Civil Supplies Department to find those left out. Citizens aged 18 years and above who are registered at fair price shops in a district but are not on the current voter list will be identified and added to the voter list if found eligible.
The officials said that every effort will be made, with the cooperation of various departments, to enrol eligible citizens, especially youth and women.

For young voters, Electoral Literacy Clubs in educational institutions are also being activated. The Assistant Electoral Registration Officer of each Assembly constituency has been asked to coordinate with the clubs’ designated coordinators and work in “mission mode”. Youth organisations such as the NSS, NCC, Nehru Yuva Kendra, Yuvak Mangal Dal and Bharat Scouts and Guides will also be roped in.
Sources said that an estimated one crore voters are likely to be added to the post-SIR voter lists based on the population estimates of the States.
The final SSR rolls in U.P. are scheduled to be published on January 4. The State is scheduled for Assembly polls early next year.

articles.title: Israel President urges compromise after divisive election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: President Isaac Herzog began meeting party leaders to decide whether to give Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or his rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government in the deeply polarised country
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) doubled down on accusations of foreign interference in last week’s election, despite calls for compromise from the President.

More than a week after Israel’s first election since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attacks, President Isaac Herzog began meeting party leaders to decide whether to give Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or his rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government in the deeply polarised country.

Mr. Eisenkot, who won the endorsement of a major Arab party, vowed to “deepen” the U.S.-Israel partnership across bipartisan lines and to work with President Donald Trump to stabilise the region if selected as Prime Minister.
Mr. Netanyahu, meanwhile, pointed to “serious suspicions that foreign states have spent considerable sums to influence the outcome of the elections in Israel”.
The premier has gone on the offensive against Arab-majority lists, who have the power to put Eisenkot in power if they team up.

Mr. Netanyahu has pointed to the arrests of several people with envelopes of cash on election day in what authorities called localised incidents, and accused leaders of accepting money from Qatar, an allegation also levelled against the Prime Minister’s own aides.

With neither bloc holding a majority in the 120-seat parliament after the October 27 vote, Mr. Herzog said both sides needed to accept that “not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled” and to avoid new elections.

“In the current reality, in which there is no clear winner after the elections, I ask for originality and creativity, courage and goodwill, so that the State of Israel emerges the winner,” Mr. Herzog said.

The election saw soaring support for lists from the Arab minority, descendants of Palestinians who stayed in Israel after its 1948 creation and who have often been outraged by the harsh rhetoric and actions of Netanyahu’s hard-right government.
Without naming any leader, Mr. Herzog, whose role is usually ceremonial, said he had “great respect” for the Arab minority, which makes up around 20% of Israel’s population.
“I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently,” he said.

Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief who has vowed to turn the page on Mr. Netanyahu’s long, divisive reign, meanwhile vowed to “renew and deepen” Israel’s partnership with the United States and “strengthen the bipartisan foundations that have long sustained it”.

articles.title: Democrats win U.S. Congress in midterm rout of U.S. President Donald Trump
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Opposition party also retained key Senate seats, while victory in Georgia’s Governor race added to mounting signs that Republicans face a difficult night

Democrats won full control of the U.S. Congress in a sweeping midterm rout on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party.
The victory handed Democrats both the House of Representatives and Senate, giving them power to block Mr. Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency.

The vote reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Mr. Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president.

Mr. Trump struck a conciliatory note despite his history of questioning election results, telling The New York Times : “I am absolutely willing to accept those results” and promising to “work with the Democrats.”
But minutes later on social media the 80-year-old signaled how he intends to deal with Democratic attempts to pass laws, posting a picture of a red baseball cap emblazoned: “VETO.”
Pia Dandiya, first-generation Indian-American, wins U.S. House of Representatives seat from Florida
Suhas Subramanyam re-elected as U.S. Congressman from Virginia
U.S. midterm election results 2026: List of key winners
The Democrats’ decisive Senate breakthroughs came in Kansas and Iowa, the fifth and sixth Republican-held seats to fall in the extraordinary “blue wave” election night.
In Kansas, Methodist Minister Adam Hamilton defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932.
Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008, again illustrating the scale of party’s inroads into Republican strongholds.
The upsets followed victories in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio, where voters rejected Republican candidates despite Trump’s intensive efforts to rally his supporters.

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed: The progressive’s progress
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Abdul El-Sayed’s describes himself as ‘just a capitalist who understands how capitalism works’ and identifies as a progressive; his candidacy was backed by leading figures such as Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez

In a country where, for more than a quarter of a century, the word “Muslim” has been used as an accusation in politics, Abdul El-Sayed’s election as the first Muslim member of the U.S. Senate breaks perhaps the thickest of glass ceilings in American public life. Dr. El-Sayed, a physician and epidemiologist, defeated the Republican former Congressman Mike Rogers with 52.5% of the vote, seven percentage points ahead of his rival.

It would be easy to dismiss this victory as merely a byproduct of the “blue wave” in the U.S. midterms, which carried Democratic candidates to wins even in Republican strongholds such as South Carolina, Texas, and Kansas. But that would be a reductive reading. The odds Dr. El-Sayed faced make the win remarkable in its own right.
Global & Diplomatic Brief: Abdul El-Sayed: The progressive’s progress. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

fullParagraphs: Court seeks affidavits on Metro curbs and alleged violations of its October 9 order

A day after mass detentions and a “curfew-like” clampdown on civil rights, which senior lawyers compared to the 1975 Emergency, the Supreme Court convened what it called an “extraordinary, exceptional” Sunday hearing to direct the Union government and the Delhi Police to stop illegal detentions and allow free and smooth movement of people and traffic, as well as the operations of Metro and rail services, but “subject to law and public order”.

A Special Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) chairperson D. Thara on a petition filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi seeking contempt action against them for allegedly violating an October 9 order which barred any “outright prohibition on the movement of Metro trains” and public transport on October 10.

The court ordered the police to forthwith review the imposition of barricades on public roads, ensure that Internet connectivity was not disturbed, and lift prohibitory orders issued under Section 163 BNSS in and around the Supreme Court and other courts of law in the capital to facilitate litigants’ access lawyers and justice.
24-hour to produce before Magistrate starts from detention, not ‘formal arrest’: Supreme Court
The court did not explicitly comment on the legality of the prohibitory orders.

Justice Bagchi, dictating the order, observed there would be no detentions except by law outside the four-km prohibitory zone in central Delhi, which includes Jantar Mantar, the designated site for protests. The court said people should be allowed to assemble peacefully outside the restricted zone. All people, including journalists and lawyers, must be allowed to perform their professional duties, the court directed.

The court’s repeated emphasis on the “subject to law and order” rider signalled a deliberate balancing act of upholding constitutional protections against illegal detention and securing rights to free movement, access to courts and Internet connectivity, while preserving the State’s power to enforce reasonable restrictions to maintain public order.

The morning began with the Bench changing courtrooms at the last moment, before 10.30 a.m., due to overcrowding. The video-conferencing link was not operational due to a “glitch” and was later found to be chock-a-block with viewers. The build-up to the hearing was punctuated by verbal confrontations over seating arrangements for senior police officers present in the courtroom. One of the lawyers, who had been detained on October 10, urged his colleagues to offer the women police officers seats, saying, “They are our guests”.

The session finally began with the entry of the two judges. Justice Bagchi, who led the Bench, responded to a word of thanks from senior advocate Kapil Sibal by assuring that the judiciary was in the service of the nation. He expressed serious concern over the “flagrant violations” committed by the police and security personnel on October 10.

Lawyers described a State crackdown that swept up thousands of people, from young students and senior citizens to professionals, journalists, and activists. The detainees were taken in police vehicles to pre-arranged centres in an operation aimed at preventing them from gathering to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The protests were sparked by the deletion of millions of registered voters across the country during the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

“Yesterday, we were one step away from a Police State. Protect the right of citizens to peacefully protest in the capital city,” senior advocate Shadan Farasat, who was dragged into a police van and detained for hours on October 10 told the court.
Senior advocate and petitioner-in-person Menaka Guruswamy asked the government how many people were detained on October 10.

articles.title: Delhi Police registers FIR over alleged circulation of child sexual abuse material on Meta platforms
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Approximately 10 links were flagged in a complaint alleging the circulation of such material, following which the police initiated an investigation to verify the allegations, says an official
The Delhi Police’s Special Cell has registered an FIR over the circulation of suspected child sexual abuse material through Meta platforms, including Facebook and Instagram.

The FIR was registered on October 8 under Sections 67 (publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form) and 67B (publishing or transmitting material depicting children in sexually explicit acts or conduct in electronic form) of the Information Technology Act, 2000.

Approximately 10 links were flagged in a complaint alleging the circulation of such material, following which the police initiated an investigation to verify the allegations, said Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) Additional CP Sanjay Bhatia.

“Acting on our directions, Delhi Police has registered an FIR regarding the availability of Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) on platforms operated by @MetaIndia,” NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo said in a post on X.
The Special Cell is investigating the matter, police said.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: Heavy rains wreak havoc in Aswaropet, Dammapeta and other mandals of Bhadradri Kothagudem
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Heavy rains triggered by Cyclone Murasu wreaked havoc in Aswaraopet, Dammapeta and several other mandals of Bhadradri Kothagudem district on Wednesday, inundating vast stretches of agricultural land and disrupting vehicular movement on several roads.

According to sources, the temporary ring bund of the Peddavagu medium irrigation project in Aswaraopet mandal reportedly suffered a breach, resulting in the inundation of agricultural fields in nearby villages.
Ponds and streams across the mandal swelled following overnight heavy downpour, causing waterlogging in low-lying areas of Aswaraopet, Naramvarigudem and other places.
Nemalipeta colony in Dammapeta was also inundated with rainwater, causing severe inconvenience to residents.
Vehicular movement on the Palvancha-Dammapeta road came to a standstill after a diversion road near Rajupeta in Mulakalapalli mandal was washed away by floodwaters on Wednesday morning.
Standing paddy and cotton crops , besides harvested produce were reportedly damaged by the heavy rains across several parts of the erstwhile undivided Khammam district, dealing a blow to farmers.
Local holidays were declared for schools in some mandals on Wednesday in view of the heavy rainfall triggered by Cyclone Murasu.

articles.title: Threat emails to Ayushmann Khurrana, Tusshar Kapoor: Mumbai Crime branch arrests techie from Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The accused had allegedly been threatening several film personalities in Mumbai through different means over the past few days

The Mumbai Crime Branch has arrested a 30-year-old IT engineer from Bengaluru for allegedly making threatening calls and sending emails to several people in Mumbai, including Bollywood actors Ayushmann Khurrana and Tusshar Kapoor. The arrest was reported on November 4.

The accused, identified as Vaibhav Mishra, was traced to Bengaluru after police tracked the IP address allegedly used to send the threatening emails. He is scheduled to be produced before a court on November 5.

According to police sources, Mr. Mishra had allegedly been threatening several film personalities in Mumbai through different means over the past few days. Mr. Khurrana and Mr. Kapoor were among those who reportedly received threatening emails.

Reports suggest that investigators suspect artificial intelligence (AI) may have been used to generate voice samples resembling those of an alleged gang member. However, no forensic report confirming the use of AI has been made public.
Mumbai Police have clarified that Mr. Mishra has no connection with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.
The Crime Branch is investigating the motive behind the threats, the nature of the alleged extortion demands and whether more individuals were targeted. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: BJP backs striking OU employees, seeks talks with varsity authorities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana BJP president N. Ramachandar Rao on Wednesday demanded that the State government and Osmania University (OU) authorities immediately hold talks with striking non-teaching employees and address their long-pending demands.

Visiting the employees’ protest camp in front of the Osmania University Administrative Building, Mr. Rao expressed solidarity with the protesting staff, including non-teaching, technical, time-scale and contractual employees. The protesters are seeking implementation of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), regularisation of services, better healthcare benefits and resolution of other service-related issues.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Rao said it was unfortunate that university employees had been forced to launch an agitation to secure what he described as their legitimate rights. Recalling his association with the university, he said he had completed his post-graduation at Osmania University before entering public life and noted that his father had served and retired from the institution as a professor.

The BJP leader criticised the university administration for what he termed its indifferent attitude towards the employees’ grievances. He pointed out that the Supreme Court had upheld the principle of “equal pay for equal work” and questioned why benefits available to employees in other universities were not being extended to staff in Osmania University.

Mr. Rao also raised concerns over the alleged non-payment of annual increments due to employees and sought immediate corrective action. Telangana BJP president N. Ramachandar Rao on Wednesday demanded that the State government and Osmania University (OU) authorities immediately hold talks with striking non-teaching employees and address their long-pending demands.

Visiting the employees’ protest camp in front of the Osmania University Administrative Building, Mr. Rao expressed solidarity with the protesting staff, including non-teaching, technical, time-scale and contractual employees. The protesters are seeking implementation of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), regularisation of services, better healthcare benefits and resolution of other service-related issues.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Rao said it was unfortunate that university employees had been forced to launch an agitation to secure what he described as their legitimate rights. Recalling his association with the university, he said he had completed his post-graduation at Osmania University before entering public life and noted that his father had served and retired from the institution as a professor.

The BJP leader criticised the university administration for what he termed its indifferent attitude towards the employees’ grievances. He pointed out that the Supreme Court had upheld the principle of “equal pay for equal work” and questioned why benefits available to employees in other universities were not being extended to staff in Osmania University.

Mr. Rao also raised concerns over the alleged non-payment of annual increments due to employees and sought immediate corrective action. He demanded restoration of the Old Pension Scheme for employees appointed between 2001 and 2004 and implementation of the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) for those recruited after 2004.

He further called for an increase in employees’ medical reimbursement limit from ₹10,000 to ₹30,000 and urged the university to clear pending internal promotions and fill vacant posts across departments without delay.

fullParagraphs: India has reduced extreme poverty, but its high prosperity gap shows that millions remain far from a comfortable standard of living; informal work, stagnant wages and limited employment opportunities continue to constrain upward mobility

From the poverty income ruler line provided by the recent World Bank estimates, India has recorded one of the fastest extreme income-poverty declines in the world, as per its latest Poverty and Equity brief, which highlights that between 2011 and 2023, an estimated 496 million people moved out of poverty, with extreme income-based poverty ($3/per day) declining to 2.6%.

For the same period, the share of the population living below the lower middle-income country line ($4.20/day, 2021 PPP) fell from 57.7% to 16.1%. Non-monetary poverty indicators, as per OPHI’s Multi-dimensional Poverty Index, also recorded a sharp reduction in overall poverty numbers, i.e., from 53.8% in 2005-06 to 16.4% in 2019-21.

articles.title: U.S. midterm elections: An economy under pressure, political shift and the road ahead
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Despite robust economic growth, a buoyant stock market and relatively low unemployment, rising living costs have emerged as a major political challenge for the Trump administration

The 2026 U.S. midterm elections have dealt a significant political setback to President Donald Trump, with Democrats securing control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Beyond their political implications, the results raise important questions about the future direction of the world’s largest economy, particularly as American households grapple with rising living costs, persistent inflation and high borrowing expenses.

The election has highlighted a contradiction in the U.S. economy. Although real GDP expanded at an annualised rate of 3.4% in Q3 2026, a substantial section of the population remains dissatisfied with its financial circumstances. Inflation accelerated to 3.7% in September, up from 3.4% in August, largely driven by rising energy costs. Fuel oil prices surged 74.2%, compared with 52% previously, adding to household financial pressures.

articles.title: Oil prices hit two-month low after U.S. Democratic win
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Brent crude futures dropped 1% to $93.5 per ⁠barrel, after an 8.7% slide in the previous session

Indian shares are expected to open higher on Thursday (November 5, 2026), as crude oil prices slumped to a two-month low ​as investors bet that Democrats’ victory in US midterm elections could hasten ‌the end of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.
GIFT ​Nifty futures were at 24,295.5 as of ⁠8:01 a.m. IST, indicating a positive start for the benchmark Nifty 50 , which closed at 23,960.6 on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).

Foreign investors bought Indian shares worth ‌₹72.84 billion ($769.65 million) on Wednesday (November 4, 2026, as per provisional data. This marks their fourth straight session of buying, ‌suggesting they may be returning to India after a ‌strong ⁠sell-off this year.
Brent crude futures dropped 1% to $93.5 per ⁠barrel, after an 8.7% slide in the previous session.

U.S. and European stocks rallied on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress in ​the US midterm elections, providing greater ‌political clarity and reducing uncertainty that has weighed on markets.

Democrats’ win is being seen as a scathing rebuke to President Donald Trump, whose administration’s global tariff policy and decision to ‌go to war in the Middle East also contributed ​to the Indian market’s underperformance this year.

The domestic markets are now showing signs of a recovery. Indian ⁠benchmark Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex have risen 5.6% in the last five sessions, in their longest winning streak in nearly ‌five months, aided by foreign buying, easing oil prices, and strong earnings.

“Unlike the earlier gradual decline (in oil prices), the magnitude of this move can materially improve India’s near-term macro and earnings outlook if sustained,” said Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder and CEO of research advisory firm HST Wealth.

articles.title: U.S. midterm elections 2026 LIVE: After midterm loss, Trump left to weigh his next move in Iran war
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Indian-American physician Amish Shah has made history after becoming the first from the community to represent Arizona in Congress

Voters in dozens of American cities approved restrictions or outright bans on data centres during Tuesday’s (November 3) midterm elections, in one of the clearest signals that a groundswell of anger over the AI boom has cut across political divides.
“Democrat, Republican, that didn’t matter,” said Alisha Lange, a farmer from Piqua, Ohio. “People want their town back.”

She was one of the driving forces behind the grassroots group Save Piqua, which advocated for a ban on data centres with a capacity of more than 25 megawatts, effectively ruling out any large-scale project.
The ban passed in a ballot measure on Tuesday and now jeopardizes the construction of a data centre worth more than $1 billion planned by Meta, even though the project had already been approved.

It is the Trump administration, not the people, that abandoned America First politics, according to U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance. He said the Republican rout in the midterm elections was a direct outcome of the administration’s policies, particularly the war on Iran. Many see Mr. Vance’s position as a rebellion against President Donald J. Trump.

Mr. Vance’s measured but pointed disavowal of the direction of his own administration keeps him in pole position as the frontrunner for the Republican presidential nomination in 2028. The election debacle strengthens, not in the least weakens, Mr. Vance’s position, and further diminishes the prospects of Secretary of State Marco Rubio, a conventional Christian conservative who boarded the America First movement largely out of political expediency.
JD Vance reframes America First, blaming Trump-era policy for the GOP rout while positioning himself as a non-Trumpist leader.

President Donald Trump was publicly humbled by inflation in Tuesday’s (November 3) midterm elections, as rising prices provoked a blistering set of losses for Republicans in House, Senate and gubernatorial races.
Most voters said that Mr. Trump’s own policies had smothered growth and drove costs even higher, according to The AP Voter Poll, a survey of roughly 100,000 midterm voters.

The President’s message that the fault lay with his predecessor, Democrat Joe Biden, didn’t land. Americans saw prices start to climb with Mr. Trump’s chaotic rash of tariffs last year, and energy costs spiked after he launched a war with Iran in February.
As he takes stock of his Republican Party’s midterm drubbing, President Donald Trump now faces the difficult question of what to do about his unpopular 8-month-old war against Iran.

For weeks, Mr. Trump has threatened to return to a full-scale bombardment of Iran once the U.S. elections were in the rearview mirror if Tehran did not come to a settlement under terms acceptable to him.

articles.title: U.S. midterm elections witness historic firsts: First Black woman governor to first Muslim senator
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The US midterm elections delivered a series of historic firsts by electing a Black female governor, a Muslim senator and openly gay male US senator

The U.S. midterm elections 2026 will be remembered not just for the stunning number of losses Democrats handed to President Donald Trump and Republicans, but also for a wave of historic firsts across the country.

The closely watched polls, held on November 3, 2026, saw voters electing the first Native American female governor, the first Black female governor, the first Muslim US senator and first openly gay male US senator. The astonishing blue wave also means the United States will likely have its first-ever Black speaker of the House.

Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms reacts at a campaign office, the day after winning Georgia's race for governor and becoming the first Black woman elected governor of a US state during the US midterm elections in Atlanta, Georgia, US, November 4, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms was elected governor of Georgia, making history as the first Black woman to be elected governor in the United States, defeating Republican businessman Rick Jackson and flipping the top job in a key swing state. Her win returns the Governor’s office to Democrats after more than two decades of Republican control.
Democrat Deb Haaland answers questions during an interview at her campaign headquarters in Albuquerque. File photo | Photo Credit: AP

Democrat Deb Haaland became the first Native American female governor in U.S. history when was declared the winner over Republican Gregg Hull, a former mayor, to lead New Mexico. In 2018, Haaland was one of the first two Native American women elected to Congress. Then she became the first Native American Cabinet secretary, running President Joe Biden’s Department of the Interior.
Democrat Abdul El-Sayed speaks at an election night event on November 4, 2026, in Detroit, as his wife Sarah Jukaku watches. | Photo Credit: AP

Abdul El-Sayed will become the first Muslim American to serve in the U.S. Senate after registering victory in Michigan. The race between the progressive Michigan Democrat and Republican Mike Rogers had grabbed attention nationally. fullParagraphs: Critics on both sides argue that Mr. Netanyahu pulled Mr. Trump into a war he could not win. Now when even the Vice-President is blaming the war for the electoral defeat, the real target is the ‘special relationship’ with Israel

The political implications were visible even before the election results. On election day, President Donald Trump announced that the U.S. would stop providing about $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel, America’s closest ally in West Asia, by the end of the year. Mr. Trump cited the political cost of the issue for Republicans, specifically referring to Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate candidate from Michigan, who has made opposition to U.S. military assistance to Israel a central campaign plank. Mr. El-Sayed beat Mike Rogers of the Republican Party to become the first Muslim Senator of the U.S..

Mr. Trump’s announcement showed that even the Republican President, who moved the American embassy to Jerusalem in his first term, cracked down on pro-Palestine protests at home and launched a war, along with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, against Iran, recognised the growing electoral liability of unconditional support for Israel.

articles.title: US midterm election results 2026: Key Indian-origin winners
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Indian-Americans Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives, while Vivek ‌Ramaswamy‌ was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor

Several Indian-origin candidates too notched up victories as Democrats made significant gains in the US midterm elections on November 3, 2026, positioning themselves to wrest key Senate seats from Republicans, delivering a stinging rebuke to President Donald Trump.

Indian-American candidates Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives from Virginia and Florida, respectively. On the other hand, Republican ‌Vivek ‌Ramaswamy ‌was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor.

Suhas Subramanyam, who served as an advisor to former president Barack Obama, has been re-elected as a member of the US House of Representatives. The 40-year-old won from Virginia’s 10th congressional district , polling over 61.5% of the vote against Republican Dave Beckwith, who managed to win 36.4 per cent of the ballots cast.

Ro Khanna has won re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, located in the heart of Silicon Valley. The 50-year-old is completing his fifth term and will begin his sixth in January. Khanna was born in Philadelphia to a middle-class family. Both his parents immigrated to the United States from India in the 1970s.

Pramila Jayapal, who represents Washington’s 7th Congressional District, has secured a sixth term in the House of Representatives. Last month, her criticism of India’s Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls drew a public rebuke from India’s ambassador to the US. Jayapal, who was first elected to Congress in 2016, has been a prominent voice on immigration reform and healthcare issues.

A former high school principal, Pia Dandiya became the newest Indian-American to be elected to the US House , defeating Republican Casey Askar in Florida’s 22nd Congressional district. Dandiya bagged 51.9% of the votes, while her opponent Askar polled 49.1% of the votes.

Indian-American Democratic lawmaker Ami Bera has won the re-election to the U.S. House in California’s 3rd Congressional District, defeating Republican Robb Tucker. The 61-year-old won his eighth term in the US House of Representatives. Physician-turned-politician Amerish Babulal ‘Ami’ Bera is the longest-serving Indian American in the US Congress and is considered a strong voice on healthcare and diplomacy, as per PTI.
Amish Shah , an Indian-American physician, has been elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in Arizona’s First Congressional District.
He has now become the sixth Indian American to be elected to the U.S. House of Representatives.
Shah, a three-term member of Arizona House of Representatives, defeated Republican Jay Feely, a former National Football League(NFL) player, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump.

In a post on social media platform X, Shah said, “I pledge to be a Representative for all of you, whether or not you voted for me. I pledge to work in a bipartisan way in Congress, just like I did in the State House.”

Trump favourite Indian-American Vivek Ramaswamy was defeated in Ohio’s gubernatorial race, the home state of Vice President J. D. Vance, by Democrat Amy Acton after a bitter campaign that left the Republican Party divided.

articles.title: Vance eyes own trail in America First politics in Republican rout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: What continues to work for Mr. Vance is that he manages to challenge and critique Mr. Trump without triggering a meltdown from the latter. Whether he can continue in that manner all the way to the 2028 election remains to be seen. But Mr. Vance would be perfectly capable of carrying forward his own version of America First without Mr. Trump

It is the Trump administration, not the people, that abandoned America First politics, according to U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance. He said the Republican rout in the midterm elections was a direct outcome of the administration’s policies, particularly the war on Iran. Many see Mr. Vance’s position as a rebellion against President Donald J. Trump.

Mr. Vance’s measured but pointed disavowal of the direction of his own administration keeps him in pole position as the frontrunner for the Republican presidential nomination in 2028. The election debacle strengthens, not in the least weakens, Mr. Vance’s position, and further diminishes the prospects of Secretary of State Marco Rubio, a conventional Christian conservative who boarded the America First movement largely out of political expediency.

articles.title: Mobile phone retailers expect 10% price hike post Diwali even as sales drop
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: All India Mobile Retail Association projects a staggering 50% volume drop after mid-Novmber that could persist over an extended period

Mainstream mobile phone retailers are experiencing a footfall and sales contraction of 25% to 35% in value-oriented categories. Furthermore, major Android handset makers are expecting a 10% price hike shortly after Diwali .

All India Mobile Retail Association (AIMRA) projects a staggering 50% volume drop after mid-Novmber that could persist over an extended period. In response to flagging demand and severe component constraints, top smartphone brands have already cut production schedules by 30%, the retail body said.
The festive season, beginning with Navratri and concluding after Diwali, is a crucial time for Indian mobile retailers. This period sees stores brimming with customers.
Retailers are facing a subdued festive market characterised by declining footfall, plummeting sales of mass-market devices and rising costs due to a global memory chip shortage.

The sub-₹20,000 smartphone segment has been the worst hit — a category that traditionally brought in volume sales. But retailers report that this segment is crippled as leading brands have not put out any lineup of viable 5G handsets.
Historic price hikes of entry-level models, depreciating rupee and drop in purchasing power of rural consumers have paralysed the sub-₹20,000 smartphone segment.

articles.title: Nothing to launch its first AI-native product next month
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: According to Carl Pei, AI’s primary value lies in professional productivity and solving the technology’s critical “context gap.”

Nothing has announced plans to launch its first AI-native product next month, a dedicated hardware tool without a new screen that cannot be replicated as a software application. Carl Pei, CEO of the London-based company, wrote a post describing their strategic direction for AI.
According to him, AI’s primary value lies in professional productivity and solving the technology’s critical “context gap.”

Reflecting on past technological shifts, Nothing noted that personal computers and mobile phones gained traction as essential work tools decades before becoming consumer staples. With enterprise spending on AI concentrated in areas like coding, IT, customer support, and legal services, the company believes productivity tools remain the primary engine for AI adoption.

A key hurdle facing current models is the context gap: while AI capabilities are advanced, systems remain disconnected from a user’s real-time daily activity and spontaneous thoughts. Addressing this issue requires integrating AI directly into daily work tools rather than confining it to text-based chatbots.

Nothing also highlighted the need for better design in workplace technology, referencing design icons like Olivetti’s 1960s typewriters to argue that utilitarian tools can be both functional and aesthetically inspired.
Looking ahead, the company envisions AI transitioning from a tool users interact with to a proactive assistant handling routine operations.

articles.title: CERT-In calls for testing AI agents for unauthorised tool use, privilege abuse
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Guidelines require checks on agents’ permissions, task delegation and emergency-stop mechanisms; multi-agent systems must maintain authenticated, logged communications and records of actions

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has set out specific security and auditing requirements for artificial intelligence (AI) systems that can independently plan and carry out tasks, use external tools, and delegate work to other AI systems.

The Artificial Intelligence (AI) Security Auditing Guidelines: Framework for Secure, Ethical, and Auditable Artificial Intelligence Systems identify features such as autonomous task execution, persistent memory, and the ability to delegate work as factors that can increase the risks associated with these systems.

Unlike conventional AI tools that primarily respond to user instructions, systems can take multiple steps to complete a task. They may access information, use software tools, execute code, or communicate with external systems. The guidelines identify such capabilities—particularly when exercised without human intervention—as factors requiring closer security scrutiny.

The framework calls for testing whether an AI agent can exceed its authorised permissions, use tools without approval, bypass approval mechanisms, or misuse credentials. It also identifies unsafe delegation of tasks and the effectiveness of emergency-stop mechanisms as areas that auditors should examine.

The guidelines also address the risks associated with an agent’s memory and the information it retains from earlier interactions or tasks. They call for testing whether this memory can be manipulated, whether information belonging to one user can leak to another, and whether sensitive information is retained or reused without authorisation.
The framework separately addresses systems in which multiple AI agents work together and pass tasks between one another.

It calls for each agent to have a unique identity and clearly defined permissions. Communications between agents must be authenticated and logged, allowing organisations to establish which agent made a request and whether it was authorised to do so.
Organisations must also have controls to detect and limit repeated delegation of tasks, uncontrolled creation of new tasks and loops in which agents keep assigning work to one another.

The guidelines call for records that allow auditors to reconstruct what happened within a multi-agent system. These should capture requests exchanged between agents, tasks delegated, permissions used, decisions made, software tools invoked and the external actions that followed.
For high-risk systems, the framework also specifies the ability to suspend an individual agent or an entire workflow and revoke its access credentials.

The guidelines also call for organisations to maintain an inventory of the components used in production AI systems, including models, training data, software and external tools. Where third-party model providers do not disclose internal details, organisations must document the information gaps and their impact on audits. Auditors using AI must independently verify its outputs, as AI-generated summaries cannot replace audit evidence or professional judgement.

articles.title: NVS-03 reaches geosynchronous orbit; satellite in good health
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: ‘Four orbit manoeuvres have been successfully completed with a cumulative LAM engine burn of 6164 seconds; with this the satellite has reached Geo Synchronous Orbit at an inclination of 29.980,’ said ISRO
The NVS-03 satellite launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on October 30, 2026, has reached the intended Geo Synchronous Orbit.

ISRO said in an update on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that following four successful orbit manoeuvres, the satellite has reached Geo Synchronous Orbit (35765 km x 36196 km) at an inclination of 29.980.

“Four orbit manoeuvres have been successfully completed with a cumulative LAM engine burn of 6164 seconds. With this the satellite has reached Geo Synchronous Orbit [35765 km x 36196 km] at an inclination of 29.980,” ISRO said.
The NVS-03 satellite was successfully injected into 170.3 km x 38080 km orbit by GSLV on October 30.
The NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next generation navigation satellite system envisaged for providing continuity of navigation services for the IRNSS series.

The satellite carries indigenous atomic clock along with the procured clocks. It also includes L1 signal in addition to L5 and S band signals with coverage over Indian land mass and a region extending 1500 km around Indian geopolitical boundary.
The space agency also said that the satellite’s health is normal.

The development is significant as ISRO in 2025 was unable to perform the intended orbit raising operations for the NVS-02 satellite due to a valve malfunction. The NVS-02, the second satellite in the NVS series, was launched by the ISRO on January 29, 2025.

Sarah Jukaku, a doctor and wife of Democrat Abdul EI-Sayed , who is the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate in the midterm elections, traces her family roots to Bhatkal in Uttara Kannada district, of Karnataka, according to media reports.

Dr. Sarah is the granddaughter of the late J.H. Shamsuddin Jukaku, a lawyer from Bhatkal who served as Deputy Finance Minister in the erstwhile Mysore State government, led by the then Chief Minister B.D. Jatti, in the late 1950s and early 1960s. Shamsuddin was also the Deputy Minister for Electricity in the then government led by then Chief Minister S. Nijalingappa, reports said.
It is said that following the death of Shamsuddin, his family members shifted to different parts of India, including to Bengaluru.
Reports said that Dr. Sarah is the daughter of Jukaku S. Tayeb, also a doctor, who was among four sons of Shamsuddin, who also had six daughters. Dr. Tayeb moved to the U.S. in the 1980s.
They said that Dr. Sarah met EI-Sayed in the University of Michigan and they got married in 2006. Reports said that their family has still maintained relations with family members in India.

articles.title: ‘Very few complaints’ received so far on police brutality during July 20 protests, says Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Court allowed the petitioners the liberty to forward whatever material they have, including video clips, to the HPEC for its consideration

The Supreme Court, on Thursday (November 5, 2026), observed that the High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC) looking into police brutality during the July 20 protests reported that “very few complaints” were received. The Action Taken Report issued on October 31 noted that none were received physically or online.
The Court allowed petitioners the liberty to forward whatever material they have, including video clips, to the HPEC for its consideration.
The apex court said the HPEC has started a new portal through which complaints could be filed anonymously.
Petitioners ask why the Delhi Police has not placed on record before HPEC information on the kind of ammunition used on the day.
The Court says HPEC may be waiting to collate all details and material before commencing an enquiry. However, the Court said HPEC has to start furnishing fact-finding reports without delay.

On July 20, 2026, Police cracked down on a protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi. The police action at one of the largest protests in the national capital in recent years left several people injured.

At least 38 of the injured were taken to the Lady Hardinge Medical College and around 65 to the Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, said sources., with fractures, swelling due to tear gas, and head and eye injuries.

The police swung into action amid an internet shutdown in the New Delhi district, even as CJP representatives Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka met with Union Minister J.P. Nadda to formally seek Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation.

articles.title: ECI announces Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in four States, two UTs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The ECI announces Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim

The Election Commission on Thursday (November 5, 2026) announced a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim.

The poll roll revision exercise seeks to enrol eligible voters, particularly young and first-time electors, and facilitate advance applications from those who will become eligible on April 1, July 1 and October 1, 2027.
The draft electoral rolls will be published on November 30.
Final publication of electoral rolls will take place on January 21, 2027.
Editorial | A necessary corrective: On the SSR, the special summary revision of electoral rolls
The Commission has directed Chief Secretaries of the respective States and UTs to ensure adequate manpower and resources for the exercise.

articles.title: Restoration of Kashmir’s Malshahi Masjid could erase a Mughal-era layer, warn conservationists
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Landscape architect Jan Haenraets says the 17th Century Ganderbal mosque built by Dara Shikoh retains much authentic material, and urges a thorough conservation plan before the ₹5.01 crore restoration project proceeds

Unattended for centuries, the 17th Century mosque, Malshahi Masjid, in central Kashmir’s Ganderbal district is likely to offer a rare peep into the past with its conservation and restoration. However, conservationists warn against tampering with the structure, which could erase a layer from the Mughal era in Kashmir.

In May this year, J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah laid the foundation stone for restoration, conservation and development of the historic Masjid Hamam and allied works at Malshahi Masjid, Malshahi Bagh, at an estimated cost of ₹5.01 crore. Since then, the site has witnessed many changes, including laying of stone pavement. However, experts expressed concern over the current conservation plan.

“The significance of the mosque lies in its association with Akhund Mulla Shah and the Sufi order, and the connection of Jahanara and Dara Shikoh to Mulla Shah, and their sponsorship of infrastructure for Mulla Shah. It is a relatively small mosque but is distinctive in its materiality and position in a terrace garden compared to two other Mughal-era mosques of Pathar Masjid and Mulla Shah Masjid in Nagar Nagar (Srinagar),” Jan Haenraets, a landscape architect and historic preservation specialist, told The Hindu .

Built in the 17th Century by Mughal prince Dara Shikoh in a highland terrace garden in Ganderbal’s Malshahi Bagh, it is one of the few structures that have not undergone major changes. Mr. Haenraets, also author of the book Kashmir’s Mughal Landscapes , said the site, importantly, even though in ruins, “actually holds much authentic material”.

“In many gardens that have been ‘conserved’, much of that has been removed, damaged, or lost. The mosque itself holds significance in its architectural plan, materiality and the views to the Anchar lake. The surviving interior details, such as plasterwork, are highly significant, even though much was damaged and lost over the years. This still shows authentic elements, which have now largely disappeared in Kashmir, often due to inappropriate redevelopment practices,” Mr. Haenraets, who is also Professor of the Practice, Preservation Studies Program at Boston University, Boston, Massachusetts, United States, said.

The expert underlined that the significance of Mulla Shah Bagh does not lie in its mosque but in the totality of the bagh and the garden’s high level of authenticity and integrity, with the masjid as only one element of the garden complex. “The garden is also of key importance for the hydrological features, including multiple irrigation nallahs that pass through the garden,” Mr. Haenraets said.
However, there is cause for concern among the experts about its restoration and conservation, which primarily stems from the originality retained by the site.

“For about 400 years, the site has been largely forgotten, and remarkably, it survived with much more authenticity and integrity than the Mughal gardens that have become popular tourist destinations (and as such have been much damaged and altered). While it is in ruins, it has a level of archaeological significance and authenticity in its terrace location that cannot be found at many Mughal sites in Kashmir,” Mr. Haenraets said.

He warned that the funding-driven and hasty interventions could destroy what the locals achieved in over 400 years. The stone pavement work and the facelifting have already raised eyebrows about the conservation plan.

“Importantly, a thorough conservation plan must be prepared before any major on-site projects are undertaken. It should be prepared by experts who are aware of the international conservation principles. It should also engage local Kashmiri experts and stakeholders. Sadly, the J&K government and the Indian government have in recent years largely dismissed such processes,” Mr. Haenraets said.

He said the launch of the project and its funding “appears to place the garden and its structures at high risk”. “If unqualified professionals were handed these projects, the objective appears to be the development of the site as a ‘major tourist destination’,” he added.

The U.S.-based expert asked the government “to revisit their plans”. “As far as it is now understood, these approaches would destroy the significance of the place in an irreversible manner and are not in line with the best standards of cultural heritage conservation,” he warned.

articles.title: Development should be people-centric, eco-friendly says Rajendra Singh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He was flagging alleged violations in Google data centre, Amaravati and Eluru coal gasification projects

Rajendra Singh, the founder of Jal Biradari and widely known as the ‘Waterman of India’, demanded that the State government should reveal full details of all environmental, forest and water-use permissions, land allocation and lease agreements related to the Google hyperscale data centre proposed to be set up near Visakhapatnam, and ensure strict compliance with laws concerning the eco-sensitive zone of Kambalakonda and surrounding water resources.

Addressing media persons along Jal Biradari National Convener Bolisetty Satyanarayana here on Thursday, Mr. Rajendra Singh said any development should be people - centric and duly focused on public participation, environmental protection and the interests of future generations.

He noted that development achieved by destroying forests, rivers, lakes, agricultural lands and natural resources could not be considered real progress, while noting that India ranking 176 among 177 countries in the 2026 Environmental Performance Index was a dire warning.

As far as the Google data centre was concerned, he questioned what was the net benefit after giving incentives of nearly Rs.22,000 crore for the 1,000 - MW project apart from the creation of a measly 500 jobs.

Speaking about the construction of the capital city Amaravati, he insisted that the 2–3 km wide stretch of land parallel to the River Krishna must be used exclusively for agriculture and the development of blue - green infrastructure as stipulated in the environmental clearance.

Mr. Singh said construction of the greenfield capital city did not appear to be legally compliant, pointing to alleged non - adherence to some of the conditions laid down in Environmental Clearance No. SEIAA /AP/GTN-151/2015, dated October 9, 2026 pertaining to Krishna River and local agricultural lands.

He also demanded that an independent assessment of the Underground Coal Gasification (UCG) project in Chintalapudi–Recherla belt of Eluru district should be done and steps taken to protect the 8,700 acres of agricultural land in its vicinity.

He asked what the justification was for the UCG project when the world was moving toward cleaner, renewable energy, and cautioned against neglecting the experiences of similar projects, such as Link Energy's in Queensland, Australia, which was abandoned due to the environmental risks associated with the technology.

Development should be people-centric, eco-friendly says Rajendra Singh

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

He was flagging alleged violations in Google data centre, Amaravati and Eluru coal gasification projects

Rajendra Singh, the founder of Jal Biradari and widely known as the ‘Waterman of India’, demanded that the State government should reveal full details of all environmental, forest and water-use permissions, land allocation and lease agreements related to the Google hyperscale data centre proposed to be set up near Visakhapatnam, and ensure strict compliance with laws concerning the eco-sensitive zone of Kambalakonda and surrounding water resources.

Addressing media persons along Jal Biradari National Convener Bolisetty Satyanarayana here on Thursday, Mr. Rajendra Singh said any development should be people - centric and duly focused on public participation, environmental protection and the interests of future generations.

He noted that development achieved by destroying forests, rivers, lakes, agricultural lands and natural resources could not be considered real progress, while noting that India ranking 176 among 177 countries in the 2026 Environmental Performance Index was a dire warning.

As far as the Google data centre was concerned, he questioned what was the net benefit after giving incentives of nearly Rs.22,000 crore for the 1,000 - MW project apart from the creation of a measly 500 jobs.

Speaking about the construction of the capital city Amaravati, he insisted that the 2–3 km wide stretch of land parallel to the River Krishna must be used exclusively for agriculture and the development of blue - green infrastructure as stipulated in the environmental clearance.

Mr. Singh said construction of the greenfield capital city did not appear to be legally compliant, pointing to alleged non - adherence to some of the conditions laid down in Environmental Clearance No. SEIAA /AP/GTN-151/2015, dated October 9, 2026 pertaining to Krishna River and local agricultural lands.

He also demanded that an independent assessment of the Underground Coal Gasification (UCG) project in Chintalapudi–Recherla belt of Eluru district should be done and steps taken to protect the 8,700 acres of agricultural land in its vicinity.

He asked what the justification was for the UCG project when the world was moving toward cleaner, renewable energy, and cautioned against neglecting the experiences of similar projects, such as Link Energy's in Queensland, Australia, which was abandoned due to the environmental risks associated with the technology.

articles.title: Cheranalloor crash case: court seeks data on BNS Section 105 invocations in accidents involving juvenile drivers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Judge Kavitha Gangadharan seeks data to append it to order on appeals filed by prosecution and family of the deceased against the bail granted to teenager by Juvenile Justice Board, warns investigation officer that he will be held answerable if no FIRs had been registered elsewhere invoking BNS Section 105 in similar cases and if the provision had been invoked only in present case

The Additional District and Sessions Court designated to try cases involving atrocities against women and children in Ernakulam, while hearing appeals seeking the suspension of bail granted to the 17-year-old involved in the Cheranalloor crash case that claimed a life, directed the investigation officer to submit within an hour data on FIRs registered in the district or elsewhere in the State in connection with accidents involving juvenile drivers in which Section 105 of the BNS, which prescribes punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder, had been invoked.

Judge Kavitha Gangadharan sought the data to append it to the order on the appeals filed by the prosecution and the family of the deceased against the bail granted to the teenager by the Juvenile Justice Board. She warned the investigation officer, Assistant Commissioner, Crime Branch, that he would be held answerable if no FIRs had been registered elsewhere invoking BNS Section 105 in similar cases and if the provision had been invoked only in the present case.

The court was also critical of the investigation agency for filing the appeal against the bail before the Principal Sessions Court and not before the court designated to try cases involving juveniles. The judge also sought to know from the prosecution whether it had any doubt that the Juvenile Justice Model Rules constituted the sole State government framework governing matters involving children in conflict with law.

On Monday (November 2, 2026), the court had expressed displeasure over the prosecution and counsel for the victim’s family trading allegations and directed that further proceedings for the day be held in camera. The judge took the decision despite objections raised by the family’s counsel. Bhadra Keerthy, daughter of the deceased Jayabalakrishnan, had told the media that the family lacked confidence in the prosecution represented by Special Public Prosecutor P.A. Bindu.

On Monday, the prosecution raised the issue before the court, accusing the victim’s family of interfering with the independent investigation through contradictory statements made to the media. M.G. Sreejith, counsel for the family, accused the prosecution of non-cooperation while denying the allegation that the victim’s family was hampering the independent investigation. The decision to conduct the proceedings in camera came after Mr. Sreejith stated that he had certain matters to place before the court that could not be discussed in open proceedings.

articles.title: Younger, dynamic Democratic leaders dealt a decisive blow to Trumpism
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: These leaders are ideologically and socially diverse, but for the most part, they fall on a progressive spectrum

The U.S. mid-term elections have delivered a damning mandate against Trumpism. After Richard Nixon and Watergate, Donald Trump is the first to accomplish a Republican rout of this scale and scope. The Democratic Party flipped seven Senate seats, 22 House seats, and four Governor seats, and has won a majority in both House and Senate.

Trump’s wars — the Iran war and the tariff war — resulting in steep costs of fuel and food are the most obvious catalyst for this “Blunami (tsunami for Democrats)”. Rural voters opposed data centres (promoted by Trump), fearing it would guzzle water as well as jobs. That’s an AI-era issue to watch as data centres make their way into India.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: Younger, dynamic Democratic leaders dealt a decisive blow to Trumpism. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: Democrats vow to rein in Donald Trump as he shows off White House ballroom
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress

Democrats vowed to use their resounding midterm victory to rein in President Donald Trump, setting ​up two years of possible deadlock in Washington, as Mr. Trump spent his first post-election appearance showing off his under-construction White House ballroom.

A wave of anger over Mr. Trump’s policies, particularly the U.S.-Iran war’s ‌role in pushing the cost of living higher, helped Democrats take the Senate, where they flipped seats in deeply Republican states for ​a majority of at least 54-44. Democrats also gained at least 30 seats in the House of Representatives.
It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that the incoming majority would be focused on affordability and accountability.
U.S. midterm elections witness historic firsts: First Black woman governor to first Muslim senator
Midterm results put U.S.-Israel ties under further strain
U.S. midterm elections: An economy under pressure, political shift and the road ahead

“We don’t work for Donald Trump,” Jeffries, a New York lawmaker who is on track to become the first Black speaker of the ‌House, told reporters on Wednesday. “We work for the American people. And the days of the House of Representatives functioning like a wholly owned subsidiary of the Trump administration are over.”

Mr. Trump, who had devoted his last pre-election public appearance on Monday (November 2, 2026) to talking about his renovations ‌of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, called in reporters on the morning after his party’s sweeping midterm defeat to show off the ballroom he is building at the ‌White ⁠House.

“When I get criticized, like, ‘Why are you working on the White House?’ I’m doing it because the White House is the ultimate symbol ⁠of America, and it’s got to be pristine, it’s got to be perfect,” Mr. Trump said. “For me, it’s relaxing.”

He turned only briefly to the elections during his nearly hour-long appearance, telling reporters, “I’ll get along probably with the Democrats, unless they want to be destructive, but I have the power of the veto.”

Mr. Trump had cast the midterm elections as a referendum on the first half of his second four-year stint in ​the White House, repeatedly urging his Republican base to “pretend I’m on the ballot,” ‌a message that Democratic Party leaders were happy to amplify.

articles.title: Jaishankar urges Commonwealth partners to 'de-risk and diversify'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: S. Jaishankar said Commonwealth partners need to make more efforts to enhance local distribution, adding that more connectivity corridors are good for business
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has urged Commonwealth partners to "de-risk and diversify", emphasising the need to enhance local distribution among member nations.
Mr. Jaishankar arrived in St. John's on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) to attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).

"Commonwealth partners also need to de-risk and diversify. This requires shorter and trusted supply chains," Mr. Jaishankar posted on social media after attending the Commonwealth heads of government and business leaders' breakfast meeting on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Mr. Jaishankar said Commonwealth partners need to make more efforts to enhance local distribution, adding that more connectivity corridors are good for business.
"Promote training and capacity building as it gives more options for partners," he said.
EAM said that the Indian business community spread across the world is an asset for the Commonwealth.
Speaking about the significance of digital public infrastructure for good governance, Mr. Jaishankar said, "Digital is a game changer as it promotes efficiency, good governance and growth."
"International Solar Alliance and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure can be leveraged for climate action," Mr. Jaishankar said.
Sharing India's experiences in Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR), Mr. Jaishankar said, "Our First Responder experiences and HADR activities suggest the need for local hubs."
He said that comfort within the Commonwealth nations "can build business for growth and prosperity", adding that mobility of skills can be an important Commonwealth focus.
The theme of this year's CHOGM is accelerating partnerships and investment for a prosperous Commonwealth.
Mr. Jaishankar also met with the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, Andy Burnham and the Prime Minister of Australia, Anthony Albanese, on the sidelines of CHOGM.

articles.title: India announces extension of $500 million line of credit for Guyana
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: EAM Jaishankar met Guyanese President Mohamed Irfaan Ali on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting

India has announced an extension of a $500 million line of credit for roads, health and defence projects in Guyana as External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Guyanese President Mohamed Irfaan Ali in Antigua and Barbuda.
Mr. Jaishankar, who arrived in St. John's on Tuesday (November 4, 2026), met President Ali on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) on Wednesday.

"Delighted to meet with President Dr Irfaan Ali of Guyana. @presidentaligy. Reviewed the steady progress in our bilateral cooperation, especially after PM @narendramodi’s visit in 2024," Mr. Jaishankar posted on social media on Wednesday after the meeting.

The two leaders discussed ways to further strengthen cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, energy, agriculture, infrastructure development, digital technology and capacity building, a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said.
"Announced extension of $500 million Line of Credit for roads, health & defence projects," Mr. Jaishankar said.
India has already completed several development projects in Guyana, and the new line of credit will further strengthen the development partnership between the two countries, the statement said.

The two countries also signed three agreements, including on the supply and installation of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) manufacturing projects and grant assistance for implementation of Quick Impact Projects (QIPs), the statement said.
The third agreement was on cooperation in the field of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and the Functioning of a Unified Payments Interface (UPI)-like System in Guyana, it said.

India and Guyana share longstanding and close relations, rooted in historical, cultural and people-to-people ties. The countries are not only members of the Commonwealth but also Global South partners.
The two countries will continue to work together to strengthen their multifaceted cooperation and advance shared priorities for development and prosperity, the statement said.
Earlier, Mr. Jaishankar attended a Commonwealth heads of government and business leaders' breakfast meeting where he urged Commonwealth partners to "de-risk and diversify”.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: The Amazon is no longer a carbon sink, it is an emitter
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Hindu’s weekly Science for All newsletter explains all things Science, without the jargon.

The world’s largest tropical forest, referred to as the ‘lungs of the planet,’ the Amazon rainforest once acted as a vast carbon sink that helped absorb human-induced CO2 emissions. But now, a study startlingly finds that the Amazon releases more CO2 than it absorbs from the atmosphere, as it is decimated by deforestation and forest fires.

Scientists measured CO2 levels at different atmospheric altitudes, using research airplanes, between the years 2010 and 2024 at four Amazonian sites. Their findings indicated that “Amazonia is a net carbon source rather than a sink and cannot offset regional anthropogenic emissions.”

Science, Space & Environment Report: The Amazon is no longer a carbon sink, it is an emitter. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Karnataka raises DA for State government staff by from 15.75% to 18%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Dearness Allowance (DA) for the State government employees would now be increased from the present 15.75% to 18% of their basic pay.
Karnataka has announced a Deepavali bonanza for State government employees by increasing the Dearness Allowance by 2.25 percentage points with retrospective effect from July 2026.

According to a notification issued on Thursday (November 5, 2026), the Dearness Allowance (DA) for the State government employees would now be increased from the present 15.75% to 18% of their basic pay. The increase will come into effect from July 1, 2026.
The increase in DA will also apply to the pensioners and family pensioners, according to the notification.
